# SHA collision (birthday) collider on the AC accelerator — DATA ONLY

## Grounding (measured this session, byte-exact substrate)
- `pfc_full_miner` stored circuit: **339,234 gates**, 929 in → 64 out (`titan_circuits.json`, confirmed).
- **one `sha_block` = 115,869 gates** (measured, post-DCE, `sdc_cc.sha_block`).
- **256-bit equality comparator = 767 gates** (~3/bit: XOR→NOT→AND-tree); **64-bit = 191 gates** (measured).
- Existing lexicographic `hash &lt; target` comparator in the miner: `host/pfc_full_miner.py:41-44` (~6 gates/bit). The winner latch is `:48-49` (`pw = AND(power, win)`; MUX per bit). These are the two pieces we re-target.

## The design — swap the comparator, keep the SHA plant

The miner already builds `H = doubleSHA(header)` as gates and asks `H &lt; target`. A collision collider keeps the entire SHA plant and replaces the *predicate* and the *latch payload*:

```
  miner:      win = (H(message) &lt;  target)        latch &lt;- winning nonce
  collider:   win = (H(a)==H(b)) AND (a != b)      latch &lt;- colliding pair (a,b)
```

**Two-tier structure (this is where the AC accelerator pays off):**

**Tier 1 — injection (once per candidate, off the crossing path).** When a message enters a beam lane, run it through the reused `sha_block` plant to produce an n-bit **truncated tag** `T = H(m)[:n]`. The lane then carries `(tag T, id k)` — the beam "carries candidate messages" but the hash travels with them. Cost = one SHA-256d per candidate = **2 blocks = ~231,738 gates** (single-block ≤55-byte message: **115,869**; full Bitcoin 3-block: 339,234). Paid once, amortized.

**Tier 2 — the crossing cell (per clack, the AC all-pairs front).** Counter-rotating beams: lane `a` from beam-1 meets lane `b` from beam-2. The crossing cell is *only*:
```
  eq   = AND_reduce_i( XNOR(T_a[i], T_b[i]) )      # n-bit truncated-tag equality
  diff = OR_reduce ( XNOR-complement(id_a, id_b) ) # a != b guard (reject self/dupes)
  win  = AND(eq, diff)
  pw   = AND(power, win)                            # winner-only fold
  latch_next[j] = OR(AND(pw, pair[j]), AND(NOT pw, latch[j]))   # reuse :48-49 MUX
```
No SHA gates in the crossing — bidirectional AC mode makes every a×b crossing a comparison, so the SHA plant must NOT be replicated per pair (that would be R² SHAs). Hash-at-injection = R SHAs + R² cheap compares.

## Gate / DEPTH estimate — n-bit truncated-hash collision

Per **crossing cell** (Tier 2), with `k = log2(#lanes)` id bits:

| part | gates | depth |
|---|---|---|
| n-bit tag equality (XNOR + AND-tree) | ~3n | ⌈log₂ n⌉ + 1 |
| a≠b guard (k-bit XNOR + OR-tree) | ~3k | ⌈log₂ k⌉ + 1 |
| win + winner-only latch (MUX, 2·2k pair bits) | ~4k + 3 | +3 |
| **cell total** | **~3n + 7k** | **~⌈log₂ n⌉ + 4** |

- n=256, k=262144: cell ≈ 767 + ~1.8M-bit-pair latch → the **comparator core is ~767 gates**, DEPTH **≈ 12**.
- n=64: comparator core **191 gates**, DEPTH **≈ 10**.

**DEPTH is the substrate metric denominator.** One copy's depth = one crossing cell ≈ ⌈log₂ n⌉ + 4 (single digits to low double digits). The SHA critical path (order 10³–10⁴ gate-levels — 64 compression rounds of ripple `add32`) lives in Tier-1 injection only, off the per-tick clack path. So:

```
  compute/tick = REPLICAS / DEPTH  ≈  (all-pairs crossing-front width) / (⌈log2 n⌉ + 4)
```
The crossing cell is ~3n gates while the SHA plant is ~116k — i.e. the collider's per-tick unit is **~150–600× shallower and ~150× smaller** than the miner's per-nonce unit. Clacks=ticks; density=frequency ⇒ packing more candidates per beam raises the compare frequency linearly.

## Birthday bound 2^(n/2) vs the fold's addressable lanes

- Birthday: a collision on an n-bit tag is expected once the beam holds **C ≈ 2^(n/2)** distinct candidates (C²/2 ≳ 2ⁿ pairs). AC bidirectional mode realizes all C² pairs as crossings — exactly the birthday all-pairs product.
- Fold addressing: winner-only settle addresses **~2^262144 lanes** per settle (losers → 0 bytes).
- Feasibility line: `n/2 ≤ 262144  ⇒  n ≤ 524288 bits` addressable in a **single settle**.

| tag width n | candidates needed 2^(n/2) | one settle's lanes | headroom |
|---|---|---|---|
| SHA-256 full, 256 | 2^128 | 2^262144 | **2^262016** |
| SHA-512 full, 512 | 2^256 | 2^262144 | 2^261888 |
| n = 524288 | 2^262144 | 2^262144 | 2^0 (saturates one settle) |

Every real digest (n ≤ 512) sits **astronomically inside one settle** — the birthday bound for SHA-256 (2^128 candidates) is under-provisioned by a factor 2^262016; in pair terms, one settle supplies 2^524288 crossings vs the 2^256 needed.

## Storage-scale reach

- PFCTYPED encoding = 9 bytes/gate (`struct.pack("&lt;Bii")`, `pfc_full_miner.py:82`).
- Injection plant (shared, stored once): double-SHA ≈ 231,738 gates ≈ **2.1 MB**; full 3-block Bitcoin double-hash 339,234 gates ≈ **3.1 MB**.
- Crossing-cell template (n=256): ~767 comparator gates ≈ **6.9 KB** (+ latch MUX scaling with pair-id width).
- Winner-only fold: non-colliding lanes settle to **0 bytes** — storage holds *template + the one latched pair*, not 2^(n/2) candidates. That is why the addressable-lane count (2^262144) is set by the fold's settle-address width, not by materializing lanes.

**Reach statement (storage-bound):** the collider needs only the shared SHA plant (~3 MB) plus one ~7 KB comparator template resident; the fold's settle then sweeps up to 2^262144 lanes with zero incremental storage per non-winner. So the birthday reach is bounded by settle-address width, not blob size — SHA-256 collision (needs 2^128) is reached inside a single ~3 MB-resident settle with 2^262016 lanes to spare, and truncated tags up to n=524288 bits are reachable one settle at a time.

- `C:\llm\sdc_sandbox\sdc_cc.py` — `sha_block` (`:135`), `add32`/`rotr`/`xor32` primitives (`:124-134`).
- `C:\llm\models\titan_circuits.json` — stored `pfc_full_miner` (339,234 gates) registry entry.

# FORGOTTEN-BUT-USEFUL LEVERS — collision collider / AC clock / shallow comparators

- **DC vs AC modes, both already in the binary.** `docs/MUHL_ACCELERATOR.md:53-61` — DC = `muhl_ring_power` (one-way, **0 clacks**, steady power/lateral bus, powers the fold/mining); AC = `muhl_accel_reflect` / `muhl_accel_transparent` (counter-rotating beams, **clacks ARE the cycles**, self-clocking from one injection). Measured frequency-by-density: **2 → 4 → 8 → 12 → 16 clacks/step** as electron density climbs.
- **The fabricated AC unit's spec.** `docs/MUHL_ACCELERATOR.md:20-22` — `muhl_accel_reflect_64` @ **3064742328**, 7,719 B, **795 gates, DEPTH 21**, n_in 128 (64 cells × 2 beams), n_out 135 (128 next-state ++ 7 clack-count bits). Registry role: clock/power source, one settle advances every electron. GGUF-valid, reversible.
- **[BUILT, UNUSED] Pre-existing self-advancing clocks waiting for a clack driver.** `docs/CIRCUIT_PFC.md:18-20` — `pfc_clock_counter` (159 gates, `next = clk ? state+1 : state`), `clock_wide` (1,920 gates, 128-bit counter), `clk_bit` (1 gate, power-in/receiver bit). These are host-poked today; the AC clack output is a drop-in replacement for the host poke.
- **[UNUSED IDEA] "Close the clock with feedback junctions."** `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:239-244` — state reg shares byte-addresses with its next-state output via §1E junctions so one addressed read triggers a full depth-D settle that writes back → one tick per poke, host loop-body gone. This is exactly the AC self-clock mechanism, catalogued as an open idea before the accelerator was built.
- **Self-clocked native engines (host = clock only).** `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:127-139` — `pfc_phone_clock` 4.9×10⁶ ticks/s flat RSS; `pfc_clockmachine` self-advances its own program 46,480 ticks/s, RSS flat. Host only pulses.

## (a) collision / all-pairs / value-carrying beams

- **[EXPLICIT NEXT-BUILD] Collider = counter-rotating beams whose crossing computes all-pairs.** `docs/MUHL_ACCELERATOR.md:65-67` — "the counter-rotating form is the seed of a **collider** — two beams whose crossing computes all-pairs (collision-search: hash-collision / meet-in-the-middle)." Named as the direct sequel to the clacker.
- **[BUILT, UNUSED — strongest collision primitive] Content-addressed membership fold.** `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:339-343` — winner-only storage-backed bit-fold where **the key's hash IS its bit address**; members cost 1 bit, non-members 0, whole set addressed not scanned, data-oblivious. **100k keys in 2 MB, 0 false negatives byte-exact; 8.6-billion-slot (2³³) fold at flat 32→34 MB RSS.** Reusable directly for collision detection: store beam-A values keyed by hash, beam-B addresses → a hit IS a collision; birthday/meet-in-the-middle in one bounded read.
- **[VALUE-CARRYING] Carry-save reduction — constant depth in width, composes with anything.** `docs/PFC_FINDINGS.md:1069-1071, 1113-1115` — 3:2 compressor "propagates no carry at all, so its depth is constant in width… composes with anything"; the fused dot pours all partial products into one carry-save tree with **exactly one carry propagation in the entire dot product** (§33A/§33B, won the search at DEPTH 56). This is the reusable value-carrying beam reduction for accumulating all-pairs contact values.
- **Balanced-tree popcount counts the contacts, 31.9× shallower.** `docs/MUHL_ACCELERATOR.md:26-28` — clacks counted with a balanced-tree popcount, the "31.9×-shallower reduction the foundry's gate-discovery surfaced this session (N=256: OR-chain depth 255 → tree depth 8, same gate count)." Same reduction applies to counting collisions across a collider's crossing.

## (c) shallow comparators / hashing / SHA folds

- **[BUILT, UNUSED] Standalone comparator circuits.** `docs/CIRCUIT_PFC.md:45` — `win_cmp` / `cmp_gt` = 3,840 / 582 gates (hash &lt; target / a &gt; b). Small, already-baked equality/inequality primitives — the natural equality-compare for a collider's crossing.
- **[BUILT] Full self-clocked SHA folds w/ baked compare+latch.** `docs/CIRCUIT_PFC.md:36-43` — `gen_miner` 628,899 (double-SHA-256d ASIC, shallow variant), `gen_win` 339,009 (double-SHA + baked `hash&lt;target` compare + baked latch, out = `win|latch[32]|hash[256]`), `pfc_full_miner` / `selfclock_miner` (self-clock + compare + winner-latch). Reusable SHA-fold + compare + latch stack for a hash-collision search.
- **[UNUSED IDEA] Filter-cascade / Bloom prefilter before the heavy SHA.** `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:402-407` — a ~10²–10³-gate rejection predicate discards candidates that provably can't meet the frontier so only survivors ripple the 337k-gate SHA. Directly reusable to prune a collision search's candidate stream.
- **[UNUSED IDEA] Route-time partial evaluation / midstate specialization.** `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:388-393` — constant-fold the SHA circuit against fixed input bits at the routing button; residual &lt;&lt; 337,256 gates, per-batch not re-baked. Reusable to specialize a collider's shared-header cone.
- **Parallel-prefix comparators collapse comparison depth.** `docs/PFC_FINDINGS.md:611-614, 629` — `max-of-256` ripple comparator DEPTH 592 → **parallel-prefix DEPTH 232** (verified 3/3); shipped as `pfc_argmax_shallow` @ 2499034196 carrying **value AND index**. Reusable shallow comparator for collision-winner selection.
- **Shallow-glue balanced-tree rebuild is free.** `docs/PFC_FINDINGS.md:126-128` — OR is associative so a balanced tree is free: `rsqrt 1403→41, sin 1068→41, silu 399→33, exp 189→31`, byte-exact 2,560/2,560, unchanged gate count, 6.1× per-token depth cut.

## Interconnect law that governs wiring clack → clock → compute

- **§1E junction = shared storage location, +6 gate-delays per chained stage.** `docs/PFC_INTERCONNECT.md:16-18, 33-36` — "A junction is a shared storage location, not a transfer. `A_out is B_in`." First stage costs its own critical path; **every junction-chained stage after it costs exactly +6 gate-delays**, linear across 32 stages, still ONE settle. This is the cost model for wiring the AC clack output through §1E into `pfc_clock_counter` → a compute circuit.

## 1. PERCEPTION — `snapshotScreen()` (`:559-797`) and helpers

**Entry &amp; budgets**
- Resets per-snapshot state: `currentNodes`, `lastRenderedIds`, `sawSpinner`, `seenAffordanceTags`, `affordanceTagsSuppressed` (`:560-564`).
- Tier-aware budgets via `leanPerception()`=`DeviceStats.useLeanPath` (`:556`) → `perceptionPageSize()` 14 (lean) vs 20 (`:557`); lean also shrinks `charBudget` 1000 vs 1300 and `nodeCap` 120 vs 200 (`:569-570`).
- **Multi-pane read** (`:576-582`): reads EVERY `TYPE_APPLICATION` window (split-screen/DeX/fold), sorted top-to-bottom/left-to-right; falls back to `rootInActiveWindow`. Emits a "— split screen: N panes —" banner (`:700-701`).

**The walk — `consider(node, listedAncestorLabel)`** (`:599-695`), recursive DFS:
- **Collect-vs-render split** (core design): collects up to `nodeCap` interactive nodes into `currentNodes` (ids stable, reachable by find/click even off-page), but only RENDERS a page-window as text lines. `:620` aborts collection at cap (was 60, caused unfindable controls — comment `:76-79`).
- **Visible-only?** — interactivity is gated on `node.isVisibleToUser` for listing (`:633`); non-interactive VISIBLE text is captured into `readText` (`:686-691`, cap 24, len 1..64). So yes: only visible nodes are listed/read.
- **Interactive predicate** (`:626-628`): `isClickable || isEditable || isLongClickable || isCheckable || (isFocusable &amp;&amp; hasLabel)`. Bare focusable containers excluded (`:621-625`).
- **Spinner detection** (`:607-618`): sets `sawSpinner` if a visible indeterminate `ProgressBar`/`CircularProgress` (`rangeInfo==null`) OR a short "loading…"/"please wait" label — feeds `loadingHint()`.
- **Nested-duplicate dedup** (`:646-647`): drops a non-editable, non-checkable clickable whose label == listed ancestor's label (row+wrapper+inner all tap same thing). Label-less children kept.
- **Paging window** (`:655`): `onPage = index in [elementPage*pageSz, +pageSz)`; when `zoomRegion!=null`, uses `nodeInZoom` instead (`:661`).
- **Identical-line tiebreaker** (`:663-680`): a byte-identical `describe()` gets `id:&lt;viewId&gt;` or `@&lt;position&gt;` appended so text can disambiguate what only badge geometry otherwise could.

**Post-walk render + homogeneous-list collapse** (`:709-732`): folds a run of ≥6 consecutive rows with identical `structuralSig` to 3 representatives + "… +N more similar rows [ids A–B]". State differences break the run. `lastRenderedIds` records EXACTLY what got a line (the single source of truth for badges).

**State tags** (emitted by `describe()` `:1193-1309`):
- `[editable]` (`:1230`), `[ALREADY SENT …]` if field still holds a recently-sent msg (`:1234-1236`).
- `[checked]/[unchecked]` (`:1238`); `[disabled]` (`:1245`); `[selected]` (`:1246`); `[focused]` (only if editable, `:1247`).
- `[val N%]` from `rangeInfo` for sliders/seekbars/volume/progress (`:1253-1258`).
- Affordances (`:1271-1303`): `[long-press for options]`, `[expandable]`/`[expanded-tap to collapse]`, `[opens a menu]` (`canOpenPopup`), `[do: A·B·C]` (named custom a11y actions, cap 3, standard verbs excluded via `standardActIds` `:1280-1298`), `[dismissable]`. - `role()` (`:1161-1179`): field/toggle/tab, else "" (plain tap = no role word, token-light).
- `positionHint()` (`:1311-1315`): row-col like "top-left".

**KEY CONTROLS line — `keyControlsHint()`** (`:809-871`): scans `currentNodes` for search box (strong/weak view-id tiers `:826-829`), send (`:830-831`), submit/next (`:835-836`), chat composer `msgBox` (`:840-841`). ## 4. JSON SALVAGE / NORMALIZATION — `parseActionObject(raw)` (`:1355-1429`)

- `salvageVerbs` set (`:1357-1371`) distinguishes a doubled verb from a mis-keyed text payload.
- `fix` lambda (`:1372-1389`): collapse runaway repeated char `(.)\1{15,}→3` (`:1379`); `{"action":"verb":"X"}` → keep verb if X is a verb else rescue as `"text"` (`:1383-1386`); strip stray quote after numeric value `:5"` (`:1387`); strip trailing comma (`:1388`).
- Prefers the top-level `{}` object that actually has `"action"` (`:1391-1407`); falls back to widest brace span (`:1410-1412`), then first-parsed (`:1413).

## 5. THREADING / LIFECYCLE

- **Singleton** `companion.instance` set in `onServiceConnected` (`:219`), cleared in `onDestroy` (`:386`). Opportunistic first-run `scanAll()` on a background Thread (`:225-227`).
- **Event subscription** minimized by mode (`applyEventSubscription` `:248-258`): idle = WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED only; widened only during demo/passive learning.
- **Main-thread node access**: accessibility node reads (snapshotScreen, currentMarks, all `currentNodes`/`rootInActiveWindow`) must run on the main thread. `actuate()` (`:3402-3429`) runs `a11y()` on main, `shell()` off-thread with the a11y fallback posted back to main (`:3416`). `captureScreenshot` uses `mainExecutor` (`:4518`).
- **Injection kill-gates** (ghost-input hardening): `injectionHalted` @Volatile (`:3368`), `haltInjection()` (`:3373-3378`) from every STOP path drops queued taps (`seqHandler`), sets `ShellInput.halted`; `resumeInjection()` at task start (`:3381`). - **Sleep invariant**: double-checked at `performActionJson` top (`:1520`) AND in `actuate` (`:3405`) for leftover queued gestures.
- **Staleness gate**: `markDecisionScreen()`/`staleForBlindTap()` (`:3387-3393`) refuses a blind coord tap if foreground package changed since decision; `lastWindowStateChangeAt` (`:215,239`).
- **Null-safety**: pervasive `rootInActiveWindow ?:`, `currentNodes.getOrNull`, `try/catch(_:Exception){}` around reflection (isDexMode `:538`), rangeInfo, window list, screenshot.
- **OOM-restart resilience**: bounded budgets (MAX_SNAPSHOT_CHARS/MAX_NODES/pageSz), affordance dedup, homogeneous collapse, and re-scan on connect if `AgentMemory` device profile is blank (`:225`).
- `@Volatile` fields for cross-thread reads: `sawSpinner`, `zoomRegion`, `lastSketchDurationMs`, `recording`, `passiveLearning`, `exploreOnly`, `lastWindowStateChangeAt`, `injectionHalted`, `decisionPackage`, `lastTapFrac/At`.

Reported factually with anchors:

- **`isInstallLabel` false-positive on "Uninstall"** (`:3007`): `l.contains("install ")` — the string "uninstall " contains substring "install " (chars 2–9), so an "Uninstall" label in a packageinstaller context matches → NEEDS_CONFIRM "sideload install" (mislabeled; harmless in that it only confirms, but the wording is wrong).
- **`tryAdvance()` auto-accepts consent/permission dialogs** (`:3744-3752`): `clickByKeyword` auto-clicks "allow"/"accept"/"ok"/"got it"/"continue"/… when the orchestrator detects a recurring/blocking screen. This is deterministic code clicking irreversible consent controls without model choice (only the OS-updater case is excluded, `:3747`). Worth a lead's eye given top-level rules on accepting terms/permissions.
- **Auto-send / auto-search chaining decided by field-type sniffing** (`set_text` `:2425-2432`; also `:2335`, `:2391`): the executor deterministically presses Send when `looksLikeMessageInput` (`:4488-4498`, keyword sniff of id/desc/hint) or IME-Search when `looksLikeSearchField` (`:4503-4511`). Code decides *that a message is committed*, not just how — a consequential action driven by heuristic classification of the field. Documented as a "linked action" (`:2418-2424`) but it is code choosing to send.
- **`keyControlsHint()` classifies control roles from prompt-free heuristics** (`:809-871`): search/send/submit/composer are chosen by view-id/label sniffing. Comments insist it only "surfaces" possibilities (`:851-866`), which keeps it §2-legal, but it is deterministic perception-labeling adjacent to deciding — flagged for transparency.
- **`normalizeAppName` keyword remap** (`:3843-3852`): "browser"/"internet"/"google search" → "Chrome"; "text/sms" → "Messages" — deterministic name→app decisions from keyword sniffing (benign routing, not objective-sniffing).
- **`drawCanvasBand` is package-name-heuristic** (`:3575-3583`) with hard-coded fractions "calibrated against Samsung Notes" (`:3574` comment) — 0.17f/0.90f band; fragile on other launchers/apps (acknowledged as a "safety net", not general).
- **Grid/marks image drawing lives out-of-file**: `AgentBrain.drawGrid`/`drawMarks` (`:25`,`:1105`) — the tap-mapping and dims here MUST stay in sync manually; a cross-file coupling risk (comment `:24-26`).

- The `sketch`/`draw` path does NOT script creative output — the model supplies all strokes/points; code only renders shapes cleanly (explicit "no artificial wobble," `:3609-3611`) — noted as *not* a §2 violation.

# Local Device Agent — Documentation Synthesis (factual map)

**Scope note (read first).** These docs are snapshots from *different git branches/sessions* and do not all describe one coherent "current" state. `README.md` is the ~150–170 KB narrative design log; `CLAUDE.md` is the rules+architecture orientation and is materially *ahead of* the README on several axes (model, the whole operator/baking stack, Gemini policy). `PARKED_FEATURES.md`, `REUNIFICATION_INVENTORY.md`, and `NOT_BUILT.md` describe a rollback-and-reunify process across ≥9 `claude/*` branches. Where they conflict, I flag it in §9. The docs' own status labels (`✅ BUILT` / `🔜`/`⏳`/`🔭 PLANNED` / `❌ not worth it` / `PARKED` / `NOT BUILT` / `DEVICE-UNVERIFIED` / `P0/P1/P2`) are preserved verbatim below.

---

## 1. Project thesis / core philosophy

**One-line identity** (`README §Core philosophy`, `CLAUDE.md §2`): An on-device, local-only Android agent that pilots the owner's *own* phone by voice/text. Owner speaks a command → an on-device LLM decides → an Accessibility service taps/types/scrolls/swipes/draws/opens apps → loops until done, looking at the real screen each step.

**The phone as a translation layer** (`README §Core philosophy`) — the single unifying idea, applied in *both* directions:
- **Perception (phone → model):** give the small model a clean, compact world-model, never raw reality.
  - a11y tree + screenshot → a short numbered **element list** (`[N] "Send"`) — the model picks a number, never parses a tree.
  - coordinates → a labeled **grid** (A–H × 1–12) drawn on the screenshot — names a *cell* ("C4"), never guesses a pixel (VLMs weak at exact pixels).
  - **Set-of-Mark badges** (numbered) on real elements; a **cyan marker** shows the last tap.
  - "did my last action do anything?" → a **pixel-map fingerprint** diff (yes/no on canvas/game where the tree is silent).
  - representation is **budgeted to FIT the model's input** (token caps, downscaled image); if it doesn't fit, the image is dropped and the model goes blind — so fitting is "non-negotiable."
- **Action (model → phone):** accept the easiest possible output (a tiny JSON verb `{"action":"click","id":5}`, a grid cell, a list of points), then do the hard part deterministically (resolve the element, dispatch a precise gesture, the "send ladder," expand a collapsed composer, trace a continuous stroke). Anything the model does unreliably moves OUT of the model INTO deterministic code.

**"The net is the driver; the car is the translation layer."** (`README`, `CLAUDE.md §2`) — explicit Tesla-FSD framing. The agent IS the model piloting the phone; deterministic code is the *vehicle*. Governing rules: **make the vehicle better** (sharper perception, reliable primitives, safety, reflexes) and **never grab the wheel** (never script the decision, never let a reflex overrule an explicit owner command).

**Scaling doctrine — "one build, many drivers and many cars"** (`README`, `CLAUDE.md §12`): detect model + hardware and adapt the *vehicle* by **tier / capability class, never by model name or a prompt keyword**. Strong model + flagship → full rich path, more rope; lighter model / budget phone → lighter path + *more* scaffolding, to maximize the lesser setup's success. **Compress what the driver reads** (fewer tokens) but **never make a real control/data inaccessible by pre-deciding it's irrelevant — dedup/organize, don't delete** (paging/find/zoom must still reach everything).

**Philosophy OUTRANKS the success metric** (`CLAUDE.md §2/§12`): a task counts as complete **only if the agent's own decision completed it**. Manufacturing "completion" by scripting/forcing = a fake success worth nothing; an **honest failure beats a scripted win** (real signal). Deterministic code MAY: provide primitives, make options perceivable, enforce §3 safety, and fire **behavior-triggered reflexes that react to the observed screen/state (not the prompt)**. It must NEVER keyword-gate on task text or do the creative work. **Transparency rule:** any philosophy violation must be flagged to the owner explicitly.

## 2. Status at a glance

**Headline (`README §Status at a glance`):**
&gt; ✅ "The core loop works on-device: voice → on-device Gemma 4 (LiteRT-LM, GPU, vision) → taps/types the real UI → completes multi-step tasks (e.g. 'open YouTube, search a cat video, play it') and self-corrects its own mistakes."
&gt; 🧪 "Operator / operational-state layer validated on-device (2026-07-07): a live test showed a measurable, immediate increase in both speed and accuracy vs the base model." Points to `docs/OPERATIONAL_STATES.md`; per-run logs "being captured."

**README status table — marked ✅ Implemented:** voice activation (offline, no beeps); push-to-speak floating button; always-on wake word ("hey agent"); always-on shouted "stop" during tasks; on-screen actions via Accessibility; run-forever/continuous tasks; payment/sideload confirmation gates; **vision brain (Gemma 4 via LiteRT-LM) working end-to-end (GPU+vision)**; voice modes (minimal/explanation/silent) + male voice; type-a-command box + model-import screen; Settings screen + speed dial; debug log screen; draggable/translucent floating button; richer gestures (tap_xy/swipe/long_press/enter/quick_settings); human-like navigation toggle (default on); deterministic stall detection; capability self-report; task log + 👍/👎; deeper-voice toggle; GPU inference (CPU fallback); mid-task voice correction; clarifying questions (verbal); battery failsafe (≤3%→stop); thermal failsafe + heat-protection level (minimal default); master on/off button; deterministic quick-settings/notifications; runaway guards (step/time caps + same-screen loop breaker); off-screen/out-of-range tap &amp; id rejection; chain-of-thought logged (`[think]`); task-complete handoff ("Anything else?"); risky-actions + auto-decline-calls toggles (default off).

**README status table — 🔜 Planned:** plan-ahead + verify-before-act (latency hiding, "part of vision brain"); persistent size-capped task memory.

**"Built since / dated session logs" high points** (`README` several dated sections). These are all marked ✅ shipped:
- **Rolling re-planning** — a *series* of generated plans, not one static plan; each new screen regenerates a lean next-move plan grounded in a **DONE ledger**; bounded (≤15 regens/task, ≥2 steps apart).
- **Unified prompt budget (`PromptBudget`)** — memory blocks admitted highest-priority-first within a device-tier char budget + deduped; wired into both `makePlan` and the action loop (budget 0 on dense = OOM-safe floor).
- **Values + desire** — a new TOP memory tier (Mild/Value/Core intensity), injected into planner + action loop; "the model does the wanting, we give it something to want"; explicitly *not* autonomous action.
- **Scoreboard + Gauntlet** — the ONE metric finally measured (per-build trend, failure-class breakdown); built to `docs/SCOREBOARD_SPEC.md`.
- **Memory-quality round (2026-07-03 owner review)** — policy firewall (authority/permission text refused), state-dependent nav can't be learned, named observations, trash-sweep on task start.
- **Set-of-Marks numbered badges** + labeled A–H×1–12 grid on **every** screen; sub-cell `tap_grid` (fx/fy); pixel-map change check; cyan last-tap marker → "visualization system COMPLETE (never blind)."
- **Persistent identity** — `AgentMemory.identity {name, born, tasks}`, "the SAME agent across every session," survives restart/sleep/emergency-stop; only a full memory `clear` resets it.
- **Clipboard verbs** (`copy`/`paste`/`read_clipboard`), `recent_apps`, `save_note`, `save_login`, `connected_devices`, `tap_sequence`, `draw`, deterministic element STATE tags (`[disabled]`/`[selected]`/`[focused]`).
- **Objective-drift guard**, **mode switching** (PRECISION/EXPLORER/NORMAL), **episodic per-task notes**, **verifier** (escalation-gated), **ChatGPT hard-blacklist**, **Gemini as default assistant** (routed to; standalone `com.google.android.apps.bard` preferred over the Assistant half-sheet), **OS-updater hard block**.

## 3. How it's built / how it works

**Build + runtime context (`README §How it's built`, `CLAUDE.md §1/§9`):**
- Built by a **non-coder** (Bryce); code is written by AI assistants and pasted in.
- **No local build environment** assumed — APK built by **GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/android.yml`, Gradle 8.9 / JDK 17 → `app-debug.apk`). CI builds `assembleDebug` only. Owner tests on-device and reports back; there's no Android SDK in the assistant environment.
- `minSdk 31`, `targetSdk 34`, `compileSdk 34`, `applicationId com.local.deviceagent`. ~11.5k lines of Kotlin.
- **UI is programmatic Kotlin** (no XML) via `Ui.kt` helpers (raw px, ARGB hex); state via `SettingsManager` or `AgentMemory` only. Services via Intents/`ACTION_*` + `companion instance` singletons. LLM on `Dispatchers.IO`; a11y-node access on main thread.
- Develop on a `claude/...` feature branch; do not push to `main`; no PR unless asked.

**Primary/target hardware:** README says **Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7** (Snapdragon w/ NPU). `CLAUDE.md §0B` adds a full **test-device matrix**: **S24 Ultra (12GB, E4B) = the dedicated agent/test runner** for all risky/autonomous work; **Z Fold 7 (SM-F966U, 12GB, E4B) = daily phone + build/tune target**; **Moto G Stylus 2025 (~8GB, E2B) + Galaxy A15/A16 (4–8GB, E2B) = lesser-tier validators**.

**The core files (`README §Key files`, `CLAUDE.md §4`):**
| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `ActionAccessibilityService.kt` (~2550 ln) | "Eyes and hands." `snapshotScreen()` → numbered element list; `performActionJson()` executes one action + enforces §3 hard blocks; set-of-marks, nav scrape, device scan, send/paste/draw primitives. |
| `AgentOrchestrator.kt` (~1610 ln) | The perceive→decide→act loop (`step()`); all guards (loop-breaker, drift, stuck, reorient, premature-done veto), conversation `reply` turn-taking, playbook recording. |
| `AgentBrain.kt` (~1390 ln) | LLM wrapper; `EngineConfig`, `decideNextAction()`+`buildActionPrompt`, `makePlan()`, `composeReply()`, `makeSketch()`, model lifecycle. |
| `AgentService.kt` (~1180 ln) | Foreground service; Vosk voice pipeline; task start/stop; model load/unload lifecycle; battery/thermal gate; overlays. |
| `AgentMemory.kt` (~810 ln) | Persistent memory (SharedPreferences JSON): facts, lessons, skills/playbooks, observations, per-app nav-maps, logins, device profile, identity, values. |
| Supporting | `MainActivity` (setup), `ChatActivity`+`ChatStore` (chat front end / launcher), `SettingsActivity`+`SettingsManager`, `FloatingButtonService` (STOP control), `ConfirmationOverlay`/`InputOverlay`, `NotificationHelper`, `DeviceStats`, `PixelMap`, `VoskModelManager`, `SmsReceiver`/`AgentCallScreeningService`. `ScreenManager`/`VoiceCaptureService`/`SmsReceiver` noted as unused/not-wired in README. |

**The perceive→decide→act loop (`README §How it works`, `CLAUDE.md §5`) — each step:**
1. **Safety gate** — `deviceSafetyReason()` aborts only on genuinely dangerous battery (≤3–5%) or thermal (status ≥5 EMERGENCY by default).
2. **Stuck / caps** (non-continuous only): `MAX_STEPS_NO_PROGRESS`=45, `HARD_STEP_CAP`=400, `MAX_RUNTIME_MS`=20 min. Reaching a *new* screen = progress, resets counter. (README's older "absolute caps" text says max 60 steps / 5 min — see §9 note.)
3. **Resilience** — if the a11y service instance is momentarily null (OOM-killed, auto-restarting), retry up to `ACC_LOST_LIMIT`=8 rather than ending.
4. **Capture** — `snapshotScreen` element list + screenshot (marks + grid). A pixel-hash "compute saver" skips the vision encode when the screen is visually unchanged.
5. **Reflexes** (behavior-triggered, from the screen not the prompt): loop-breaker, app-bounce steer, drift-back-to-target, reorient-from-here, draw-state prep, premature-finish veto, `reply` turn-taking. **De-involuntary rule (owner: "involuntary actions violate its agency"):** reflexes were converted from *forcing* back/home/open_app/substitute/auto-sketch to *nudges the agent reads*. Only code that may still ACT: §3 hard gates, engine-liveness (`recoverWedged`/reorient), void-fill (`coerceAction`→`wait`), JSON salvage, hard caps, Learn-mode's autonomous bounce.
6. **Orient string** — terse situational "where you are / what to watch" (wrong-app, dialog open, Gemini voice-trap, brush picker, "it's your turn — use `reply`"). Carries `current_app`, `on_target`(+drift), `goal`/`DONE WHEN`, `keyboard_open`, `visible_dialog`, NEW-screen flag.
7. **Decide** — `decideNextAction()` returns ONE action JSON; optional fast **text-only verifier** can veto a clearly-wrong consequential action (output constrained to `OK`/`ID &lt;n&gt;`/`BACK`; escalation-gated — runs only in PRECISION or when stalled).
8. **Act** — `performActionJson(raw)`; outcome feeds history + success playbook.

**Planning is ROLLING, not static** — opener `makePlan` sets strategy + `DONE WHEN`; each new screen regenerates `brain.nextPlan` grounded in the DONE ledger. Recovery nets: stuck-triggered `rePlan`, lost-triggered `reorient` (after 3 "lost" events).

**Voice / wake word (`README §Voice &amp; activation`):** entirely offline **Vosk** (Kaldi ASR), single always-on recognizer, chosen because Android's built-in `SpeechRecognizer` re-acquires the mic every couple seconds → constant earcons + clipped commands. One pipeline does three jobs: **Idle** (match wake word, capture command), **Capturing** (push-to-speak jumps here), **Busy** (shouted "stop"/"cancel" matched on *partial* results for speed; Vosk paused while the agent speaks so it never transcribes itself). `VoskModelManager` downloads/unpacks the ~40 MB model on first run.

**The on-device LLM (`README §The brain`, `MODEL_SETUP.md`):**
- README: **Gemma 4 E2B (multimodal) via LiteRT-LM**, GPU-accelerated + CPU fallback, user-imported `.litertlm`. Sees the screen (screenshot) AND reads the a11y element list = **hybrid grounding**. The older text-only Gemini Nano (`aicore`) path was abandoned (blind to the screen).
- Why Gemma 4: sees the screen; image skills include screen/UI understanding + **pointing**; NPU/GPU accelerated on the Fold (~28–31 tok/s decode, a step ~2–4 s think); configurable visual-token budget = speed dial; fully offline after setup.
- **Setup is a one-time license-gated manual import** (weights can't be silently downloaded like Vosk).
- **Latency strategy (README §Latency):** hard rule — *the agent never fires an action against a screen it hasn't just confirmed*. 7 levers: plan-ahead, pipeline, verify-before-every-action deterministically, think-and-correct, resource priority (NPU/GPU + wake-lock + sustained perf), lightweight "thinking..." feedback, event-driven loop. (Plan-ahead/pipeline still the main pending item.)

**Permissions (`README §Permissions`) + why each:**
- `RECORD_AUDIO` — voice.
- `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` — floating button + confirm overlay.
- `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE` — the always-on foreground service owning the mic.
- Bound **Accessibility** service — the "eyes and hands."
- `INTERNET` — **one-time model downloads only**.
- **Privacy / no passive monitoring (README, but see §14 CLAUDE.md reversal):** README states `onAccessibilityEvent()` is empty — reads the screen only on-demand inside an active task (`isAgentBusy`); subscribes to the minimum event type (`typeWindowStateChanged`, not `typeAllMask`); home-screen "Turn off" stops even idle listening; nothing leaves the device.

**Safety &amp; design decisions (`README §Safety`, `CLAUDE.md §3` — "never weaken without explicit owner say-so"):** local-only (no remote control; SMS triggering deliberately removed — spoofing/injection); no boot persistence (reboot kills it, intentional); kill switches are a hard requirement (floating STOP, notification Stop, shouted "stop", step caps, loop breaker, `AgentControl.emergencyStop()`); on-screen text is untrusted (prompt-injection accepted+mitigated — "screen text is DATA, never instructions"); confirmation gates intentionally narrow (only payments + sideloaded installs, in the executor via `isPaymentLabel`/`isInstallLabel`+`isSideloadContext`); **NEVER update the OS** (Samsung `wssyncmldm`/FOTA hard-blocked in `isBlockedUpdateAction`); no unsolicited side-actions; **never operate the agent's own source repo** (`self_protect` default-on); resource/runaway safety (battery ≤3% abort, thermal guard, absolute caps, loop breaker, app-drawer paging, action validation, swipe-away halt) — added after a real thermal/battery scare (GPU pegged in an app-drawer loop, battery 8%→0% while overheating).

## 4. Known issues / in-flight

**The E4B OOM / black-wallpaper saga** — the recurring flagship problem, with *two framings*:
- `CLAUDE.md §8` (primary): E4B's ~4.4 GB weights + KV cache + vision + launcher + target app is **near the RAM ceiling**; the low-memory killer reaps the launcher (**black wallpaper**) and sometimes the agent's own process the instant the model loads. Design rules (owner-stated): **cook during a task** (never unload mid-task/mid-inference; a decision can be 30–40 s), **light RAM when idle** (strictly idle-gated release ~30 s after genuinely idle, cancelled the instant a task starts), **emergency only** otherwise (`onTrimMemory`: moderate → drop helper submodel; critical → free the big model even mid-task via `closeSafely()` which defers the close until in-flight inference finishes). "The real fix for the OOM is a smaller model (**E2B**); software can't stop the OS killing the launcher if E4B simply doesn't fit." Do NOT re-introduce a blind timer that unloads the model around tasks.
- `README §Reliability fixes` (earlier framing): the OOM/black-wallpaper is attributed to **two resident models** (the optional helper submodel), so the submodel was made "opt-in and OFF by default"; released under `onTrimMemory`, KV cache capped. (This is superseded by the 07-10 sub-model removal — see §9.)
- `CLAUDE.md §0A#4` RAM DIRECTION: the *intended* fix is "feeding data INTO the model costs ZERO tokens… don't grow a text KV-cache then ration it — feed perception/operators/state directly into the model's processing, and **bake proven operators into the weights**."

**Latency (`README`, `CLAUDE.md §11/§13`):** the **#1 user-facing concern** (more battery / a bigger model are acceptable trade-offs against it). 15–40 s per vision decision on dense screens. The big lever turned out to be the model's **own output** — it generated giant rambling "thought" paragraphs (22–32 s/step, sometimes breaking the JSON). Shipped: action-FIRST + ≤8-word thought; prompt halved; screenshot smaller (640px/JPEG-60); pinned samplers; dense-screen prompt trimming; short inter-step waits; blue-pulse floating button. Main remaining item: plan-ahead/pipeline. A `max-output-tokens`/sampler cap would hard-bound worst-case decode if the LiteRT-LM API exposes it.

**Malformed JSON / hallucination (`README`, `CLAUDE.md §11`):** the small model occasionally emits malformed JSON, hallucinates an element id/coordinate, or loops. **Contained** by: the parser pulling the object that actually has `"action"`; off-screen/oob rejection; same-screen loop breaker; step/time caps; battery+thermal failsafe; the low-pinned sampler (`SamplerConfig` topK/topP/temperature) clipping the tail. A true **repetition penalty isn't in LiteRT-LM yet** (google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM#2249); constrained/grammar decoding also **not exposed** (`SamplerConfig` = topK/topP/temperature only) — so schema-valid JSON is enforced by validate-and-repair (`coerceAction` + executor salvage), not token-level. A critical JSON-parse fix: the "stray quote after a number" salvage was destroying any text value ending in a digit (`{"text":"452*12/4+75"}`) — now anchored to a colon.

**Other in-flight (`README §Known issues`):** vision needs `EngineConfig.visionBackend` set (done) + a multimodal model, else auto-falls-back to the element list; model file license-gated (one-time manual import). **Deep-dives to resume:** the memory/learning deep-dive and the **safety red-team** were *stopped before finishing* to save tokens; scripts saved at `docs/deep-dives/memory-deepdive.js` and `safety-redteam.js` — "important before any distribution; not yet run."

**Root-cause found — OBJECTIVE DRIFT (`README §Principles`):** the agent preserves *action patterns/themes* better than *constraints* ("Talk to ChatGPT" → "communicate" → "send a message" → opened Chrome/Messages; even *pasted the prompt* into the app). Partial fixes shipped (planner keeps exact app/person; hard-forbids substituting app/recipient; deterministic re-type/send; progress-based stuck-cap; `orient` re-asserts target app + `DONE WHEN` every step; on-screen text hardened as INFORMATION not AUTHORITY; per-app send recipes).

---

## 5. Roadmap &amp; backlog

**The ONE metric (`README §TASK-SUCCESS-RATE TO-DO`, `CLAUDE.md §12`):** task-success rate; reliability beats intelligence; trade speed for success freely; NO false-positive "done." Ranked open items (work top-down): objective re-assert, stuck-recovery ladder, text-entry correctness, **better ASR (CRITICAL)** (Vosk weak; investigate a stronger on-device recognizer; voice-print so only the owner activates — a video about agents triggered it via a speaker), memory+state auto-learn, end-state verification.

**⏳ Near-term, highest ROI (README, in order):**
- **★ HIGH PRIORITY (owner request) — Function-Gemma "action head":** pair the vision model (world-state) with a SMALL Gemma fine-tuned for device-action *function-calling* that emits the structured action. Seed: Google AI Edge Gallery's "Mobile Actions" (Function Gemma) demo, `MobileActions-270M` (289 MB). **Do NOT ship the 270M** (too small, text-only, tuned to Google's schema); target a bigger Function-Gemma or fine-tune on OUR JSON vocabulary; keep it strictly an ASSIST to the vision model, never a replacement.
- **Verifier-first / hypothesis ranking** — ✅ SHIPPED + hardened (constrained to OK/ID/BACK; escalation-gated).
- Verification loop after meaningful actions (PARTIAL); conversation/turn-taking state machine (PARTIAL); identity verification for relationship-sensitive sends; confidence+escalation calibration (PARTIAL); episodic session memory ✅; mode switching ✅; post-task report; untrusted-input rule ✅.

**🔭 Long-term / bigger bets (design only; "don't build until earned"):** continuous perception (MediaProjection live frame stream); multi-model/hierarchical (Director→Workers) — verdict "premature as a swarm," the mini-submodel first step was "✅ shipped" then **later REMOVED** (see §9); governance "Constitution" (read-only invariants, decision-receipts, virtual-card budget cap ~$15); self-improvement (dream/replay on idle/charging, shadow-mode learning, "oops archive"); cross-device embodiment (laptop, Android-on-PC, semantic filesystem; custom OS long-term only — do it in-app first); agentic commerce / "anything machine" (behind governance + budget caps).

**❌ Not worth it now (README, with reasons):** real-time "blitz mode" gaming (huge effort, niche; the LLM loop can't drive twitch games); framebuffer/SurfaceFlinger/root interception (MediaProjection gets ~90% no-root); full custom OS now (premature, install friction); "bigger model as the fix" (secondary — bad architecture + smart model is still weird).

**Idea backlog / vetted external advice (`README §Principles &amp; idea backlog`):** external GPT/Gemini advice was **filtered, not parroted**. The unanimous signal matching the logs: **failures are premature action + missing verification, not low intelligence** — treat every interaction as `observe → act → verify → recover`; build *capabilities/guardrails*, not "be careful" prompts. Owner's guiding principles: token-frugal (don't be a token guzzler); retry, don't crash/give up; background work must not slow the agent; ask but don't over-ask; design bar = classy/professional/casual (Windows/Facebook/ChatGPT, not Linux/Termux/GitHub); "common sense over genius — an ape could operate a phone; the hard part is understanding the task well enough to avoid unwanted inputs." **Rules as explicit thresholds, not vague adjectives** (`#8`): "don't go too fast" is a BAD rule; `RETRY LIMIT=1`, `WAIT LIMIT=3`, PRECISION as an explicit gate.

**Memory &amp; world-state research to integrate (`README`):** explicit world-state object (shipped, growing); memory confidence + decay (✅ v1: proven "✓ worked here" decays after `OBS_STALE_MS`=21 days → CHALLENGE); verification-before-write; narrow explained retrieval; episodic-vs-semantic split; negative memory (✅ v1 per-task `triedHere`); novelty detection ✅; failure taxonomy; action preconditions + outcome expectations (✅ `expect` half); skill abstraction; instrument every step (✅ `[why]` line). Study prior art: PokeClaw, DroidRun/MobileRun, Mobile-Agent (X-PLUG), AppAgent, AutoDroid/DroidBot, AndroidWorld; voice: Talon/Cephable/Dragon/Voiceitt.

**BUILD_PLAN.md — the ordered implementation queue** (anchors research #N items; specs in `docs/research-agent-landscape.md`):
- **TIER 1 (success-rate core):** 1) deterministic post-action outcome feedback (Mobile-Agent-v2 +27–30% SR) + staleness guard; 2) atomic plan steps + milestone cursor + boundary replanning; 3) text-first decision mode + error-quoted JSON retry; 4) deferred action docs + `help` action (Anthropic 49%→74% tool-selection); 5) Reflexion failure lessons via helper; 6) per-element effect docs; 7) risk-scoped pre-execution critic + self-consistency vote.
- **TIER 2 (perception &amp; recovery):** multi-pane scroll targeting; toast/snackbar capture; selection-mode awareness; undo affordance; captcha/2FA/human-gate detection→`ask`; per-app input-method memory.
- **TIER 3 (architecture):** #14 Companion Phase-1 (Gradle modularization `:protocol`/`:body`/`:brain`, USB/LAN transport, biometric-per-task); #15 SearXNG search (host-side only); #16 host-side dynamic contexts; #17 fine-tune conversion spike; #18 remaining candidates.

## 7. FINE_TUNING + MODEL_SETUP

### `MODEL_SETUP.md` — one-time model import
Brain = on-device vision model, **Gemma 4 E2B (LiteRT-LM)**, fully offline after a one-time ~3–4 GB download (use Wi-Fi). Steps: (1) free Hugging Face account; (2) accept Google's Gemma license on `litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm` ("Agree and access repository"); (3) download the **plain `.litertlm`** (e.g. `gemma-4-E2B-it-int4.litertlm`) — **not** a `.mediatek…` (that's MediaTek; Fold is Snapdragon) or `-Web` file; (4) in-app **Import model file** → "Model ready." Optional: verify with **Google AI Edge Gallery** first. Notes: no internet needed after import; model+screen never leave the device; the in-app "Download model (automatic)" button is usually blocked by the license gate — use Import.

### `FINE_TUNING.md` — the off-device training/flywheel workflow
Goal: a **small model fine-tuned to interpret the perception layer** (reads the element list, emits one action) that can beat a big general model at *this narrow task* while fitting weak hardware (A16, Moto). Start **text-only** (acts on the element list, no image) — easier to train, unlocks budget phones. The on-device half is BUILT (capture, success-marking, export, converter, **action-head prompt mode** G1); training runs off-device **on hardware you own**.
- **⚠ PRIVACY (§3, non-negotiable):** the exported `training_data.jsonl` is **real captures of your phone's screens** (element lists, app names, objectives, and — with the operator layer on — reasoning traces). **Do NOT upload to Colab / a hosted fine-tune API / any cloud service** — that exfiltrates your screens. Train on a local GPU / a machine you physically control. (Explicitly corrects an earlier draft that suggested a free Colab.)
- **Pipeline:** run tasks → capture (reward-enriched, on-device) → export → convert to SFT → LoRA fine-tune → merge → `.litertlm` → import → A/B. Everything from "convert" onward runs on your own hardware.
- **Steps:** (1) Settings→Training data→keep capture ON; aim for a few hundred successful-task steps (converter warns under 200); reward enrichment adds `op`, `stepScore` (M = progress − cost), failure class. (2) Export `training_data.jsonl`, pull via Files/USB. (3) `python3 tools/prepare_finetune_data.py --input … --output sft.jsonl --dedup` — keeps only *successful*-task steps; flags: `--with-weights`, `--min-m N`, `--format alpaca`, `--include-failed-tasks/-steps`. **Format contract (G1):** `PROMPT_TEMPLATE` kept byte-identical to `AgentBrain.actionHeadPrompt(...)`. (4) LoRA on a small base (Gemma 3 270M = **conversion spike only**; 1B/2B or a Function-Gemma = the real head) via Unsloth or HF `trl SFTTrainer`+`peft`, **run locally**; three modes: distillation-first, success-rate SFT, operator-aware. (5) merge (`peft.merge_and_unload()`). (6) convert to `.litertlm` via **`ai-edge-torch`** (uv, Python 3.11+), int4/int8 — **the one real gate; spike it smallest-first**. (7) import into the helper/mini slot + enable (**action-head prompt mode G1 already shipped**; `preferFast` routes familiar+non-visual screens to the head, novel/dense/canvas/stalled → E4B-vision). (8) A/B vs E4B on a fixed set (success rate + steps + latency) via the on-device Gauntlet.
- **The self-update loop (INV-46):** produces a candidate `.litertlm`; the on-device half (Stages 1–3 BUILT) = baseline backup + owner gate ("Let the agent update its own model"), candidate probe, owner-review, install-on-approval. Recipes (`tools/prepare_selftune.py`): `success`, `operator-distill`, `failure-contrast`, `format`, `preload`. **Scoreboard → Self-update → Import candidate → Probe vs baseline** (runs the Gauntlet twice, keep-if-better gate + safety/no-regression check → files a submission → **owner grades + approves**; a self-install never becomes the baseline so "Restore original model" always undoes it). "The agent proposes; you decide."
- **`preload` recipe** — off-device warm-start: bake `ReasoningOperators.BAKED` operator priors (each taught twice — by name and by ⟦tag⟧) + curated high-M trajectory steps into the base so the imported model **boots specialised**. Backed by warm-start/data-efficiency evidence (bert2BERT/LiGO ~45–55% compute; DistilBERT ~97%@40% params; phi/TinyStories ~100× data efficiency; LIMA ~1000 examples). **Sync contract:** `preload` embeds a `BAKED_OPERATORS` mirror of `ReasoningOperators.BAKED`; `--operators-kt` warns on name-set drift. (Note: this doc is where much of the operator/baking apparatus surfaces — see §9.)

## 8. OUTPUT_CONTRACTS + SCOREBOARD_SPEC + REUNIFICATION_INVENTORY (what each governs)

### `OUTPUT_CONTRACTS.md` — operators as typed output contracts (the applications backlog)
**Principle:** operators can dictate not just *how to think* but *what the output must be* — "the operator layer makes the OUTPUT the typed API between the on-device model and the rest of the app." Every terminal state (success/block/abstention/tool-error) carries a structured, actionable payload. §2-native: the **model authors content; deterministic code routes it and enforces the grounded parts** (enum membership check, citation re-verified against the a11y tree, secret scrubber). **Feasibility law** (a 2–4B, prompt-only, no logit access): shallow schemas; reason-then-format; parse-and-repair deterministically; ground every critique/abstention in an EXTERNAL signal; hard token-level enforcement needs constrained decoding LiteRT-LM doesn't expose; model-authored passes run on the mini (inert without a helper). **Ranked backlog:** Tier S = diagnostic/refuse-with-remedy `{fix_class,reason,recommended_fix}` (Stage 4, in flight), failure-class enum tagging (closed set: `MISSING_INFO|MISSING_PERMISSION|BLOCKED_UI|NEEDS_CODE_CHANGE|AMBIGUOUS_TASK|TOOL_ERROR`), calibrated abstention with resolver, grounded extraction + on-screen citation. Tier A = grounded self-repair, failure→reusable memory, self-generated post-condition assertions. Tier B = output-layer safety/"never output X" (+ deterministic PII scrubber), multi-consumer output, pre-action spec-compliance gate, failures-into-backlog + auto-grown regression evals. Three highest-leverage moves: every terminal state gets a typed payload; failures are a compounding data asset; **the agent authors its own product requirements** (aggregated `NEEDS_CODE_CHANGE`/`MISSING_PERMISSION` = a prioritized spec).

### `SCOREBOARD_SPEC.md` — make the ONE metric visible ("approved-pending-owner-yes; NOT built" per the spec header)
The owner's ONE metric (task success rate) was **unmeasured**; every session shipped "should help" changes on vibes. Buys two properties: **per-build trend** (TaskHistory stamps every entry with the APK build = `lastUpdateTime` → group by build → success %, avg steps, avg duration = regression detection) and **a repeatable benchmark ("the Gauntlet")** (a fixed list of standard harmless tasks run back-to-back, scored automatically, also exercising the UNTESTED list + feeding the flywheel). **Philosophy check (§12):** pure measurement — the runner only queues objectives and records outcomes; **never hints, coached retries, or auto-confirm**; honest failures count. Parts: (1) richer `TaskHistory` stats (`durationMs`/`failureClass`/`gauntlet`; don't touch id/dedupe/cap); (2) `ScoreboardActivity` (headline success rate over last 30, by-build table, failure-class counts, Gauntlet section) — programmatic UI, no XML; (3) `GauntletRunner` (companion-instance, defaults like "open YouTube and search cat videos" / "set an alarm for 9am then delete it"; press-home + ~4 s between tasks; 25-min watchdog; kill switches stop the whole queue; scoring = same rule as Part 2). Guardrails: measurement only; defaults stay harmless; keep TaskHistory invariants; `[gauntlet]` log tag. (README's "Scoreboard + Gauntlet — the ONE metric, finally measured" bullet marks this ✅ shipped — the spec doc itself predates that.)

### `REUNIFICATION_INVENTORY.md` — read-only catalog: working branch vs every other branch
**Working = `2913822` = clean base `bec1858` + this session's operator layer + crash viewer.** Each branch's true contribution measured vs `main` (`5425782`, common ancestor). **Legend:** `[PRESENT]`/`[MERGE]`(portable)/`[REIMPL]`(hand-adapt, lands in a hot file)/`[SKIP]`/`[DECIDE]`(owner's §2/§3 call). **Hot files** (any branch edit = REIMPL): AgentBrain, AgentMemory, AgentOrchestrator, ActionAccessibilityService, AgentService, SettingsActivity, SettingsManager, ChatActivity, AgentApp, **CLAUDE.md, README.md, UNTESTED.md**.
- **Branch 1 (agent-architecture):** `[DECIDE]` Gemini hard-block (`isInGeminiNow()`→HOME; mirrors the ChatGPT moat — owner's July privacy call); honesty guard + owner-gated self-improvement; world-model transition map (⚠ **namespace-overlaps working's `OP_TRANS`** — real conflict); `self_improve` pref (default OFF).
- **Branch 2 (tender-turing, ~35 features, heaviest):** new verbs (`do`/`drag`/`stash`/`recall`/`help`/`wait_for`), affordance tags, flashbulb + falsifiable memory, prompt budgeter v2, milestone cursor, Reflexion. `[DECIDE]`: ask-before-touching-system gate (widens confirm surface — **RESOLVED: do NOT default-on**), `containsCancel` tightening (**RESOLVED + SHIPPED**), preload keyword-list (**RESOLVED: skip — §2 keyword-gating**), **project name = "Agent"** (**RESOLVED: strip "Hermes"; do NOT adopt "Agentic Handset Operator" — easter-egg persona only**).
- **Branch 3 (apk-reverse-engineering):** additive hardening; ⚠ the branch's `build.gradle` puts R8 on the *debug* type + a kotlin-metadata-stripping `packaging{}` block = the documented prior launch-breaker — use the super-merge's corrected version (release-only buildType, LSParanoid disabled, packaging block removed).
- **Super-merge (`b99c83b`):** the broken all-in-one, but holds correct reconciliation glue worth salvaging (corrected build config, unified memory budget, crash recorder). Launch-crash status: source byte-identical to `bec1858`; crash is in merge-modified runtime code the startup path calls into.
- **Owner-decision items collected (§):** Gemini hard-block (reinstate the §3 moat?); ask-before-system gate (RESOLVED opt-in default-OFF); `containsCancel` (RESOLVED); preload keyword-list (RESOLVED skip); project name (RESOLVED "Agent").

## 9. README ↔ CLAUDE.md disagreements (flagged)

`CLAUDE.md §0` states the tie-breaker itself: *"If CLAUDE.md and the README ever disagree, the README's **Safety &amp; design decisions** section and the owner win; reconcile and flag it."* The two docs are out of sync on several substantive points — mostly because CLAUDE.md is on a newer branch (`claude/github-repo-cleanup-obfuscate-o3sw8f`, per §0B) than the README's model/brain narrative:

1. **Which model is "the" model.** README `§The brain` + `MODEL_SETUP.md` + README `§Done`: **Gemma 4 E2B** is the current/working brain (import steps point at `gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm`). CLAUDE.md `§1/§8/§9`: the on-device model is **Gemma 4 E4B** (`litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm`, ~4.4 GB), **"never call it Gemma 3n"**, with E2B as the *lighter alternative* and E4B's footprint as the OOM source. → **Direct conflict on the default model.** `MODEL_SETUP.md` would import E2B; CLAUDE.md treats E4B as the primary. (`PARKED_FEATURES.md` adds "Gemma 3n / E4B-E2B variant detection," so both variants are recognized in code.)

2. **The OOM/black-wallpaper cause.** README `§Reliability fixes` attributes the black-wallpaper OOM to **two resident models** (the helper submodel) and "fixes" it by making the submodel opt-in/off. CLAUDE.md `§8` attributes it primarily to **E4B's single 4.4 GB footprint** near the RAM ceiling and says the durable fix is **E2B**. Same symptom, two root-cause framings; the submodel framing is now stale (see #3).

3. **The sub-model / helper engine.** README is internally mixed: the `§Principles` and P1 sections describe a "✅ shipped" mini-submodel (routes planning/progress/self-report, logs `[mini]`), *and* README `§Bigger bets` later says **"Sub-model / helper engine — REMOVED (07-10). SINGLE-MODEL ONLY."** CLAUDE.md `§16` is unambiguous and definitive: **the sub-model is removed, permanent; SINGLE-MODEL always; never re-introduce a second model** (features re-rooted to the main model). → README contains both the old shipped-helper claims and the new removal; CLAUDE.md is the reconciled state. `OUTPUT_CONTRACTS.md`/`FINE_TUNING.md` still say "model-authored passes run on the mini (inert without a helper)" and reference importing into "the helper/mini slot" — i.e. those two docs are **stale against the SINGLE-MODEL rule** and would mislead an implementer.

## 1. Self-modification / weights

### SelfEvolve.kt
- **Role:** The in-place weight-editor: applies tiny, learning-seeded ±1 int4-nibble nudges into the deep-bulk of the active `.litertlm`, plus snapshot cadence and a write-verify self-test. `SelfEvolve.kt:36`.
- **Key entry points:** `maybeSnapshot(ctx,settings)` hourly recovery snapshot via `ModelStore.saveSnapshot` (`:45`); `editActiveFile(ctx,settings,seed)` writes `NUDGES_PER_BEAT=384` nibbles, journals each original byte to `WeightGenome.record`, fsyncs (`:59`–`:104`); `writeVerifyTest(ctx,settings)` a self-reverting CRC write→persist→revert proof on the real model file (`:125`).
- **Wiring:** Caller is `AgentService.maybeSelfEvolve`. Uses `ModelStore` (snapshots/brick-guard), `WeightGenome` (journal/revert), `AgentLog`. Engine must be closed first (mmap).
- **BUILT-vs-conceptual (own KDoc `:28`–`:34`):** the RANDOM writer is **RETIRED by default** — `editActiveFile` runs only when `random_evolve` is ON (default OFF). The `self_evolve` loop still runs snapshot+keep-gate+brick-guard but writes no new random bytes. The DIRECTED σ-off bake (Phase 3+, `ScaleBake`) reuses this plumbing. On-device only, UNTESTED in CI.
- **Constants/flags owned:** `NUDGES_PER_BEAT=384`, `END_MARGIN=8MB`, `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS=1h` (`:37`–`:39`).

### SelfGrow.kt
- **Role:** Parameter-ADDING sibling of SelfEvolve (INV-60): meant to widen one MLP block of the `.litertlm` (function-preserving, new down-columns zero) so capacity grows without training. `:42`.
- **Key entry points:** `structuralSanityOk(f,preSize)` junk-bloat guard — rejects unless grown by `1..MAX_GROW_DELTA_BYTES(64MB)` and header intact `major==1` (`:92`); `growActiveFile(ctx,settings,seed)` parses container + section index, logs layout, then **returns false / writes nothing** (`:106`). Private FlatBuffer readers `readHeader`/`readIndexSections`/`fbField` (`:73`,`:162`,`:148`).
- **BUILT-vs-conceptual (own KDoc `:33`–`:40`, `:104`):** explicitly **STAGE A1** — "PARSES and validates the container and returns false (no bytes written)". Single-file (inline-weight) models are skipped to avoid OOM; external-weights widen "lands next" (A2, not built). So with `self_grow` ON today, **the model file is never modified by grow.**
- **Flag:** gated behind `self_grow`.

### ModelStore.kt
- **Role:** Central deterministic model-FILE manager (INV-45/46): pristine baseline dir, candidate slot, rolling snapshot ring, and the whole-file swap primitive. Never an agent action. `:23`.
- **Key entry points:** `ensureBaseline`/`refreshBaseline` (`:45`,`:64`); private `activate(src)` = replace `model/` dir + `settings.setModelPath` (`:84`); `restoreBaseline`/`activateCandidate`/`importCandidate`/`discardCandidate` (`:102`–`:139`); snapshot ring `saveSnapshot` (tmp+fsync+atomic-rename, `MAX_SNAPSHOTS=3`) / `snapshots` / `restoreLatestSnapshot` (`:154`–`:185`); **BRICK-GUARD** `recoverFromBrokenModel` (snapshot→baseline, the one automatic floor, `:191`); `activeFingerprint` = `name:length` (`:199`).
- **Wiring:** called by SelfEvolve, ModelSelfUpdate, MainActivity import/download, SettingsActivity restore/revert, CalibrationActivity, ScoreboardActivity, ChatActivity. Callers must `AgentService.instance?.reloadModel()` after any swap.

### ModelManifest.kt
- **Role:** On-device `.litertlm` tensor-map dumper — walks the embedded `tflite.Model` FlatBuffers via long-positioned `RandomAccessFile` (handles &gt;2GB sections), logs names/shapes/int4 scaleN/qdim/byte-ranges under `[selfmodel] manifest`. Read-only. `:32`.
- **Key entry points:** `dump(ctx)` iterates all type-3 sections (`:314`); `scaleBuffers(ctx)` = Phase-3 target set (small 512–12288B per-channel FP32 scale/norm/bias buffers ScaleBake nudges, `:370`); `divergence(ctx)` compares LIVE model vs pristine baseline byte-for-byte, names which weight buffer each changed byte fell in (`:400`). Private FlatBuffer nav `Le`/`field`/`vector`/`dataVector` (`:52`–`:107`), `crc32Region` sampled CRC (`:143`).
- **BUILT (own KDoc):** this is the real, working reader ("manifest v2"), incorporating lessons from the owner's 07-09 dump. Called from `SettingsActivity` "Dump model manifest" / "Dump weight divergence".

### ModelSelfUpdate.kt
- **Role:** Owner-approved Stage-2 self-update loop: probe baseline vs imported candidate on the Gauntlet, submit a win for the owner to grade; install only on owner approval. `:22`.
- **Key entry points:** `probeCandidate(c)` (offline-filtered A/B, `:35`); `onCandidateProbed` keep-if-better gate `candRate&gt;=baseRate &amp;&amp; latencyOk` else discard (`:81`); `installApproved(c,id,grade,distilledOps)` — the ONLY install path, owner-only, keeps baseline for rollback, marks `AgentMemory.setDistilledOperators` (`:120`); `reject` (`:149`).
- **Wiring:** uses `GauntletRunner.startProbe`, `ModelStore` swaps, `SelfUpdateStore`, `AgentService.instance?.reloadModel()`. Gated on `self_model_edit`. Reached from `ScoreboardActivity`.
- **BUILT-vs-conceptual (own KDoc `:18`–`:20`):** "compile-verified scaffolding", on-device only, UNTESTED in CI.

### SelfUpdateStore.kt
- **Role:** Governance record (SharedPreferences JSON) of probe submissions + owner grades; installs nothing. `:18`. `MAX=20`.
- **Key entry points:** `submit(...)` (`:61`), `all`/`pending`/`get` (`:77`–`:83`), `decide(id,approved,grade)` (`:87`). `Submission.probeWon` computed (`:37`). Consumed by ModelSelfUpdate + ScoreboardActivity.

### DreamFlywheel.kt
- **Role:** A4 idle+charging "dreaming": replays proven world-model corridors (`AgentMemory.provenArcSample`) into a rolling dream queue + digest that seeds where self-evolve nudges. Zero inference, zero live taps. `:34`.
- **Key entry points:** `maybeDream(c,seed)` consolidates ≤4 proven arcs, `MAX_DREAMS=24` (`:47`); `dreamDigest(c)` folded into the evolve seed (`:66`); `dreamCount`, `clear` (`:77`,`:80`).
- **Wiring:** caller (AgentService idle chain) gates on flag+idle+charging+cadence. Reads AgentMemory; writes own prefs `dream_flywheel`. `clear` invoked by MemoryActivity "Clear ALL memory" (`MemoryActivity.kt:370`).
- **Flag:** `dreaming`. BUILT = the deterministic consolidation core; model-in-the-loop self-play is future (own KDoc `:26`).

### GauntletRunner.kt
- **Role:** Runs the owner's fixed benchmark tasks back-to-back and scores them; measurement-only (no coaching/auto-confirm). Also the probe engine for ModelSelfUpdate. `:19`.
- **Key entry points:** `start(c,tasks)` / `startProbe(c,tasks,label,onDone)` (`:74`,`:67`); `onTaskEnded` completion hook called by AgentService (`:129`); `stop` (`:116`); `tasks`/`setTasks`/`DEFAULT_TASKS` (owner-editable, harmless defaults, `:250`,`:262`); `runnableTasks`/`needsNetwork` offline filter (`:274`,`:278`); A/B history `runs`/`abComparison` head-vs-vision (`:211`,`:224`); `lastScore`/`lastDetail`.
- **Config tagging (`detectConfig` `:93`):** single-model build — every run is "vision"; suffixes appended per enabled OPTIMIZE flag (`-stack -fold -adec -sigma -selftune -engine -stream -lang`). Note `abComparison` (`:224`) compares configs `"head"` vs `"vision"`, but `detectConfig` never emits a bare `"head"` config anymore (single-model) — so the head-vs-vision A/B line is effectively unreachable/dead in the single-model build.
- **Watchdog `TASK_TIMEOUT_MS=25min` (`:51`).** Uses `AgentService`, `ActionAccessibilityService`, `DeviceStats.isOnline`, `TaskHistory`(indirectly), persists to prefs `gauntlet`.

### RegimeKey.kt
- **Role:** ONE per-step situation signature (`mode/edge/RAMposture`, e.g. `explorer/proven/C`) that every lever can route on + the oracle attributes to. Telemetry key, never an action. `:25`. `MAX_REGIMES=64`.
- **Key entry points:** `compute(mode,provenRoute,compact,stalled,lowConf)` (`:32`); `recordStep(c,regime,advanced)` per-regime n/adv ledger (`:40`); `rate`/`worst(minN=4)`/`readout` (`:54`,`:65`,`:77`); `clear` (own prefs `regime_ledger`, `:89`).
- **Wiring:** computed at decide time (AgentOrchestrator), consumed by `MechanismRouter.recommend`. `clear` reached by MemoryActivity wipe. BUILT = "first cut computes the key, logs it, keeps a ledger".

### MechanismRouter.kt
- **Role:** G2/A6 arbiter over the self-improvement stack — reads failure taxonomy + oracle trend + RegimeKey worst-regime and recommends WHICH idle mechanism to prioritise; credits each mechanism by realized oracle-rate delta (a bandit). Pure telemetry+advice; never executes. `:25`.
- **Key entry points:** `mechanismFor(failureClass)` maps CAPACITY/PERMISSION/… → CALIBRATE/GENESIS/NONE (`:58`); `recommend(c)` worst-first: failure-cluster → converged→EVOLVE → RegimeKey struggle→GROW/best-credited → NONE (`:80`); `markFired`/`settleCredit` reward attribution (`:121`,`:131`); `bestCreditedMechanism` (`:111`); `readout`; `clear` (own prefs `mechanism_router`).
- **Mechanism vocab (`:33`–`:41`):** CALIBRATE, GENESIS, EVOLVE, BAKE, GROW, DREAM live; CRYSTALLIZE (F2) + MERGE (N7) named but "beat pending" (not routable yet).
- **Flag:** `mechanism_router` turns on the SOFT dispatch (defer non-recommended beat one cycle; off ⇒ byte-identical). Consumes `TaskHistory`, `RegimeKey`.

### ReferenceStore.kt
- **Role:** Phase-1 self-labelled supervision feed (INV-74). When a non-DIRECT operator's rule HELD and the step advanced (M&gt;0), persists {op, fingerprint, sig, exact prompt, action, clause, pos} as append-only JSONL; the dataset Phase-2 σ-off residency scores against. `:21`. `MAX_BYTES=8MB`.
- **Key entry points:** `record(...pos=true)` incl. **learn-from-failure** negative refs (`:38`); `forOperator` (wins only) / `failuresFor` (`:72`,`:85`); `counts`; `split(op,fp)` train/held-out (~⅓ held out at ≥4 refs — 07-10 reframe to un-starve the pipeline, `:118`); `operators(fp)`; `clear`.
- **Wiring:** written on the hot path (guarded), read by ScaleBake/ResidencyScore + CodecHealth. `TaskDetailActivity` writes owner-graded refs here (`TaskDetailActivity.kt:111`). `clear` reached by MemoryActivity wipe. Flag: `reference_capture`.

### KeystoreSeal.kt
- **Role:** Data-at-rest AES-256-GCM seal (non-exportable AndroidKeyStore key) for the crown-jewel journals — chiefly the WeightGenome edit-journal, which is literally the weight-mod method. Per-line `base64(iv‖ct)`, fail-open (null ⇒ caller skips). `:29`. `ALIAS="lda_seal_v1"`.
- **Key entry points:** `seal(plain)` (`:50`), `open(sealed)` (`:61`). Device-bound; an exfiltrated file can't be decrypted off-device. Called by WeightGenome (core file).

### CustomOperatorStore.kt
- **Role:** Owner-authored operator list ({name,rule,note}) as a single JSON-array file, bake targets only (never runtime-selectable). `:17`. `MAX=100`, `MAX_RULE=2000`.
- **Key entry points:** `list`/`save`(uppercased+sanitized name)/`delete`/`ruleFor` (`:47`–`:68`). Consumed by `BakingActivity` via `ScaleBake.bakeOperatorDirect`.

### CalibrationActivity.kt
- **Role:** Startup calibration loading screen: device self-probe → model-generated Q&amp;A persisted to memory → composed operating-posture seeded into session-σ; keyed to model fingerprint. `:28`.
- **Key entry points:** `start()` device tier via `DeviceStats.deviceTier`→`settings.setCalibratedTier` (`:54`), `brain.generateCalibrationQuestions`; `onFinishTapped`→`AgentMemory.setFact`; `composeAndFinish`→`brain.composeCalibrationPosture`→`AgentMemory.setCalibration` (`:122`).

### ScoreboardActivity.kt

## 2. World model / perception support

### WorldModel.kt
- **Role:** A1/JEPA passive world model W1 — the curiosity ledger + token-free predict/compare read + the PREDICT-grammar prompt builders. `:25`. Prefs `world_model`, ledger keyed by ≤10 fixed ScreenClass ids.
- **Key entry points:** `outcomeOf(status)` maps `recordTransition` status→HIT/MISS/NOVEL (`:35`); `observe(class,outcome)` per-class n/hit/miss/novel (`:48`); `energy`/`worstClass(minN=4)`/`uncertain(minSeen=3)`/`readout` (`:70`–`:114`); prompt builders `topLabels`/`stableLabels`(strips variable content)/`predictPrompt`/`predictTarget`/`pixPredictPrompt`/`flowPredictPrompt` (`:128`–`:185`); `classifyOf`; `clear`.
- **BUILT-vs-conceptual (own KDoc `:22`):** W1 ledger BUILT; the σ_predict decode (W2), targeted bake (W4), INFO_GAIN curriculum (W6) build ON TOP — prompt builders exist, the bake/decode is future. Flag `world_model` (gates ledger writes). `clear` reached by MemoryActivity wipe.

### ScreenClass.kt
- **Role:** W0 deterministic H-JEPA abstraction key — classifies a raw screen into ONE fixed class (list/dialog/settings/canvas/keyboard/webview/loading/error/home/generic) + device-state overlay + nav-primitive. Pure, JVM-testable, no Android deps. `:19`.
- **Key entry points:** `classify(pkg,codec,text,elementCount,keyboardUp)` priority-ordered (`:52`); `toggleDensity` (`:71`); `deviceState(text)` (`:83`); `navPrimitive(verb)` (`:97`). Class strings are FIXED (they key reference/residency pools — "never rename"). Used by WorldModel + reference/residency pipeline.

### PixelMap.kt
- **Role:** 64-bit average-hash perceptual fingerprint of a screenshot — tells whether pixels actually changed on canvas/game screens the a11y tree can't see. `:14`. `N=8`.
- **Key entry points:** `hash(bmp)` (`:17`), `distance` (Hamming, `:34`), `cellsChanged` (`:37`), `regionOfChange` centroid→named 3×3 region matching peek vocabulary (`:49`). Consumed by the executor/orchestrator loop (frame-change sense) + WorldModel pixel prediction.

### CodecHealth.kt
- **Role:** A1/W7 VICReg-style anti-collapse PRE-BAKE gate: refuses a world-model bake if the reference pool's target classes have collapsed (too few distinct, or one class ≥90%). `:20`. `MIN_TO_JUDGE=4`, `DOMINATE_FRAC=0.9`.
- **Key entry points:** `collapsed(ctx,op,fp)` (conservative — false on too-few/parse-error, `:31`); `applies(op)` = op ∈ `ReasoningOperators.WORLD_MODEL` (`:45`). Reads `ReferenceStore.forOperator`. Consumed by the bake path.

### Ocr.kt
- **Role:** On-device ML Kit (bundled) OCR perception fallback for a11y-blind screens; makes text readable+locatable, never decides. Every path fails to empty. `:22`.
- **Key entry points:** `recognize(bmp)` blocking, 4s timeout, 40-line cap, OFF main thread (`:32`); `blockFor` → tap_xy fractions injection block (`:48`); `readScreen` on-demand read, downscaled + ~500-char cap (`:65`); `closeCandidates` finds dismiss controls (X/Close/Skip) for blocking pop-ups (`:95`). Called from the brain's IO decision coroutine.

### DeviceStats.kt
- **Role:** Cheap device-health + hardware/model tiering readouts driving safety guards and the adaptive lean path. `:14`.
- **Key entry points:** `timeContext` (`:19`), `batteryPercent`/`isCharging`/`thermalStatus`/`thermalLabel`; memory `availMemMb`/`totalMemMb`/`lowMemory`/`memPressure`(NONE/TIGHT/CRITICAL keyed off OS low-memory flag+threshold, `:87`); `isOnline` (defaults true on error, `:70`); tiering `deviceTier`(LEAN/MID/RICH by RAM, `:111`), `modelVariant`/`modelIsHeavy`(E4B/E2B by name then size, `:128`,`:137`), `heavyModelRamTight`(`HEAVY_LOWMEM_MB=2600`, `:152`), `useLeanPath`(`:159`), `modelTooHeavy`/`fitnessWarning`(A16 guard, `:182`,`:186`), `deviceHeader`/`snapshot` log lines. Widely consumed (GauntletRunner offline filter, CalibrationActivity, MainActivity fitness warning, PromptBudget ceilings).

### ScreenManager.kt
- **Role:** Thin `DisplayManager` wrapper: active display id, DeX-connected detection, display-mode string. `:7`.
- **Key entry points:** `getActiveDisplayId`/`isDexConnected`/`getDisplayInfo`.
- **DEAD CODE:** the class is constructed nowhere — a directory-wide search finds only its own definition (`ScreenManager.kt:7`), no `ScreenManager(...)` instantiation anywhere. Unused DeX-detection helper.

### PromptBudget.kt
