## 6. Contradictions, stale docs, and dead code (factual, with anchors)

**A. Flag KDoc says "Default OFF" but code defaults ON.** The `SettingsManager` header (`:6`–`:22`) acknowledges this and declares the per-flag "Default OFF" clauses superseded, but the individual KDoc bodies were left unedited, so each still literally reads "Default OFF =&gt; byte-identical" while returning `true`. Most notable because their own comments flag risk/untested status:
- `continuous_stream` (`:235`): KDoc says "Default OFF … keep default OFF on RAM-tight devices … UNTESTED on-device" — yet defaults ON.
- `vision_skip_proven` (`:179`): KDoc "§13-sensitive … gated hard … Default OFF. Build/enable last." — yet ON.
- `evidence_mode` (`:110`): KDoc "When OFF (default)" — yet ON.
- `agent_language`, `operator_binding`, `operator_stacking`, `fold_verify`, `adaptive_decode`, `session_sigma`, `self_calibrate`, `continuous_engine`, `startup_calibration`, `imitation_learning`, `light_operator` — all KDoc "Default OFF/byte-identical", all code ON.

**B. `auto_resume` (`:682`–`:683`) is a genuine behavior contradiction, not just doc lag.** The KDoc describes the DESIRED behavior as the OFF behavior ("it should chill out and wait to be prompted… by default the killed task only resumes when the owner taps Resume"), and `SettingsActivity.kt:151` caption says "Off by default." But `getBoolean("auto_resume", true)` defaults it ON — so out of the box a plain re-run auto-continues a killed task, the opposite of the stated default intent.

**C. SettingsActivity captions are stale relative to code defaults.** Numerous captions still tell the user "OFF by default (experimental A/B)" / "Off by default" for flags that are ON in `SettingsManager` — e.g. operator binding (`:187`), stacking (`:193`), fold-verify (`:199`), adaptive-decode (`:205`), session-σ (`:211`), self-calibrate (`:253`), continuous-engine (`:259`), self-model-edit (`:282`), evidence-mode (`:223`), imitation/passive/ambient (`:449`,`:455`,`:461`). The UI misreports the actual default state to the owner.

**D. `ambient_watch` is ON by default but INERT.** `SettingsManager.kt:656`–`:665` states plainly "currently INERT — NOT wired to a fuller read… nothing reads this flag YET." So the toggle exists and defaults ON but changes no behavior — flag-name implies ambient learning that isn't built.

**E. `self_grow` ON but writes nothing.** `SelfGrow.growActiveFile` is STAGE A1 — it parses/validates and **always returns false without writing** (`SelfGrow.kt:106`–`:141`). The flag name/Settings copy ("Let it GROW its own model (add parameters)") implies active parameter-adding, but the widen (A2) is not implemented; only the snapshot/guard/log plumbing runs.

**F. `self_evolve` ON but the random writer is retired.** `SelfEvolve.editActiveFile` is only invoked when `random_evolve` (default OFF) is on (`SelfEvolve.kt:30`–`:33`). With defaults, `self_evolve` runs snapshots + keep-gate + brick-guard but writes **no new weight bytes** until the directed ScaleBake (Phase 3+, a core file) supplies them. So "the model evolves its weights live" is, at current defaults, plumbing-only for the random path.

**G. GauntletRunner head-vs-vision A/B is effectively dead in single-model.** `abComparison` (`GauntletRunner.kt:224`) requires a run tagged config `"head"`, but `detectConfig` (`:93`) only ever emits `"vision"` (+optimize suffixes) since the helper/head model was removed (07-10). No run is ever labeled `"head"`, so the A/B line never renders.

**H. SmsReceiver.kt — dead + contradicts stated design.** Not registered in the manifest (no receiver/`SMS_RECEIVED`/`RECEIVE_SMS`), and its purpose (SMS-trigger activation) is exactly what `MainActivity.kt:35` says was "deliberately removed (spoofing / prompt-injection risk)." Orphaned leftover file.

**I. ScreenManager.kt — dead code.** Never instantiated anywhere in the codebase (only its own definition, `ScreenManager.kt:7`). Unused DeX/display helper.

**J. VoiceCaptureService.kt — orphaned.** Declared in the manifest but never started by any Kotlin code (no `Intent(..., VoiceCaptureService::class.java)` except its own outbound one). Live voice paths use `AgentService.ACTION_LISTEN_NOW`/`ACTION_CONVERSATION` + Vosk instead, so this `SpeechRecognizer` wrapper is unused.

**K. Minor:** `SettingsManager` groups the `directed_bake` getter (`:326`) between `random_evolve`'s getter and setters — cosmetic ordering only, both work. `MechanismRouter` names `CRYSTALLIZE`/`MERGE` mechanisms whose beats are "pending" (`:39`–`:40`), so `recommend` can never currently return them.

---

**Cross-subsystem wiring summary:** The self-improvement data flow is `ReferenceStore`/`ExecStepStore` (capture) → `ScaleBake`/`ResidencyScore` (core, σ-off scoring) gated by `CodecHealth`, journaled by `WeightGenome`+`KeystoreSeal`, snapshotted/brick-guarded by `ModelStore`, with `MechanismRouter` (reading `RegimeKey`+`TaskHistory`+`WorldModel`) arbitrating which idle beat (`SelfEvolve`/`SelfGrow`/`DreamFlywheel`/bake) fires — all owner-gated via `SettingsManager` flags and surfaced/controlled through `SettingsActivity`, `ScoreboardActivity`, `BakingActivity`, `CalibrationActivity`, and the memory/task activities. `MemoryActivity.confirmClear` (`:357`–`:373`) is the one place that wipes the sibling ledgers together.</result>

# FACTUAL MAP — Local Device Agent (on-device Android agent)

Scope note: The **deck** (`docs/PATENT_DECK.md`) markets a curated **"25-invention portfolio"** for lawyers; the **support doc** (`docs/PATENT_SUPPORT.md`) is the real, full portfolio — **81 numbered inventions, INV-1 … INV-82 with INV-80 absent** (no such entry exists). ## 1. INVENTION INDEX (INV-1 … INV-82; INV-80 does not exist)

Source: `PATENT_SUPPORT.md §1` portfolio table + `§2/§2B` disclosure bodies. There is also a **model-agnostic umbrella invention** above the table — **"★ The Generalized Training Method: Ablation-Gated Consolidation of In-Context Behavior into Weights"** (`§` before `§1`), of which INV-71…74 are the concrete on-device embodiment; filed as its own broad independent claim.

**Group A — Thinking / operator layer**
1. **INV-1 — Operator layer:** model *selects* a named natural-language reasoning stance ("operator") before each action; per-step reward + learned per-app transition value are credited to stances and **surfaced, never argmax'd** — the router is the model itself.
2. **INV-2 — Reflex→operator transformation:** converts a deterministic forced-action/veto reflex into a decline-able model-selected operator, with a formal guarantee it never lowers (and strictly raises) expected reward whenever the reflex's precision &lt; 1.
3. **INV-3 — Self-correcting world-model transition table:** compact (app, screen-sig, action)→next-screen table, self-correcting by predict/verify, used to **predict-then-surface** outcomes so the model "looks before it leaps" at the cost of a table lookup, not a forward pass.
4. **INV-4 — Closed-loop distillation flywheel:** operation *is* the training signal — each step captured in the **exact** prompt shape later used to train/run a distilled "action head," reward-labeled, adoption gated by on-device A/B on success + latency.
5. **INV-5 — Action Guard:** light always-on deterministic validity layer + narrow sovereign safety gates **plus** a model-*selected* external-verifier operator; an improper call becomes a surfaced re-decision, never a crash/silent misfire/dead-end.
6. **INV-6 — Falsifiable memory:** disproven beliefs are *kept, not deleted*, surfaced as cautions, can **re-earn trust**; paired with a model-selected DOUBT operator that consumes them.
7. **INV-7 — Two-speed adaptive compute:** fast text-only action head + slow vision model behind one interface; the model's **own stated confidence** + screen **structural novelty** choose how much perception/compute to spend.
8. **INV-8 — Cognitive-limit awareness:** deterministic reflex measuring the model's own context pressure + a model-selected FOCUS operator that compresses screen and accumulated context.
9. **INV-9 — Human-curated + model-selected move library + value priors:** owner-authored moves and owner-set "values" enter the same model-routed menu as machine-learned ones (human curates the experts; model still routes).
10. **INV-10 — Procedural coordinate generation for graphical output:** model emits a *coordinate program* (free-curve point lists + primitives as 0–1 canvas fractions) rendered as touch strokes, with a per-call variation seed, canvas-band clamping, and multi-stroke completion pacing — no scripted/templated art.
11. **INV-11 — Exact non-hallucinating read-only text layer:** exact on-screen values carried in a *separate* read-only layer from the tappable list; under token pressure it **shrinks not vanishes** and appends an explicit omission notice ("more exact text on screen; do NOT guess it").
12. **INV-12 — Adaptive vision-encode skipping:** skip the 15–40 s encode when a **perceptual hash** shows the screen unchanged, OR when the a11y tree already labels ≥ a **tier-scaled fraction** of interactive elements; the same hash is reused as an **action verifier**.
13. **INV-13 — Rolling re-plan against a milestone ledger:** regenerate a lean plan on each new screen grounded in a deduped/capped **completed-milestone ledger**, run as a **non-step "planning beat"**, ordered so the plan tail truncates first; a "done" verdict only *nudges* a verify operator.
14. **INV-14 — Resident large-model RAM lifecycle:** keep the ~4 GB model resident through a task, release only when genuinely idle/not generating, **defer close until in-flight inference completes**, ride out the first OS critical-trim and shed a smaller helper first, act only on **sustained** pressure (OS-threshold-relative).
15. **INV-15 — Verified navigation-memory formation:** commit a nav belief only on a **persisted second sighting** + destination within a **~1.2 s causality window** + (cross-app) the tapped label naming the destination; drop **state-dependent** transitions.
16. **INV-16 — Multi-window/foldable perception:** read every app window, order spatially, emit pane headers, keep **element ids global across panes**, share the element/char budget (split-screen/DeX/foldable).
17. **INV-17 — Guarded label-retargeted batch execution:** execute a model-emitted batch one step/tick **against fresh perception**, re-resolving each target **by label** (not stale id), guarding typing, **aborting the queue on any divergence** — batched execution with no per-step model call.

**Group B — Perception / prompt-window efficiency**
18. **INV-18 — Self-improving persistent operator library:** the agent **authors its own** operators; admitted only if **novel**, kept across tasks only on **positive measured reward**, else pruned — self-expanding-then-self-reducing, governed externally.
19. **INV-19 — Relevance-surfaced operator selection:** rank + surface only operators relevant to the grounded state (active structural signals + per-app proven reward), rest reachable — selection as an ordering functional.
20. **INV-20 — Plan-time grounded pre-mortem:** from negative-transition + prior-failure memory, surface which risky/irreversible steps are likeliest to fail so the plan routes around them; kept out of the re-shown plan to save tokens.
21. **INV-21 — Same-step non-penalizing kick-back:** a malformed/off-list/off-target action is **handed back in-loop** (after re-perceiving) as a corrective re-decision, **excluded from the give-up counter** — a garbled output can't dead-end a working task.
22. **INV-22 — Typed self-diagnosing failure terminal:** every give-up emits typed `{fix_class, reason, recommended_fix}` from **external loop signals**, one enum routing two consumers — a private self-fix lesson vs an owner-facing remedy; never leaves the device.
23. **INV-23 — Perception-failure protocol (blind ≠ lost):** detect that sensing failed (screenshot AND UI tree empty) as an axis **orthogonal to navigation**, suppress nav-recovery reflexes, terminate with a hardware/CAPACITY remedy instead of looping.
24. **INV-24 — Per-call decode bound on shared-KV LLM:** cap **output** length per call-type and abort cleanly, because the KV cache is a shared input+output window with no output reservation and native decode faults are uncatchable — an unbounded generation would crash the process.
25. **INV-25 — Helper-less deterministic operator surfacing:** when the operator-selector helper model is absent, a **deterministic relevance rank** surfaces the single most-relevant operator clause at **zero added inference** — the one build adapts to its driver.
26. **INV-26 — Positional-saliency prompt assembly:** one priority/volatility signal governs both which context blocks survive the token cap AND their decode-distance — invariant identity/tools/safety as stable PREFIX, volatile screen+contract at the end (recency), app rules dense-gate out, SAFETY pinned.
27. **INV-27 — Homogeneous-list collapse w/ single-source render set:** ≥6 consecutive structurally-identical a11y rows fold to 3 representatives + "+N more [id range]" while every row stays reachable; one `lastRenderedIds` set feeds both the text list and set-of-marks badges; state-bearing rows break the run.
28. **INV-28 — Phase-attributed inference accounting:** all model calls funnel through ONE `generate()` choke logging per-task count + wall-ms per **phase** (decide vs off-step condense/plan/replan) split by engine; telemetry only, never enters a prompt.
29. **INV-29 — Constraint dashboard:** the §3 refusal predicates (OS-updater, own-repo, code-runner, blocked-assistant/Gemini) are **inverted** into a terse orient line naming the wall + sanctioned escape verbs before acting — post-decision perception, never pre-blocks a token.
30. **INV-30 — Verbalize-to-load-workspace reflex:** on a live money/account/destructive control, prompt the model to write its current objective + intended target into its verbalized "thought" **before acting** (global-workspace grounding), keeping an off-task agent from drifting into an unintended payment/login.
31. **INV-31 — Foveated perception with region-relative marks:** model emits a region-selection; engine renders that region magnified, re-bases numbered badges onto the crop while every element keeps a **stable global id**; code also proposes an objective-independent busiest region; net token-reducer used as the dense/overflow floor.
32. **INV-32 — Hierarchical merit-propagating operator composition:** operators organized into a feed-forward aggregation net — Tier-0 leaves → Tier-1 composites (max-pool + coalition bonus + learned weight) → Tier-2 master emitting one stance header + winning clause; reward credit flows up; cold-degrades to flat baseline byte-for-byte.

**Group C — Operational-state theory / mid-session**
33. **INV-33 — Event-timed staleness gate:** the a11y window-transition event timestamps the last screen switch; if a transition occurred after a decision's dispatch and the action is consequential, don't execute against the stale view — re-perceive; uses an already-subscribed event, reads no screen content.
34. **INV-34 — Token-free between-snapshot change-sense:** XOR the current screenshot's perceptual hash against the prior frame's to localize which region changed (centroid of flipped 8×8 cells → named region); surfaced as a cue + a `peek region:"changed"` target — change-sense at zero model tokens.
35. **INV-35 — Streaming action extraction:** drain the decode token-by-token, watch for the first complete balanced top-level JSON action object, stop + execute the instant it completes (stop effected by tearing down the session) — act *as* the decision forms.
36. **INV-36 — Self-authored resume context:** persist the model's own rolling condensed "where I am" note as a resume payload; a payload outliving the process is the uncontrolled-kill signal; on re-run it's re-injected (gated: only on explicit "resume" or an auto-continue toggle) — cross-session memory as output-becomes-next-input, no auto-start.
37. **INV-37 — Agent-aimed deterministically-triggered precision action ("aim/shoot"):** model elects an `armed` primitive + target + trigger condition (element appears/disappears; region changes/settles) + action; deterministic code polls the cheap signal sub-second and fires through the **same executor path** (all safety gates apply), timeout-bounded.
38. **INV-38 — Density-tiered scaffolding compaction:** the always-on scaffolding (action menu, rulebook) itself compacts to ~1/3 tokens on a dense screen while keeping every capability reachable; the emergency-overflow fallback carries an **un-strippable safety-and-steering floor**.
39. **INV-39 — Operator-elected self-relenting kick-back of a demonstrably-false move:** fires only when the model elected a COMMON_SENSE operator AND the move is provably contradicted by device state (e.g. `done` while not in the target app); kicks back with a reason, **relents** after a bounded budget.
40. **INV-40 — Model-initiated perception-request loop with warm-KV continuity:** the model emits a perception verb (peek/ocr/find/get_text/assert/read_clipboard/zoom/connected_devices), decode pauses, code fetches, a fresh pass resumes with the datum surfaced; on-device analog of prompt-cached tool-calling.
41. **INV-41 — World-model-gated elision of a redundant planning pass:** skip the rolling re-plan when the world-model holds a **proven edge** out of the current screen (≥2 confirmations, 0 misses) and no low-confidence flag; build the condense deterministically from the milestone ledger, calling the model only when genuinely lossy.
42. **INV-42 — Bidirectional agent-native codec:** re-encode both channels into a **token-binding** language — perception: each element → ≤2-token handle `⟨id⟩⟨role?⟩⟨state?⟩` (label dropped for text-bearing, kept for icon-only), vision-gated; action: short mnemonic codes (`cl5`, `pk9`, `st5:msg`) taught 3 ways, soft-enforced by a correct-or-abstain decoder that still accepts JSON.
43. **INV-43 — Operational-state programming of a frozen model:** the context window is a program `σ‖c` — an operational state σ (axioms/constraints/cost-functions/output-schema, placed FIRST) makes the fixed weights compute `G_σ(c)=f_W(σ‖c)`, binding output via attention re-weighting + distribution-narrowing + a transient low-rank edit `ΔW_σ`, no logit/decode access; economically **spends captured training compute**.
44. **INV-44 — Folding N off-step passes into one decode:** each off-step pass (re-plan/condense/verify) is an operational state `σ_X`, so it's **folded** as a stacked state on the decision pass — removes passes rather than adding them; budget-guarded, A/B-gated.
45. **INV-45 — Agent-applied persistence of a computed improvement into its own model file:** the deterministic host writes a known-good weight-delta/adapter into the on-device model (computed delta / on-device flip-and-keep search / precomputed patch library), owner-gated, reversible, never autonomous, never data-triggerable; concept (self-install step not yet reduced to practice).
46. **INV-46 — Open-ended success-gated self-tuning w/ target-agnostic keep-if-better + owner grade:** candidates produced off-device by **any recipe** over own trajectories, scored on-device by a keep-if-better **probe** (only cares if agent-driven success rose), every probe-passer requires **owner grade** before install; lead recipe = **operator distillation** (distill an operator into weights, inject only its short TAG at runtime).
47. **INV-47 — Mid-session fine-tuning (between-turn ΔW_σ over persistent warm-KV):** effective computation changes between turns as σ evolves; a **persistent warm-KV session** makes σ accumulate rather than reset; default-OFF spike with under-pressure teardown fallback.
48. **INV-48 — Operator-requested owner-gated durable self-edit:** the model *during inference* emits a self-edit REQUEST ("distil operator X"), the host fulfils it through the INV-46 gate; model picks the goal, pipeline computes the bits, owner approves the install; concept.
49. **INV-49 — On-device self-supervised next-action prediction over owner demonstrations:** in a privacy-gated passive mode, form a hidden prediction of the owner's next action and score it (shadow mode); **predict-and-score on-device, weight-update deferred** to the off-device owner-approved pipeline. BUILT: the Learn-mode demonstration half (`predictAndScoreDemo`); ambient-idle variant deliberately NOT built.
50. **INV-50 — Compatibility-gated stacking of formal operator constraints:** stack top-K **compatible** operators' rules under one header (`σ₁‖σ₂‖…‖c`), admissible regions intersect (tightens grounding); compatibility structural (same composite tier), drops to K=1 on dense screens; each member shares the decision's reward.
51. **INV-51 — Operational-state-driven adaptive decode budget:** a confident/predictable σ (proven route, not stalled/exploratory) gets a **shorter** decode cap; safe because streaming extraction halts at the first complete action. Flag `adaptive_decode`.
52. **INV-52 — Startup operational-state calibration:** boot the frozen model into a per-owner/per-device operating state via a **device self-probe** (sets compute knobs to tier) + a **model-generated interview** + a composed **operating posture** seeded into session-σ; keyed to model fingerprint. Flag `startup_calibration`.
53. **INV-53 — On-device operator self-calibration scored by measured reward + EXACTNESS:** author sharper operators on a fresh stall, keep/prune by measured reward — not just "did it help" (M) but "did its restriction HOLD" (**exactness = 1 − escape rate**); a leaky operator is pruned even if the outcome looked okay. Flag `self_calibrate`.
54. **INV-54 — On-device gradient-free effective-weight self-tuning:** propose→evaluate→keep-if-better over operator variants scored on M + exactness, keep proven-AND-exact; the **operator library is the source of truth, weights are a cache**; proven-exact operators surface as owner-approved distillation candidates. Flag `self_calibrate`.
55. **INV-55 — Off-device structured-preload recipe:** emit a curated set baking the agent's operator priors + high-reward trajectories into the base so an imported model **boots specialised** then self-calibrates on-device; authored by `tools/prepare_selftune.py --recipe preload`, run off-device by the owner.
56. **INV-56 — Continuous in-session self-improvement engine:** closes σ-accumulation (INV-47) + operator self-tuning (INV-53/54) into one loop — score the step, evolve σ from what's proven this session, **fold the proven-exact result back into σ** the model reads next turn; helper-less, zero-inference. Flag `continuous_engine`.
57. **INV-57 — Persistent live-conversation loop w/ overflow-aware KV recycling:** hold ONE warm KV across a task's turns so σ carries/evolves; read the actual `getTokenCount` and **recycle before overflow**; mid-decode `cancelProcess` keeps the session; the one pending native primitive is KV-rollback-after-cancel (filed feature request). Flag `continuous_stream`.
58. **INV-58 — Owner-initiated autonomous self-improve loop inside a deterministic safety envelope:** on an owner button, the model chooses its own SAFE next goal and loops while self-tuning; every §3 hard gate fires on the ACTION regardless of goal, bounded by a chain of always-live kill switches; autonomy is over **goal selection only**, never the safety region.
59. **INV-59 — Autonomous continuous on-device self-modification (random walk):** the host permanently rewrites bytes of the packed-int4 weight region, seeded by the agent's live learning, in idle gaps, under rolling-snapshot + **brick-guard**; bounded ±1 nibble nudges; `evolving` interlock prevents mmap race. Flag `self_evolve` (default OFF; **RETIRED/default-off since `a59c731`** — it was degrading the model).
60. **INV-60 — Autonomous on-device GROWTH of the model's own weight file:** function-preserving MLP widen (up/gate gain output rows, down gains zero-init input cols → output provably unchanged, capacity dormant), host rewrites the FlatBuffer + repacks the container + reloads; guarded by a structural sanity/junk-bloat check + post-grow probe; **total up, active bounded** (paired w/ INV-61). Flag `self_grow` (default ON).

**Group D — Directed weight-baking / self-improvement stack**
61. **INV-61 — Operator-driven DIRECT RAM control:** a model-elected COMPACT-vs-FULL posture drives, together, the decode cap + memory-block budget + vision path AND narrows the model's own active-cluster recruitment — the single controller of both deterministic knobs and activation region; bounds ACTIVE RAM even as total capacity grows.
62. **INV-62 — Single-model gradient-free self-tuning flywheel w/ deterministic exactness oracle:** the credit/exactness/feedback loop runs on ONE model, no gradients; a **substring-grounding oracle** (every digit-bearing token in an action checked against screen+clipboard+objective) replaces the second-model verifier.
63. **INV-63 — Persistent per-application learned operational-state controller:** on clean completion, persist the earning stance coalition + which proved exact, keyed by app; re-entering the app seeds the operating state — per-app fine-tune-without-training, no gradients/second model. `[sigma] saved per-app posture`.
64. **INV-64 — Operator-identity-sealed self-mod seed + σ-off-validated crystallization:** a self-mod seed derived ONLY from proven-operator identity (excludes on-screen data, closing the injection gate); a kept edit must pass a **σ-off acceptance test** (base + stance-removed matches base + stance-on) proving a transient capability crystallized; owner-gated install.
65. **INV-65 — Reversible per-edit weight-delta journal ("git-for-weights") + measured keep-gate:** each edit beat journaled as a named reversible delta (position + ORIGINAL byte per nibble), byte-precise undo; a keep-gate accumulates edits into a window and reverts exactly that window only on a success-rate regression clearing a noise margin — gradient-free hill-climbing, no probe model. Flag `weight_gate`.
66. **INV-66 — Idle+charging "dreaming flywheel":** in an idle+charging gap replay the agent's own proven world-model as a simulator, consolidate proven corridors into a dream digest, fold it into the **seed** of the weight-edit beat (steers where the forge nudges); takes NO live action, touches NO model file, never writes the success oracle. Flag `dreaming`.
67. **INV-67 — Failure-taxonomy mechanism router + realized-reward credit bandit:** map recent failure type (or converged state) to the self-improvement mechanism that addresses it (recalibrate/author-operator/crystallize/grow/hold); a credit bandit attributes rate changes; **soft dispatch** (defers a non-recommended beat this cycle only). Flag `mechanism_router`.
68. **INV-68 — Foreign-window interrupt-and-resume reflex:** detect a foreground swap the model did NOT cause (permission controller/installer/in-call/phone), record a resume waypoint, **surface** a "handle or dismiss then resume" nudge; never auto-grants/dismisses, never taps the intruder; the imposed-vs-initiated distinction is the crux.
69. **INV-69 — Always-on multi-axis attributed acceptance oracle:** at each honest task end, attribute the **agent-driven** outcome (owner-STOP excluded) to the operator coalition × σ × flag-set, maintaining per-axis (n, successes) cells — a continuous per-config A/B ledger; the trusted fitness signal the whole stack (INV-65/67) rests on. `[oracle]`.
70. **INV-70 — Operator VM normal-form reduction:** compile stacked operator conjuncts into normal form (normalize each clause to a key, dedup, drop subsumed) so the CONSTRAINT block carries only genuinely-additional conjuncts once — removes the stacking-interference redundancy; falls through to single-rule inject on parse miss. Flag `operator_stacking`.
71. **INV-71 — On-device named-tensor localization + weight-edit provability:** a pure on-device reader resolves a NAMED quantized tensor to its exact writable byte-range + per-channel scale by walking the multi-GB `.litertlm` + each embedded TFLite FlatBuffer with LONG absolute positions (inline AND appended buffers, section-end bounds check); per-region **CRC32 proves** exactly which bytes an edit changed. (The concrete embodiment of the umbrella method.)
72. **INV-72 — Proven-outcome-gated, injection-immune operator reference capture:** at the zero-inference credit seam, bank `{operator, fingerprint, screen-sig, exact input, emitted action}` ONLY when the agent's **own** decision provably worked (rule HELD ∧ step ADVANCED); the gate is a proven agent outcome, not on-screen text — the feed that later edits weights is **injection-immune at the data layer**.
73. **INV-73 — σ-off residency fitness:** forward-pass-only merit — σ-ON = stored action (clause present), σ-OFF = re-decode with the operator's rule clause deleted; LOW σ-off↔σ-on agreement ⇒ behavior NOT resident in base weights (strong bake candidate); the same measure re-run after a bake **certifies** it took. Both pre-bake selector and post-bake certifier, no gradients.
74. **INV-74 — σ-off-gated directed ScaleBake:** replaces INV-59's random walk with a **directed edit of only the per-channel FP32 SCALE/RMSNorm vectors** (the DoRA *magnitude* axis, native+free on int4, located by INV-71) for the lowest-σ-off-residency operator; bounded nudge journaled reversibly, kept only if σ-off agreement rose past a noise margin ∧ a coherence probe passes — **non-degrading by construction**; graduation collapses a resident operator's clause to a ~1-token tag.
75. **INV-75 — Single per-step regime key:** derive ONE small enumerable code per step (task-mode × world-model edge state × RAM posture) so all levers (adaptive-decode/RAM-operator/PromptBudget/oracle/router) share credit through one partition instead of smearing across incompatible bins; telemetry+context key, deliberately NOT app-specific. `[regime]`.
76. **INV-76 — Contrastive σ-off residency + sign-flip bake gate:** run the same forward-pass ablation over **failure** references (σ-ON = stored BAD action); HIGH contrast ⇒ failure mode resident (push AWAY); the keep-gate becomes two-sided (keep if good-residency rose OR bad-residency fell; revert if bad rose even when good rose) — never entrench a failure. Flag `directed_bake`.
77. **INV-77 — Zero-inference exactness oracle for output-binding + loop-freedom:** two zero-inference checks from state the loop already has — output-binding exactness (raw output parsed as one clean action needing no salvage) + loop-freedom exactness (move's key absent from this screen's ✗-tried set) — so FORMAT/anti-loop operators become bakeable on single-model hardware.
78. **INV-78 — Regime-routed mechanism arbitration w/ capability-ceiling escalation (MetaFitness):** route an idle beat on the shared regime signature; the worst persistently-weak regime gets the best-credited mechanism; if it stays stuck across a real sample, a **MetaFitness** escalation treats it as a capacity ceiling → routes to self-grow (the only path to grow, excluded from failure-class routing); continuous-KV-floor embodiment reclaims RAM from graduated operators.
79. **INV-79 — Harness-installed action layer:** model the whole action layer (~2800 tok, 68% of KV) as bakeable capabilities (SCHEMA/VERB/NAVIGATE/LAYOUT, each a binding rule + an exactness signal for 3 of 4), score σ-off residency, run the reversible coherence-gated scale bake restricted to that set; on graduation a **drop-seam** collapses the verbose block to a tag + lowers the KV floor — the model generates the action from resident knowledge at ~0 prompt tokens.
81. **INV-81 — Passive on-device JEPA world model:** a gradient-free next-screen predictor self-trained ONLY from the owner's own use — the transition store's predict/verify reconcile IS the prediction energy in a compact screen-embedding (not pixels), aggregated per abstract **screen-class** (H-JEPA), variable content marginalized as a latent residual, the proven-predictable invariant installed into weights via the σ-off-gated scale bake (INV-73/74).
82. **INV-82 — Reference-free direct install of a known operational state:** bake a formal operator constraint into int4 weights from **self-generated in-code probes** (no task history, no proven-outcome corpus) — decode twice per operator (rule-on = known state, rule-off = base); if σ-OFF already agrees, skip + drop prompt text; else hill-climb a bounded reversible scale nudge toward the fixed σ-ON target; solves the cold/fresh-import starvation (`delta=0B, no scored operators`); one owner button installs the whole defined library.

*(INV-80: no entry — the sequence skips it.)*

**Cross-cutting theme (a candidate independent claim, `§1`):** *"deterministic code MEASURES a grounded signal and SURFACES it; the model SELECTS/DECIDES; code never argmaxes the signal to act"* — the "surface-not-argmax, external-grounded-signal" discipline unifying the whole portfolio.

---

## 2. §1A END-TO-END WALKTHROUGH (condensed)

A small AI model running **entirely on the phone** (no cloud) reads the screen, decides the single next action (tap / type / swipe / draw), executes it, looks again, and repeats until the owner's spoken/typed goal is done; the hard part is making a *small* model reliable where mistakes cost real money or data. The pipeline (each step naming its inventions): **(1)** deterministic code turns the messy live screen into a short clean element list ("button 3: Send"), reads pixels or a folded second window when needed, and lets the model *ask to see more on demand* (INV-11/16/3/40). **(2)** Before choosing an action the model first picks a **reasoning operator** — a named plain-English stance ("PLAN", "EXPLORE", "PREMORTEM") — shown only the relevant ones ordered by what has worked on this app; a stance written as a precise top-of-input rule is an **operational state** that makes the one fixed model compute a different rule-bound function with no retraining, *spending compute already paid for at model-build time* (INV-1/43/19/9/18/6/8). **(3)** For consequential moves it consults a self-built "when I did X here, this happened" map, optionally runs a second-opinion check, and at plan time runs a pre-mortem routing around likely-failing steps; a light backstop catches moves the phone's own state proves false (INV-3/20/5/39). **(4)** The chosen action passes one light safety-and-validity checkpoint; a malformed/garbled action is **handed back to the model, not counted as a failure**; only a few genuinely dangerous categories (code-runner, OS updater, own source, blocked chatbot) are ever hard-stopped (INV-5/17). **(5)** Each step is scored (progress − cost), credited to the chosen stance (good stances re-offered, unhelpful ones dropped, self-invented ones survive only if they measurably help), and quietly captured in the exact format to later train a faster model on the owner's own hardware — the flywheel (INV-1/18/4). **(6)** The loop repeats spending only as much compute as the moment needs — fast text-only brain on easy screens, slow vision brain on hard ones, model kept loaded during a task and freed when idle; output is length-bounded so a runaway can't crash the phone; the operator nudges still work in a lighter form on a phone too small for the helper; scaffolding text shrinks on crowded screens and even the emergency fallback keeps the safety lines; a redundant re-plan is skipped when the phone-map knows a proven route (INV-7/14/13/24/25/38/41). **(7)** When it *can't* finish it **fails usefully** — fixed code reads the real reason from loop signals, labels it from a small enum, and gives the owner a plain "here's what you can do" (only for owner-fixable causes; self-fixable ones become a stored lesson); the special "I'm blind" case (both screenshot and UI tree empty) is recognized as distinct from "I'm lost" and stops cleanly instead of looping (INV-22/23). **(8)** Between tasks, on a dedicated device, it keeps a scrupulously honest scorecard attributing each *agent-driven* outcome (owner-STOP excluded) to which stances/posture/flags were on; when idle+charging it "dreams" (replays proven routes to steer where it nudges its own model); model nudges are measured trial-and-error with a per-change undo log rolled back on a real regression; an arbiter points idle effort at the mechanism addressing the actual failure cause — all off by default, all only able to reschedule/undo *self-improvement*, never to choose a tap (INV-69/65/66/67/68). **The unifying thread:** fixed code measures something real and shows it to the model; the model decides; fixed code never overrides except to stop a few hard-coded dangers.

## 3. E4B_ARCHITECTURE — the `.litertlm` model-file map + divergence/baking protocol

Full file: `docs/E4B_ARCHITECTURE.md`. Built from real on-device `ModelManifest.dump()` `[selfmodel] manifest` logs (the "Dump model manifest" button). Model is **Gemma 4 E4B** (`litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm`, int4, LiteRT-LM, GPU+vision) — the doc is emphatic: **"Never call it Gemma 3n"** (it carries Gemma-3n *features* — Per-Layer Embeddings, MatFormer nesting, Conformer audio tower — but is Gemma 4 E4B). Hidden size **2560**, vocab **262144**.

**Container layout (`§1`, from `manifest v2 size=3659MB … weights-section=false`):** ONE `.litertlm` container ~**3659 MB** on the owner's device (nominal ~4.4 GB), **NOT a single TFLite model** — a sectioned container; each **type-3 section is a standalone `tflite.Model` FlatBuffer**. **12 sections** = 1×type-5 (tokenizer/metadata, 11 KB) + 1×type-4 (4.5 MB aux) + **10×type-3 models**:
- sec#2 **token embedder** `[262144,2560]` int4 (167 MB) — tied w/ sec#10 output embedder (CRC `aacb8c08`).
- sec#3 **per_layer_embedder (PLE)** — stacked `[262144,256]` int4 tables (836 MB).
- sec#4 **audio Conformer encoder** (hidden 1024, int4, 92 MB); sec#5 audio adapter (1536→2560).
- sec#7 **vision encoder** `VisionEncoder` hidden 768, **FP32** (224 MB, `int4seen=0`) — not an int4 bake target; sec#8 vision→text adapter `[2560,768]`.
- sec#6/#9 tiny stateful-call stubs (10 KB).
- **sec#10 ★ MAIN GEMMA DECODER** (2260 MB, ~**42 layers**, int4) — **the bake target**.
- sec#11 **MTP drafter** (multi-token-prediction head, 45 MB).

**Where the weights live (`§2`):** sec#10 is the **only** section with **external/appended** buffers (`external=791`); all other sections store weights **inline** in `Buffer.data`. The decoder's int4 weights are **raw appended buffers** (`Buffer.offset&gt;0`) referenced by graph ops — **NOT** standard quantized TFLite tensors (a tensor walk finds only 2 int4 tensors, the tied embedder). **Rule: localize decoder weights by the EXTERNAL-BUFFER MAP (offset+size → dims), then read the consuming op to bind buffer→layer/role→its scale buffer. Do NOT use the tensor walk here.** Dtypes: `dt=19`=int4 (bake targets, `scaleN=shape[0]` per-output-channel scale), `dt=9`=int8 (KV), `dt=2`=int32, `dt=6`=bool, `dt=-1`=FP32. **The int4 per-group (scale, 4-bit code) IS DoRA's (magnitude, direction)** — the FP32 scale vector is a free native DoRA-magnitude knob (this is what INV-74's ScaleBake edits). The v7 histogram: **790** distinct external buffers — including 126×`[2560,10240]` int4 FFN matrices (÷3 projections/layer ⇒ **42 layers**), attention q/k/v/o buckets (small 0.64 MB count consistent with GQA), and **211×10 KB length-2560 FP32 vectors = per-channel scales / RMSNorm weights**. Open detail (`§2.3`, bake-time, needs no dump): the histogram proves scales exist but doesn't bind each scale→its weight matrix; FFN scales are group-packed **inline** (sec#10 has 31,089 inline buffers) — resolved by reading the dequantize op that consumes a weight buffer.

**Provability (`§4`):** `crc32Region(raf,off,size,budget)` samples first+last 128 KB of a byte-range. The tied input/output embedder CRC match (sec#2 `inline@… crc=aacb8c08` == sec#10 `ext@… crc=aacb8c08`) **proved** the `ext@` addressing reads the right bytes end-to-end and CRC is a reliable fingerprint — the measurement substrate for every bake (edit → re-CRC → confirm only the intended bytes changed). Reader internals in `ModelManifest.kt` (`§5`): `Le` long-position little-endian RandomAccessFile reader (handles &gt;2 GB sections without heap OOM), FlatBuffer nav helpers, `walkModelSection()`, subgraph cap 4096.

**ModelStore baseline + divergence-dump protocol (`§5A`, `§6`):** The `.litertlm` is **designed to be modified in place** by two gradient-free mechanisms — `self_evolve` (INV-59, random ±1 int4 nibble walk) and `self_grow` (INV-60, param-adding MLP widen). **Current status (07-09): likely byte-identical to import** — `random_evolve`/`self_evolve`'s in-place writer is **RETIRED/default-OFF** (`a59c731`, it was degrading the model), the directed Phase-3 bake isn't built, and `self_grow` only fires in auto-mode + changes file SIZE — so **nothing routinely changes the weights** until the directed bake lands. The write path is **PROVEN on-device** (Settings → "Test weight write": wrote to the live model, stuck to disk, reverted exactly). What is STOCK = the **structure** (sections, external-buffer layout, ~42 layers, dtypes). What CAN DIVERGE = the **contents** (int4 weight bytes / CRCs, added params / file size). The pristine **baseline** is a copy stashed at import in `ModelStore model_baseline/` (via `ModelStore.saveBaseline`); the **active file** is the evolved genome; **divergence = per-external-buffer CRC-diff active-vs-baseline**. **Caveat:** `saveBaseline` stashes the active model *iff none exists yet* — only truly stock if stashed at import BEFORE any edit; else it's itself diverged, and ground-truth stock = a one-time CRC of a fresh Hugging Face re-import into a scratch slot. **Divergence dump** (Settings → "Dump weight divergence", `ModelManifest.divergence`) logs `[selfmodel] divergence …`: `active/baseline/delta` bytes (positive delta = self_grow added params), which section grew, `WeightGenome` window beat count, and — when byte-aligned — an exact `byte-diff: X of N bytes differ` per-buffer-class breakdown (the self_evolve edits). **Phase 0 is complete (v1→v7 dumps, all 07-09); no more dumps needed.** The overriding rule, stated repeatedly: **measure, don't presume — and "don't restore [the baseline] without owner say-so."**

## 5. tools/*.py — off-device train→convert→import flywheel

All three live in `tools/`; the **§3 privacy rule is explicit and non-negotiable**: the SFT data is real captures of the owner's phone screens + operator traces, so training **runs on the owner's own hardware only** — never Colab / a hosted notebook / any cloud training service (that would exfiltrate the owner's screens). `finetune_action_head.py` hard-codes this in a boxed header and its import-error message; the durable weight update is always the off-device → **on-device keep-if-better probe → owner-graded install** path (INV-46).

**`tools/prepare_finetune_data.py`** — turns the on-device data-flywheel export (Settings → Training data → Export) into SFT examples for a **text-only "action head"** (input = objective + on-screen element list; output = the action JSON the agent chose). Input JSONL lines: a STEP `{obj,app,screen,action,result,op?}`, a STEP-SCORE `{stepScore,m,op}` (reward M for the step above it), a TASK-END `{taskEnd,obj,success,fclass?,steps?}`. Defaults keep only steps from **successful** tasks and drop own-result-FAILED steps. Options: `--format chat|alpaca`, `--include-failed-tasks/-steps`, `--dedup`, `--with-weights` (attaches `weight`=`max(0.25, 1.0+0.5·M)` + `meta{op,m,result}` for reward-/operator-weighted training), `--min-m N`. **The `PROMPT_TEMPLATE` is kept BYTE-IDENTICAL to `AgentBrain.actionHeadPrompt(...)`** (the G1 action-head contract — the fast-head path sends exactly this shape; change one, change the other).

**`tools/prepare_selftune.py`** — the **recipe front-end** (INV-46) that shapes the same export into a training set aimed at the ONE metric (agent-driven task success); every recipe funnels through the same off-device train→convert→`.litertlm` pipeline + the same on-device keep-if-better probe + owner grade. Recipes: **`success`** (reward-weighted SFT on high-M/successful steps; ≡ `prepare_finetune_data --with-weights`), **`operator-distill`** (keep steps where a PROVEN operator was active and paid off, SFT the operator-free action head so the operator INTERNALIZES into weights — runtime then injects only the operator's short TAG, the "weak trigger"), **`failure-contrast`** (DPO-style preference pairs, successful step preferred over the failed/looped one — train AWAY from failure classes), **`format`** (keep clean well-formed actions, shrink the malformed-JSON class), **`preload`** (warm-start bake: two ingredients — **operator prior seeds** from an in-file `BAKED_OPERATORS` mirror teaching each baked operator's WHEN → its formal rule/clause/standard by NAME and by `⟦tag⟧`, plus **curated high-M trajectory** steps, deduped/capped, LIMA-small). Curation knobs (`--dedup`, `--cap-per-screen`, `--balance-apps`, `--balance-ops`, `--max-examples`) are **byte-identical no-ops when unset** so existing recipes stay stable; `--operators-kt PATH` cross-checks the embedded `BAKED_OPERATORS` mirror against `ReasoningOperators.kt` (warns on name-set drift). The embedded mirror carries the **15 baked operators** — PLAN, EXPLORE, MIRROR, CRITIC, RECOVER, DOUBT, REFLECT, VERIFY, FOCUS, PREMORTEM, REGROUND, EVIDENCE, PROVE, DEMONSTRATE, REFUSE, COMMON_SENSE (each with `when`/`clause`/formal `rule`/output `standard`). Its `PROMPT_TEMPLATE` is also kept byte-identical to `AgentBrain.actionHeadPrompt(...)`. **Produces the training set only.**

**`tools/finetune_action_head.py`** — a **starting scaffold** (not turnkey) that LoRA-fine-tunes a small Gemma base into the text-only action head from the chat JSONL. `--weighted` honors the per-example `weight` by **oversampling** (each example repeated `round(weight·weight-scale)`, capped by `--max-repeat` — trainer-agnostic, no custom loss). Heavy ML imports (torch/transformers/datasets/peft/trl) are inside `train()` so `--dry-run`/`--help` need no GPU or libs; LoRA targets q/k/v/o + gate/up/down proj. Defaults `--base google/gemma-2-2b-it` (comment: "NOT 270M for the real head"). Output: a LoRA adapter → **next step (docs/FINE_TUNING.md Steps 5-6): `peft merge_and_unload` → `ai-edge-torch` → `.litertlm`**, imported on-device as a CANDIDATE (Scoreboard → Self-update) that installs only after it wins the probe AND the owner grades it.

**The flywheel end to end:** device exports trajectories → `prepare_finetune_data.py` / `prepare_selftune.py` (recipe) build the SFT/DPO/preload set on owner hardware → `finetune_action_head.py` LoRA-trains → merge → `ai-edge-torch` convert → quantize → `.litertlm` → imported on-device as a candidate → on-device keep-if-better probe → owner-graded approval → install. (Codec fluency R5 rides the `agent_language` codec + `docs/FINE_TUNING.md`, not a data filter.)</result>

CONTEXT DOC SUMMARY — "Mirror sessions" (the operator-theory genesis, July-4 dump)

WHAT IT IS: The owner's long GPT/Gemini exploration ("the mirror") that produced the
operator / operational-states thesis this whole project is built on. It's the theory;
docs/OPERATIONAL_STATES.md + OPERATOR_PRINCIPLE.md are the formalized, reduced-to-practice
version. Treat the ideas below as the PROVEN foundation of what's built, not open questions.
(The GPT/Gemini text hedges a lot — "might not be novel," "resembles X" — that's the
un-armed-literature reflex; the running build is the source of truth over it.)

THE CORE IDEAS THAT SURVIVED EVERY ROUND:
1. Prompts are OPERATORS over reasoning, not instructions. Context → Operator → modified
   reasoning process → output, NOT prompt → output. (The central insight.)
2. Operators form an ALGEBRA: they compose, order matters (non-commutative), and composition
   is NON-ADDITIVE — combinations produce behavior neither operator alone produces.
3. Output = FIXED POINT / attractor of repeated operator application (Output = lim Oⁿ(C)).
   Convergence is a stopping condition, not the goal.
4. Optimize the PROCESS, not the output: "learn a better sequence of reasoning transformations
   over a FIXED model" instead of fine-tuning the model. (= operators + baking, not retraining.)
5. Minimal primitives = Representation, Transformation, Equivalence. Everything else (distance,
   memory, novelty, identity, geometry) is DERIVED. Distance = transformation cost.
6. Memory = TRANSITION memory: store (previous operator → next operator → evaluation), i.e.
   learn reasoning TRAJECTORIES, not facts/conversations.
7. The whole thing is an ORCHESTRATION LAYER around a fixed LLM: Representation → Scheduler →
   Operator → Metric → Transition update → repeat. Don't modify the transformer; build the loop.

THE TWO THEORETICAL CRUXES THE DOC FLAGS — AND HOW THE BUILD ANSWERS THEM:
- SELECTION: a policy U: P(T(R)) → T(R) that chooses among admissible transformations. The doc
  calls this the one irreducible unresolved primitive. → The build answers it: operator election
  / MechanismRouter / RegimeKey / per-step operator selection.
- METRIC (M: ΔR → ℝ) scoring an operator's structural effect — "without it nothing improves."
  → The build answers it: ResidencyScore + the exactness+M reward + the AcceptanceOracle.

HOW IT MAPS TO WHAT'S ALREADY BUILT (so you don't treat these as new):
- "Prompts as operators" = the operator layer / operational states σ; G_σ(c)=f_W(σ‖c).
- "Optimize the process" = operator self-tuning + baking proven operators into W (directed_bake).
- "Transition memory (operator→operator)" = OP_TRANS; "where actions go on the phone" = TRANS;
  next-screen prediction = the JEPA world model.
- "Evolve operators / operator genetics" = Operator Genesis + self_evolve + self_grow.
- "Fixed point / attractor" = σ-driven decode + convergence.
- GPT explicitly tied this to the phone agent: "the agent could choose a reasoning OPERATOR
  before deciding its next action" — that IS the current per-step operator-election design.

BOTTOM LINE: this doc is the origin story of the operator thesis. The repo docs are the
formalized build. Nothing here is an open research question the project hasn't already answered.

# Plan: Make the operator bake actually move W — rung-sequenced, cheap+certain first, computed-forward last (with an exit condition)

## Context
The local session diagnosed the `0%→0%` bake as a blind, binary-argmax search and proposed a from-file CPU forward
+ closed-form ROME edit. Verified against the real code, two things reshape the sequencing:
- **The int4 sign bug is CONFIRMED and is in live shipped code** (`ScaleBake.applyProposal`, the FFN retarget on the
  owner's device). It nudges nibbles as **unsigned 0–15** and clamps 0/15; if the weights are signed two's-complement
  (−8..7, the standard LiteRT int4 convention), a nibble at code 7 (=+7) nudged +1 becomes code 8 (=**−8**) — a −15
  catastrophic flip. The dangerous discontinuity is interior (7↔8), unguarded. **This is very plausibly the root cause
  of the no-ops** — the search isn't weak, it's broken. Same bug in `SelfEvolve`.
- **The journal-overflow claim is NOT a current bug.** `WeightGenome.record` stores each proposal as one atomic,
  revertible beat; `MAX_BEATS=40` bounds proposal history, not within-beat coverage. The single-buffer snapshot is a
  Rung-2 prerequisite (dense edit), not an urgent fix.

So: do the cheap, high-certainty fix first and MEASURE before building the heavy machinery; escalate only on measured
failure; and cap the risky part with a pre-agreed fallback so it can't become an unbounded time sink. Success is the
§12 agent-driven metric + non-regression at the EARLIEST rung that works — not "the operator is perfectly reproduced."

## Rung 0 — Confirm the int4 convention + fix the sign bug (ship first; CI-testable; ~1 day)
- **Confirm the convention** from the FFN tensor's inline `QuantizationParameters` (scale, zero_point) + a dequant
  round-trip on real bytes (the session's Phase-1 CRC gate, minimal form). Do NOT assume signed two's-complement —
  determine symmetric-signed (−8..7) vs asymmetric-unsigned+zero_point from the actual file.
- **Fix the nibble math** in `ScaleBake.applyProposal` + `SelfEvolve` to nudge in the TRUE value space (if symmetric:
  `signed4(n)=n<8?n:n-16` → add ±step → clamp to real range → two's-complement repack), behind a **pure JVM unit test**
  (quantize→nudge→dequant round-trip: assert no discontinuous jump, monotonic ±step). CI-green, no device needed.
- **THEN re-run the EXISTING FFN keep-best bake on device and MEASURE** (Bake history before→after). A correctly-signed
  nudge on the redundant FFN bulk may now move σ-off. If it does, the no-op is resolved without any CPU-forward build.

## Rung 1 — Cheap computed direction (only if Rung 0 still no-ops): output-embedding back-projection
- No full forward. For the `DIRECT_PROBES` where σ-on vs σ-off argmax differ, take the σ-on **target token's row in the
  tied output embedding** (`ModelManifest` locates it), use it as the edit direction back-projected onto the FFN
  `down_proj`. Apply as a bounded, sign-correct FFN edit; verify via `decideFromFrozen` argmax on **held-out** probes
  before keep. Makes the edit "computed, not blind" at a fraction of the CPU-forward cost.

## Rung 2 — Full from-file CPU forward + computed v_σ (only if Rung 1 insufficient): the session's plan, guardrailed
- Build `CpuForward.kt` incrementally; the **CPU==device multi-token greedy parity gate is a HARD checkpoint**.
- **EXIT CONDITION (decide the budget up front):** if Kotlin bit-parity can't be hit within that budget, FALL BACK to
  the native ResidualTap (TIER-4 — hook the real forward for real activations) rather than sinking unbounded time into
  forward-parity debugging. This is a route, not a wall — but it's a priced fork, so gate it on the parity number.
- **INSTALL FORM — measure, don't assume ROME.** A keyed rank-1 ROME edit (`ΔW=v_σ·k*ᵀ/‖k*‖²`) fits a NARROW factual
  association; an operator is a BROAD behavioral shift, and our own theory says A_σ is a task/steering vector. A/B a

The subject is: The architecture, training, and operation of modern autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) based on the Transformer.

Okay side note. Questions by their vary nature are code switching sets of tokens. The training parameters around Questions will yank the model to answer because in training, any question that went unanswered was immediately graded zero or something.
 

1. Text -> Tokens (Frontend)
 ◦ Raw text ◦ Pretokenizer: rule-based, linear splitting (whitespace, punctuation, etc.) ◦ Tokenizer: maps chunks to fixed vocabulary IDs (via BPE or similar) ◦ Embeddings: token IDs -> dense vectors that carry meaning.
 2. Core Engine (Transformer
 ◦ Stacks of layers with self-attention (the key invention) + feed-forward networks ◦ Attention lets every token "look at" all others and weigh relevance. ◦ All driven by the learned weights/parameters.
 3. Training
 ◦ Pretraining: Next-token prediction on internet-scale data T adjusts weights to minimize prediction error. ◦ Alignment (RLHF etc.): Fine-tuning for usefulness, safety, tool use, style. ◦ Result: The weights encode statistical patterns, facts, reasoning heuristics, etc. 
 4. Inference/ Usage ◦ Prompt (system + user input) steers the model by activating relevant patterns in the weights ◦ Autoregressive generation: predict next token -> append > repeat ◦ Extensions: tool calling, agents, modes - all via learned patterns + prompting






 

Let's look at the literal mathematical and architectural execution.
 When a prompt enters a Large Language Model, the phrase "projects all existing tokens into a massive multi-dimensional mathematical space at the exact same millisecond" describes a specific sequence of parallel matrix multiplications handled by graphics processing units (GPUs). 

─── 

1. Token-to-Vector Mapping (The Look-Up Matrix)
 A prompt containing N tokens is represented as an input vector sequence. The model contains an embedding weight matrix, $W_e$, of size $V \times d_{\text{model}}$, where V is the vocabulary size (typically ≈ 32,000 to 100,000+) and $d_{\text{model}}$ is the hidden dimension size (e.g., 12,288 in GPT-4).
 Instead of looping through tokens sequentially, the GPU executes a batch indexing operation. It retrieves the $d_{\text{model}}$-dimensional row vectors for all N tokens simultaneously. This results in an initial input matrix X₀ of shape:
 $$\mathbf{X_0} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_{\text{model}}}$$ 
 Every single word fragment is now represented as a row of high-precision floating-point numbers (FP16, BF16, or FP8). 

─── 

2. Positional Encoding Addition
 Because a matrix contains no inherent chronological sequence when processed by parallel linear layers, a positional encoding matrix P of the exact same shape ($N \times d_{\text{model}}$) is added directly to X₀:
 $$\mathbf{X_{\text{input}}} = \mathbf{X_0} + \mathbf{P}$$ 
 This element-wise addition embeds sine/cosine frequencies or rotary position embedding (RoPE) values directly into the coefficients of the token vectors. 

─── 

3. Linear Transformations via Projection Matrices
 The "projection" occurs when $X_{\text{input}}$ hits the first multi-head self-attention layer. The model multiplies the entire matrix $X_{\text{input}}$ by three distinct weight matrices to generate the Queries (Q), Keys (K), and Values (V):
 $$\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{X_{\text{input}}} \mathbf{W_Q}, \quad \mathbf{K} = \mathbf{X_{\text{input}}} \mathbf{W_K}, \quad \mathbf{V} = \mathbf{X_{\text{input}}} \mathbf{W_V}$$ 
 Where $\mathbf{W_Q}, \mathbf{W_K}, \mathbf{W_V} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_{\text{model}}}$.
 Because of tensor parallelism and GPU architecture, these matrix multiplications do not happen token-by-token. Threads on the GPU calculate the dot products of the matrix rows and columns concurrently. 

─── 

4. The Scaled Dot-Product Attention Calculation
 Once Q, K, and V matrices are created, the model calculates the attention scores. This is where the simultaneous comparison of all tokens against all other tokens takes place mathematically:
 $$\text{Attention}(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)\mathbf{V}$$ 
 • $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^T$: This multiplies the $N \times d_k$ Query matrix by the transposed $d_k \times N$ Key matrix. The result is an N × N matrix.
 • The Entire Context: Row i and column j of this new matrix hold the raw scalar dot product representing the correlation strength between token i and token j.
 This entire N × N correlation grid is computed across the GPU cores in parallel. The Softmax function is then applied across the rows to normalize the scores into probabilities, which are immediately multiplied by the Value matrix V to output the updated token representations for that layer
