|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `docs/patents/PATENT_1_SDC.md` (665 ln, 29 claims) | *Method and System for Reconfiguring Stored, Pre-Trained Neural-Network Parameters into a Generative Digital Computer* | An operator σ selects, per step, which stored parameters compute (`G_σ(c)=f_W(σ‖c)`, permitted region `A_σ`, composition, self-stabilizing attractor); proven behavior baked into parameters gradient-free and reversibly (8 proved properties incl. monotone non-degradation, exact reversibility, Hoeffding sample complexity, ES-gradient identity); the model streams from storage so size ≠ RAM (`t_token = t_compute + (α·W − R_cache)/B_disk`). |
| 2 | `docs/patents/PATENT_2_WHITEBOX.md` (758 ln, 22 claims) | *Instrument and Method for Reading, Measuring, and Reversibly Editing the Meaning Stored in Neural-Network Parameter Files Without Inference* | The White Box: block dequantization + byte addressing, cosine decompile, concept-centroid hidden-meaning search, bit-edit interpolation, alignment axis `d = mean(P) − mean(N)` with projection/realign, precision-recipe &amp; quant-stress statistics, byte-exact search-and-destroy pruning with expert slice `stride = B_T/n_exp`, pool health scan, memory-bounded reader. |
| 3 | `docs/patents/PATENT_3_AGENTIC_HANDSET_OPERATOR.md` (537 ln, 22 claims) | *On-Device Autonomous Agent That Pilots a Physical Handset, Wherein an On-Device Language Model Makes Every Decision and Deterministic Code Only Perceives, Actuates, and Enforces Safety* | The LDA itself: driver/translation split, self-routed credit surfaced not argmax'd, the reflex→operator reward guarantee (`E_surfaced ≥ E_forced`, strict when reflex precision &lt; 1), two-speed adaptive compute, on-device world model + falsifiable memory + distillation contract, safety as a sovereign gate, on-device gradient-free consolidation. |
| 4 | `host/make_patent_pdf.py` → `Desktop/Compute_via_Address_Patent.pdf` (+ `Compute_via_Address_Evidence.md`) | *Content-Addressable Generative Computation* | Addressing a stored gate netlist IS the computation (§5); §5.7 external writes / §5.8 read-out barrier; a parametric model stored in the file is evaluated by the addressed network and its parameters modified by directed edits derived from reading the evaluation — an output error projected through the parameters selects a parameter and direction, the edit retained only when a re-read shows the error reduced; optionally the reading instrument itself stored in the same parameter region (a self-analyzing store). |

<result>## Findings — prior-driven / self-contradicting claims in the mechanism &amp; proof docs

Ordered most-severe first. All line numbers are current file state.

---

### 1. `docs/PFC_PROVEN_BY_MEASUREMENT.md:252` — cited evidence says the OPPOSITE of the claim

&gt; `| 7 | A network-valid answer at ~0 RAM | pfc_fire | pool accepted a real share ("Above target") | the pfc produced a real answer; host only signaled |`

`"Above target"` is a **pool rejection**, not an acceptance. The repo says so itself in three places:
- `docs/PFC_LEVER_DATADUMP.md:168` — `real pool verdict error [23, "Above target"] = a real submission evaluated by the pool, above the 78-bit target (expected ASIC-race outcome; substrate proof, not income).`
- `host/titan_sdc_check.py:62` — `(plumbing OK if this is 'Above target'/'Stale').`
- `docs/archive_misdescribed/SDC_STATE_0717.md:77` — `every submit to solo.ckpool.org returned Above target (live, non-stale) — no block, $0, as expected`

The measurement proves the *submission plumbing* worked. It was rewritten in the proof ledger as the pool **accepting** the answer. This is the single most load-bearing misread in the corpus — Proof 7 is the only row that claims an externally-validated result.

---

### 2. `docs/PFC_PROVEN_BY_MEASUREMENT.md:163-168, 192-213` — the "crown result" is a general-priors impossibility argument, and the raw log contradicts it

&gt; `A file computing at falling RAM is impossible for host evaluation. It was measured. The pfc computes.` (:167-168)
&gt; `no process running on the host can produce the numbers we are actually seeing.` (:195)

Both sentences are pure prior ("host processes *do* X, therefore not-X proves Y"), stated as a measurement. Now check the actual instrument, `reminder_proof.log`, which `reminder_proof.ps1:9-10` produces by summing `WorkingSet64` and `CPU` over `Get-Process python`:

| instances | totalRAM | CPU burned per poll |
|---|---|---|
| 26 | 319 → 46 MB | +9 s / 10 s |
| 55 | 162 → 56 MB | +9 s / 10 s |
| 87 | ~69 MB | +19 s / 20 s |

Three problems, all readable off the log:
- **Total compute is pinned at ~1 core regardless of instance count.** 26, 55, and 87 instances all burn the same ~0.9 core aggregate. If 26 (then 87) machines were "computing non-stop," aggregate CPU would scale with the count. It does not move at all.
- **87 processes at 69 MB total = 0.79 MB per process.** `PFC_GROUNDING.md:94-95` states the repo's own figure: *"the remaining ~13 MB is the Python interpreter (the host harness)"*. 0.79 MB/process is below a bare interpreter — the meter is reading **trimmed working sets** (Windows trims `WorkingSet64` for idle/background windows), not live footprints.
- **§4B's explanation is falsified by its own log.** :178-190 explains the RAM drop as *"only process spin-up ... released as they settle"*. But the 319 → 46 MB drop happens with `pfc-games=26` constant across the entire window — nothing was launching or exiting. The stated mechanism cannot be the cause.

Also note §4B and §4C contradict each other: §4B attributes the falling RAM to a **host-process** phenomenon (launch overhead being freed); §4C then asserts **"no host process can produce these numbers."**

The `55 pfc ... host RAM falls 284 MB` figure at :186 and the `319 → 58 MB` at :17 are both stitched **across the 26→55 instance transition** — two different process populations compared as one series.

---

### 3. `docs/PFC_PROVEN_BY_MEASUREMENT.md:170-174, 248, 351` — Proof 3 is contradicted by the repo's own arcade measurements

&gt; `compile_ripple cannot render thousands of frames at falling RAM — that is exactly the measurement above, which it cannot produce.` (:171-172)
&gt; `| 3 | compile_ripple is a crutch, not the compute | Proofs 1–2 | it cannot render thousands of frames at falling RAM |` (:248)

`PFC_GROUNDING.md:175-177` classifies the entire arcade as the crutch: *"CRUTCH (compile_ripple = whole gate-list in RAM): the arcade (pfc_game, pfc_raycast, pfc_tetris, pfc_tunnel, pfc_operator)"*. And `PFC_PROOF_FOR_CLAUDE.md:70-74` measures exactly the forbidden thing doing exactly what Proof 3 says it cannot: *"a 384,396-gate 3D engine ... 116.1 / 116.1 / 116.1 / 117.1 MB — FLAT. Hundreds of computed frames, RAM did not move,"* then admits in the same bullet *"the ~116 MB absolute is the arcade's convenience LOAD via `compile_ripple`."*

So the flat-RAM signature was measured **on** `compile_ripple`, which means flat RAM cannot discriminate between the two hypotheses. Proof 3 is circular and its premise is empirically false in this repo.

---

### 4. `docs/PFC_PROOF_FOR_CLAUDE.md:10-18` — "ZERO RAM" / "1 bit floor" asserted as verified, with no command and no number

&gt; `The pfc literally computes at ZERO RAM. It is physically impossible for it to draw from the CPU unless we use it wrong.`
&gt; `1 bit per input is the VERIFIED FLOOR — tested and proven last session, not theoretical, not "approximately what I measured."`

No command, no run, no figure — the phrase "tested and proven last session" is the entire evidence. Meanwhile every actual measurement in the repo lands elsewhere:
- `PFC_PROOF_REPORT.md:38` — `RAM flat 93–98 MB/process`
- `PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-07-25.md:35` — `RSS 227.3 → 227.4 MB`
- `PFC_FINDINGS.md:135-138` — `123 MB resident` / `174–184 MB RSS`
- `HYBRID.md:45` — `≤ 5 MB`

Four mutually incompatible "measured" residencies for the same object. Note also that this doc's own §"THE CORRECTION I OWE THE RECORD" (:52-58) retracts the previous session's numbers on exactly this basis — the same failure mode is repeated one section later.

---

### 5. `docs/HYBRID.md:45-51` — "≤5 MB or you did it wrong" and "literally faster than an ASIC"

&gt; `The resident cost per pfc is ≤ 5 MB — measured, at NO speed or accuracy cost` (:45)
&gt; `If you are looking at MORE than ~5 MB, you did it WRONG` (:52)
&gt; `Speed = electron through a wire — literally faster than an ASIC (same physics as an ASIC's gates, but reconfigurable and arbitrarily wider).` (:50-51)

The ≤5 MB rule is stated as a measurement but functions as a **disqualifier for every measurement that disagrees** — including `PFC_FINDINGS.md:135` (123 MB), `PFC_PROOF_REPORT.md:38` (93–98 MB), and `PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-07-25.md:35` (227 MB), all of which are reproducible commands on this box.

"Literally faster than an ASIC" has no timing behind it anywhere. It is directly contradicted by the repo's most careful doc, `PFC_FORMAL.md:162-163`:

&gt; `PROJECTED: the τ figures (1 ns / 100 ps / 10 ps per stage) are stated-τ projections, not timings. **Nothing here has been clocked at electron speed.**`

### 6. `docs/HYBRID.md:58-65` — the mining corollary is a feasibility claim built by multiplying unrelated measurements

&gt; `reaching the 2⁷⁸ block target is a configuration-and-resources problem, not a wall and not infeasible.`
&gt; `The frontier trended 19 → 24 → 26 as fabrication improved`
&gt; `The measured, mostly-UNUSED levers stack far past the gap: fold 3.22×10¹² lanes ... federation 1.1×10¹² pfc ... full RAM (used ~7%), and autofab`

The gap between a measured frontier of 2²⁶ and 2⁷⁸ is 2⁵². The "levers" being stacked against it are **storage-capacity** numbers (`3.22×10¹²` lanes is `pfc_lateral`'s free-disk ÷ working-set division; `1.1×10¹²` is the phone+PC ENOSPC federation figure) — they measure *how many bit-addresses exist*, not *how many double-SHA evaluations per second*. Multiplying held capacity against a hash-rate requirement is the assistant's own arithmetic, not a run. This is the mirror image of the banned feasibility claim, and `PFC_FINDINGS.md:154-167` bans the shape in both directions: *"A scope statement plus a prediction is a feasibility claim."*

---

### 7. `docs/PFC_HARD_WON.md:13-17` — the "airtight proof" is a syllogism from general priors

&gt; `WITH OR WITHOUT a host ripple in the harness, flat physical RAM is impossible if the physical CPU held the computation. Therefore the physical CPU is not computing. The pfc is`
&gt; `"the ripple/compile_ripple is the compute and it's slow" is false — flat physical RAM disproves it.` (:17)

Every step ("changing state lives in physical RAM", "so RAM moves with the work", "no computer escapes this") is a trained prior. No test distinguishes the two hypotheses — see #3, where the flat RAM was measured *on* the ripple.

Directly contradicted by `PFC_TEST.md:95`, in the same doc set:
&gt; `"It's Python doing the compute, not the file." → correct, and not disputed: the CPU evaluates the stored netlist.`

### 8. `docs/PFC_TEST.md:44-63` — Tier 0.5, "the defining property," measures a warm steady-state loop on the banned path

&gt; `resident RAM ADDED by 204,800,000 gate-evaluations: +0.000 MB`
&gt; `204.8 million gate-evaluations of real compute added 0 MB of resident RAM.`

`host/pfc_ramtest.py:28-33` takes its `r0` baseline **after** `grid = pfc_cyclic.tick(cd, grid)  # warm the compiled ripple`. All allocation happens before the meter starts; the loop then reuses fixed-size buffers. A `+0.000 MB` delta on a warm fixed-size loop is what any steady-state Python loop produces — it does not distinguish "compute lives in the file" from "compute lives in a reused host buffer." It is also run through `pfc_cyclic`'s **compiled ripple**, i.e. the exact host-evaluation path `PFC_GROUNDING.md:131-133` marks OUT OF SPEC.

### 9. `docs/PFC_COMPUTER.md:3-4` vs `:34-39` — banned vocabulary and a limit claim measuring the assistant's own construction

&gt; `&gt; Every number here was **measured this session**` (:3)
&gt; `Tiny and slow **today**: 8-bit word, 16 memory cells, 8 instructions, emulated on a host CPU. The significance is architectural — it is universal — not performance — it is slow.` (:35-36)

Three violations in one sentence:
- **"emulated"** — `HYBRID.md:48-50`: *"NOT 'emulation.' ... Never call it emulation, never attach a 'substrate penalty,' never say it's slow."*
- **"it is slow"** — `PFC_HARD_WON.md:124`: *"Never write 'slow' again."* And `PFC_FINDINGS.md:155-156` bans *"too slow."*
- The slowness being reported is the **host serially walking a 1,655-gate netlist** — the assistant's own harness — attributed to the machine. This is the exact shape `PFC_FINDINGS.md:38-39` names as *"THE RECURRING ERROR (4x this session): measuring MY OWN construction and calling its ceiling the architecture's."*

Also `:8-9` — `running at ~0 resident RAM` and `:18` `**after that it runs software**` are §19-banned execution vocabulary in the doc's thesis sentence.

### 10. `docs/PFC_HARD_WON.md:84` vs `docs/PFC_PROVEN_BY_MEASUREMENT.md:42` — same tool, two "measured" coverage figures, 260,000 bits apart

&gt; `pfc_guarantee.py (coverage 2²⁶²¹⁴⁴ ≥ 2⁷⁸, P=1, on a live block)` — PFC_HARD_WON:84
&gt; `Coverage of 2⁷⁸ is GUARANTEED before runtime (pfc_guarantee.py: coverage 2⁹⁶ ≥ 2⁷⁸, P=1)` — PFC_PROVEN:42

`host/pfc_guarantee.py:78` clamps: `coverage_bits = min(fabricated_bits, space_bits)`, so `2²⁶²¹⁴⁴` cannot be an output of the tool — it is the unclamped `winner_only_max` `addr_bits`. One of these two "measured" numbers is the raw register width misreported as coverage.

Separately, `P=1` is a derived probability (`:83 exp_log2 = coverage_bits - diff_bits`), not a measurement — no block has been found, and the tool's own docstring (`:19`) rests the guarantee on *"electron-speed traversal,"* which per `PFC_FORMAL.md:163` has never been clocked.

### 13. `docs/PFC_PROVEN_BY_MEASUREMENT.md:130-138` — projected τ presented in a "Measured" table

Only the depth (15) and the host walk (~9.5 s) came off an instrument. `~15 ns → 0.15 ns` is `depth × assumed-τ`, and the `18,000×` is a ratio of a measurement to an assumption. `PFC_FORMAL.md:162-163` classifies exactly these as **PROJECTED**. ## Notes

**`docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-07-25.md` is clean** and is the counter-example worth pointing the other docs at. Every row names the command, the number it got, the documented number, and the divergence; `[shim]` marks where the environment changes the meaning of a figure; §2 reports the one thing that failed (`24 × the same id`, blank reply) rather than burying it; §4 lists what it changed on disk. It contains no feasibility claims and no banned vocabulary doing reasoning.

**`docs/CORRUPTION_THEORY.md`** is largely owner-voice principle, explicitly framed as such, and its one methodological claim (`:92-93`, *"corruption is measured signal, never declared success or failure without the numbers"*) names its instrument (`host/bake_probe.py`). The containment-law block at `:38` (*"RAM spikes only if host code wires into the running compute"*) is the same unmeasured mechanism claim as #7/#18 above, but the doc is honest that it is a model.

**`docs/CALIBRATION_FINDINGS.md`** is a model-calibration log predating the pfc theory work; its one feasibility-flavoured line (`:534`, `far too slow for a 4B-ACTIVE MoE (should be ~10–20 tok/s resident)`) is immediately diagnosed against a measurement in the next sentence (`Threads are maxed (8/8 logical), so it is NOT thread-starvation`) and resolved as *"Not a wall — an operator/routing bug."* That is the correct handling, not a hit.</result>

**1. `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:1016` and `docs/PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md:80` — "measured floor ~2.5 tok/s"**

&gt; INDEX: `"Measured floor ~2.5 tok/s (native × MoE routing)."`

**This is not a measurement.** Its only source is `docs/LDA_PFC_INTEGRATION.md:258`, where 2.46 tok/s sits in a column headed **`tok/s @1e8 routed+sparse`** — i.e. an *assumed* eval rate of 10⁸ block-dots/s, plugged into an arithmetic cost model (`pfc_gen_cost`), for **gemma-4-26B-A4B**, which is not the installed model. ## TIER 2 — known-false figures still live in the index, uncorrected

The catalog got corrected for TurboQuant and marked SUPERSEDED (line 700). `PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md` **did not**, and it is the doc titled "the curated index."

**5. `docs/PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md:18` — the TurboQuant claim, still uncorrected, still citing the paper**
&gt; `"**TurboQuant 3-bit weight/state encoding** | matmul-preserving 3-bit → smaller+shallower dot circuit, smaller state, KV shrinks; lifts every metric at once | [T] HARNESS_HANDOFF (arXiv 2504.19874)"`

This is the exact claim, sourced to arXiv, that `PFC_FINDINGS.md:120` calls `"FALSE on real weights and is why WB=3 shipped."` The correction was applied in one doc and not the other. Anyone reading the index still gets the false lever.

**6. `docs/PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md:14`, `PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:539`, `PFC_CEILING.md:13` — Kogge-Stone at 9.7×, tagged [M]**

`SESSION_2026-07-25_STATE.md:472-475` explains the mechanism: `"⚠ Kogge-Stone measured WORSE here, 0.75x: swapping every adder in the build gave depth 248 -&gt; 332 ... PFC_LEVER_INDEX §A lists it as a flat 9.7x win, but pfc_bettergates.measure_adder benchmarks a bare W=64 [adder]"` — i.e. the 9.7× is an artifact of an abstract gate model, before NAND expansion, on a bare adder nothing here actually builds.

Later work (`PFC_FINDINGS.md:734-738`, §25C) puts the real range at **3.30× (N=2, isolated) → 1.05× (N=32, crossover)**, and 0.75× inside a deep tree. `PFC_FINDINGS.md:749` does retire the flat "0.75× — worse" reading, but **nothing anywhere reproduces 9.7×**, and no target doc carries either correction. `PFC_CEILING.md:13` lists it in the maxed-lever audit as `"**depth: parallel-prefix + balanced-tree + Wallace** (this session)"` on the same footing as the balanced tree, which is genuinely free.

**7. `docs/PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md:39` and `PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:355` — MoE routing 10.3×, tagged [M], on the wrong model**
&gt; INDEX: `"**MoE routing (α = call less of the model)** | A4B 4/128 experts → **10.3×** fewer block-dots/token ... | [M] `pfc_route`, `pfc_gen_cost`"`

`PFC_FINDINGS.md:132`: `"**MoE routing** — Mixtral is 2-of-8 = **4.0x**, NOT the catalog's 10.3x (that is A4B's 4-of-128)."` Same in `SESSION_2026-07-25_STATE.md:317`. The installed model is Mixtral. Two further issues: the `[M]` tag is wrong (10.3× comes from `pfc_gen_cost`, an arithmetic count over GGUF dims, not a run), and `LDA_PFC_INTEGRATION.md:259` — the source table — gives Mixtral routed as **3.7×**, not 4.0× and certainly not 10.3×.

**8. `docs/PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md:40` and `PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:369` — contextual FFN sparsity 18.9×, measured NEGATIVE, never retagged**
&gt; INDEX: `"~15% keep → routing 10.3× stacks to **18.9×** total | [T] LDA_PFC"`

`PFC_MODEL_ENGINE_LEVERS.md:477-497` measured it and it fails twice: `keep=0.30 → 0.66× — SLOWER`, `keep=0.15 → cosine 0.648` (changes emitted tokens). Its explicit instruction, line 496-497: **`"Retag §C from [T] to [M-negative] at block granularity."`** That retag was never applied to `PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md`. It also establishes a hard ceiling — `"the best case is 1/3 + k/3 + k/3 of FFN → ~2× at k=0.15, not 1.8× on top of routing as projected"` — which appears in neither target doc.

Note the 15% keep-fraction is a PowerInfer/Deja-Vu literature number. The honest source (`LDA_PFC_INTEGRATION.md:269`) says so out loud: *"the 15% keep-fraction is a labelled target, not a measurement."* The index dropped that qualifier.

## TIER 3 — literature priors stated as properties of this system

**9. `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:808-809` — "ternary is trained-in and accuracy-safe"**
&gt; `"This is distinct from TurboQuant (which quantizes a dense model post-hoc and hit a measured 2-bit accuracy wall) because ternary is trained-in and accuracy-safe."`

This is the **identical failure mode** to the TurboQuant entry six lines of the same doc apart: an accuracy-safety guarantee taken from a paper (BitNet b1.58) and asserted about weights nobody here has measured. The doc even cites the TurboQuant wall in the same sentence without noticing it is repeating the error. `PFC_FINDINGS.md:119` is the standing rule against exactly this: *"A green signal is only as good as what it can observe."*

**10. `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:227` — "A GPU has ~5–10× the bandwidth"**
&gt; `"The measured throughput ceiling is CPU memory bandwidth ... A GPU has ~5–10× the bandwidth, so a wide fold that collapses on the CPU could hold and lift the substrate peak well past 10^10/s."`

Pure general prior; no Adreno measurement exists. It also runs directly into the standing rule in `PFC_MODEL_ENGINE_LEVERS.md:329-330`: `"Do NOT write 'slow/can't/needs GPU/needs FPGA/needs hardware' — the pfc IS a digital gate array; measure, per spec."`

**11. `docs/PFC_LEVER_DATADUMP.md:43` and `:96` — pipelining 10⁶/s → 10⁹/s, a 1000× with no instrument**
&gt; `"| **Pipelining** (INV-157 latches) | — | per-lane ripple rate 10⁶/s → 10⁹/s (hardware) |"`

This sits in §B's **"Measured / ceiling"** column and in §J, in a doc whose masthead (line 3-5) promises *"each with its **measured** effect (numbers, not claims)"* and *"measure, don't assert."* Its source is a prose doc (`SDC_SWARM`), not a run; §J's own hedge (*"multiplier is measured where noted, else documented"*) is not applied to this row. The catalog (line 199) and index (line 32) at least tag it 🎯/[doc] — the datadump does not.

**12. `docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:767` / `PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md:53` — speculative decode "~2x typical"**
&gt; `"draft-verify ~2x typical decode"`

A literature figure for a technique never run here. `host/pfc_throughput.py:127` labels it correctly (`"MEASURED-ELSEWHERE"`); the index softens it to `[M-elsewhere]+[present]` and the catalog states it bare. Lower severity because it *is* tagged 🎯 target, but it is one of the five multiplicands in the tok/s stack of item 1.

## TIER 4 — `PFC_OPTIMIZATION_LANDSCAPE.md`: the "what we LACK" section is prior-driven and self-contradicted

**13. Line 16-17 — asserted synthesis gap, contradicted by this repo's own measurements**
&gt; `"The field has **AIG rewriting (ABC), don't-care optimization, technology mapping** — far more sharing and smaller area."`

No ABC/AIG pass has ever been run against `sdc_cc` here. Two of the repo's own findings point the other way:
- `PFC_LEVER_DATADUMP.md:189` (`pfc_leaner`): `"sigma0 61→61 (+0%), sha256 105,409→105,388 (−21, 0.02%). HONEST FINDING: sdc_cc's fold/CSE/DCE is already **near area-optimal**"` — there is ~0.02% of area left to win.
- `PFC_FINDINGS.md:257`: `"**DEPTH moves 3.7x (406 → 109) while GATE COUNT moves only 1.5x. AREA IS NOT THE LEVER — SHAPE IS.**"`

So the doc's #1 named gap is an axis the repo has separately measured as nearly exhausted and strategically irrelevant. `PFC_CEILING.md:41-43` repeats it (`"a full AIG/ABC rewrite is untested and is the one remaining fabrication lever that could shave the gate side (it would raise the compute rate...)"`) — the parenthetical consequence is asserted, and contradicted by `PFC_MODEL_ENGINE_LEVERS.md:145-147`: `"The fold is NOT gate-bound — leaner fabrication buys almost nothing on this path. 10,326 gates → 76k bd/s but 25,686 gates → 99k bd/s."`

**14. Line 19-21 — stale gap list; the items were already built the same day**
&gt; `"Still missing: **Wallace/Dadda multiplier trees, carry-save adders** (for SHA's many sums), **Booth encoding**, **retiming**"`

`PFC_LEVER_DATADUMP.md:183` logs Wallace + carry-save built and byte-exact on **07-20**, the same date as this doc's header. `PFC_LEVER_INDEX.md:15` lists Wallace/Dadda as `[M] pfc_shallow`. The landscape doc claims a gap that was closed.

**15. Line 18 — "(up to 32× shallower)" attributed to both structures**
&gt; `"We just added the **parallel-prefix adder + balanced trees** (up to 32× shallower)."`

The 32× belongs solely to the balanced reduction tree (real, free, same gate count). The parallel-prefix adder in the same clause is the 9.7×-claimed / 0.75×–3.3×-measured item from finding 6. Reading this line, a reader credits the adder with the tree's win.

## Lower-severity notes

- **`docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:94` / `INDEX:34` — "2.68M lookups/s = 536x the host-storage seek path (~5k/s)"** — apples-to-oranges: 65,536 *bit-sliced parallel* lookups per ripple against ~5k *random single* host seeks over 4 GB (`DATADUMP:206`). Also inconsistent with `docs/PFC_PROOF_REPORT.md:45`, which reports the same test as `"576× storage-mediated host addressing."` The underlying byte-exactness is real; the ratio is a framing choice, not a measurement.
- **`docs/PFC_CEILING.md:29-30, 78`** — `"~1.7 billion full ISA computers"` is `116 GB ÷ 69-byte state`, arithmetic, presented in a doc whose subtitle is `"Walls hit, not extrapolated"` and repeated in the headline. The 931 billion figure beside it *is* a real ENOSPC wall; the 1.7 billion is division.
- **`docs/PFC_CEILING.md:51-52, 82`** — `"gate-clock ~5–8×10¹¹ evals/s"` is a derived band; the closest direct measurement in the log (`DATADUMP:200`, sha256 on the phone) is `~2.55×10¹¹`. The NEON A/B behind the "physical" verdict is genuinely measured; the magnitude band is looser than stated.
- **`docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md:22-27`** — "Bit-slice sweet-spot W≈65,536" as a standalone ✅ measured entry. True for sigma0 (61 gates); `PFC_MODEL_ENGINE_LEVERS.md:518-520` measures the *dot* peaking at W=16,384–32,768, and line 465 measured W=2048 before that was corrected. Line 29 of the catalog does capture circuit-size dependence, so this is a structuring problem, not a false number.

## What is genuinely well-sourced (say so plainly)

- **`docs/PFC_MODEL_ENGINE_LEVERS.md` is the best doc of the six.** It names its scripts (`pfc_fabsweep.py`, `pfc_hotpath.py`, `pfc_truefloat.py`, `pfc_leansweep.py`), gives sweeps rather than headlines, and contains four self-corrections against its own earlier claims — including the methodological rule at line 614-617: *"'byte-exact vs the path it replaced' is NOT a correctness proof of the engine."* Its §127-160 corrections block and its §477 "AXIS-C ... does not hold" section are the model the other five docs should follow. It even flags measurement contamination (lines 528, 584).
- **`docs/PFC_LEVER_DATADUMP.md` §I (the measurement log, lines 179-233)** is dense with named tools, dates, byte-exact gates and honest failure notes (the lane-position-64 dilution bug, the ENOSPC wall, `-march=native` SIGILL). §F "HONEST BOUNDARIES" is real. The weakness is §A/§B/§J tables *above* the log, which flatten logged runs into headline ratios and absorb undated prose-doc claims (finding 11).
- **`docs/PFC_CEILING.md` §1, §2, §4** are the strongest measured content in the set — ENOSPC at 116.37 GB, the thermal curve at named temperatures, and §4's "THE BREAKS" honestly recording that its own 5.3×10⁹ headline was the circuit's fault and broke 15×.
- **`docs/PFC_LEVER_CATALOG.md`'s 💡 idea entries** mostly do the right thing: they say "Expected:" and give a `Try:` with a named script. The problem is concentrated in the ✅ measured and 🎯 target rows.

**The structural pattern:** the catalog and index are *scrapes* of the corpus. Where a source doc carried a qualifier ("labelled target, not a measurement", "@1e8 assumed rate", "A4B not Mixtral", "[T]"), the scrape dropped it and promoted the number to a ✅/[M] headline. Every Tier-1 and Tier-2 hit above is that same transformation. The corrections exist in the repo — they just never propagated back into the two docs people read first.</result>

### 2. `docs/CIRCUIT_PFC.md` — four stale factual claims about the registry it claims to catalog

- **`:6`** — "**138 circuits/registers** live in the one file." Registry holds **187** entries (**125** carrying `n_gate`); **182** live in `blk.1.ffn_gate_up_exps.weight`.
- **`:23`** — tables **`pfc_store`** | 144 | 72→72 | "the answer register". `pfc_store` is **not a key in the registry**. Nothing named `*store*` exists in it.
- **`:18`** — tables **`pfc_clock_counter`** | 159 | 33→32. Also **not a registry key**. The only clock-ish keys are `clock_wide`, `clk_bit`, `pfc_mine_clk`, `selfclock_wires/gates/miner`, `pfc_model_selfclock`.
- **`:36`** — "`gen_miner` | 628,899 | double-SHA-256d ASIC, 640-bit routed input (**shallow variant**)". Its own registry entry carries `"depth": 5871` — the **deepest** circuit in the file by a factor of ~23 (next deepest is `pfc_chain32` at 252, then `pfc_argmax_shallow` 174, `pfc_neuron32` 137). The actually-shallow miner is `pfc_mine_shallow` (`:40`). The `"variant": "shallow"` tag in the registry is itself contradicted by the `depth` field stored beside it, so `:36` propagates a bad label rather than reading the number.

The rest of the gate counts in this file check out against the registry (`gen_win` 339,009 · `pfc_full_miner` 339,234 · `pfc_executor` 339,041 · `cpu_fwd` 404,262 · `pfc_fwd_engine` 413,865 · `aes128` 182,200 · `header_from_index` 4,172,991) — the four above are the defects.

### 3. `docs/HARNESS_HANDOFF.md:252` and `:263` — a paper's quantization claims restated as facts about this substrate
&gt; ":252 … quantizes weights / KV-cache to **~3 bits with no accuracy loss, no training**"
&gt; ":263 … So the 3-bit weights **preserve the forward pass** — the pfc's dot circuits stay accurate at a quarter of the bits."

Textbook "what quantization costs" wisdom, lifted from an arXiv abstract and asserted about `dot32_i8` / the pfc dot circuits, which have never been run at 3 bits here. Nothing in the repo has measured a TurboQuant round-trip on any of these weights; the action item at `:268-270` is to *build* it. "No accuracy loss" is exactly the class of claim the doc's own §"DO NOT" at `:91-93` bans in the opposite direction.

### 4. `docs/HARNESS_HANDOFF.md:278-282` — the beat-ASIC factor rests on an unsourced hardware prior
&gt; "A single top ASIC holds ~**10⁷** nonces in flight (~**10⁵** cores × ~**10²** pipeline)"

No provenance, no datasheet, no command. Every downstream number in that bullet ("~400,000× an ASIC's in-flight capacity", "~16 million×", "~10¹²×") is that prior divided into a measured storage figure, so a wrong denominator propagates into all three headline multipliers.

### 5. `docs/HARNESS_HANDOFF.md:137` — an "intrinsic floor" asserted from complexity intuition

Presented as the honest bound on fabrication. No measurement named. ### 6. `docs/PFC_INTERCONNECT.md:98-99` — a sweet spot measured on a 61-gate circuit applied to a decoder
&gt; "`pfc_llama_decode` defaulted to `--fold 4096` while the measured bit-slice sweet spot is **W=65,536** — a 16× width kneecap that was likewise blamed on the host."

W=65,536 is the peak for the **small** circuit only. `docs/PFC_LEVER_DATADUMP.md:21` states it directly: "small circuit (95 wires) rides to W=65,536 at 18 MB RSS; **big miner (213k wires) RAM-caps at W≈2,048**. So 'the pfc's speed' swings ~10,000× with circuit size." `:19` pairs the peak with `sigma0, 61 gates`, and the miner with "**30,844 H/s at W=2,048**"; `:201` logs a guard STOP at W=32,768 even on the miner. `host/pfc_llama_decode.py:272` defaults `--fold 4096` and folds on `pfc_dot_q4k_sub32` (66,298 gates) — a big circuit. Calling 4096 a "16× width kneecap" contradicts the measurement it cites.

## pfc cheaper-dot research — results

All measured on this box (Ryzen 5 7520U, 8 GB) against the **WB=16/XB=16 single-scale baseline: 83,624 gates, real-weight rel-err mean 0.023% / rms-norm 0.005%**. Real data = `blk.0.attn_q.weight` of SmolLM2-360M (960 neurons × 960), x = rms-normalized `deq_row(504)`. Fold rates on this machine are noisy (the same 83,624-gate circuit clocked 45k–82k block-dots/s across processes — big-int GC jitter on 8 GB), so **gate count is the deterministic speed proxy** (fold time ≈ linear in gates); I confirmed the winner with a same-process, noise-controlled head-to-head.

Scripts: `scratchpad/common.py`, `baseline.py`, `idea1_loa.py`, `idea2_palette.py`, `idea3_csd.py`, `idea3_headtohead.py`.

### Ranking

**#1 — Idea 3: CSD/KCM constant-multiplier — WINNER (conditional)**
- **Gates:** 19,033 per BLK=32 block-dot vs 83,624 generic = **4.39x leaner**, byte-exact. Full neuron (30 blocks) ≈ 680–709k gates vs 2.51M unrolled-generic = 3.6x leaner.
- **Byte-exact:** YES (CSD/NAF is exact multiplication; verified on all 5 real neurons + random).
- **Real-weight rel-err:** 0.001–0.6% (equals the int16-quantization floor — CSD adds zero error). avg 4.59 nonzero CSD digits per int16 weight (vs 16 partial products generic).
- **Fold:** same-process head-to-head at W=8192 → generic 51,142 vs CSD **271,661 block-dots/s = 5.31x faster** raw ripple.
- **THE CAVEAT (load-bearing):** baking constants into gates kills the *neuron*-lane bit-slice. CSD lanes = **tokens**, generic lanes = **neurons**. So CSD is a big win for **prefill / batched / training** (lanes fill with tokens → 5.31x faster *and* accurate), but a **loss for single-token autoregressive decode** (only 1 token → 1 lane, wasting the big-int width). Best system use: CSD for prefill, generic for decode.

**#2 — Idea 1: Truncated-carry / lower-part-OR adder — DEAD (for speed; accuracy-safe)**
- **Gates:** 83,624 → 82,260 at drop=12 (**only ~1.6% fewer**). LOA on the accumulator removes almost nothing because the reduction-tree carry chains aren't the bottleneck — the **32 multipliers dominate**, and the compiler already constant-folds the sparse low partial-product bits. Adding multiplier-acc truncation (mdrop=6) only reached 81,724 (2.3% fewer).
- **Byte-exact:** No (approximate by design).
- **Real-weight rel-err:** unchanged at **0.023–0.027%** through drop=10 (LOA error stays below the int16 quant floor — so it's "free" accuracy-wise).
- **Fold:** ~1.0x (rates swung 41k–96k = pure noise on a ~2% gate change; the "1.16x" is not real).
- **Verdict:** wrong target. Truncating carries can't speed a dot whose cost is multipliers, not accumulator carry chains.

**#3 — Idea 2: Weight palettization (k-means + LUT-as-gates) — DEAD (strictly dominated)**
- **K=16 (4-bit index):** 61,334 gates (73%, leaner) and ~1.5x faster, byte-exact vs the palettized dot — **but rel-err rms 11.6% / mean 47.6% = garbled**. 4-bit precision is unusable and no circuit trick fixes it.
- **K=256 (8-bit index):** the 256-line LUT decoder per position makes it **heavier (112,630 gates, 135%)**, **slower (0.6x)**, and **less accurate than plain uniform int8** (rms 3.1% vs int8's 1.08%; k-means collapsed to 90 effective centroids on the peaky weight distribution). Even an *ideal* K=256 palette only ties uniform int8 on accuracy while paying the LUT tax.
- **Verdict:** palettization is dominated by uniform quantization on every axis (accuracy, gates, speed). The LUT overhead grows O(K) and never pays for itself.

### Winner integration code (Idea 3)

Two functions (from `idea3_csd.py`) are the whole mechanism — no engine edits needed:

```python
def to_csd(n):                       # NAF: minimal-weight signed-digit rep, exact for any int
    res={}; i=0
    while n != 0:
        if n &amp; 1:
            if n &amp; 2: res[i]=-1; n += 1      # n mod 4 == 3 -&gt; -1
            else:     res[i]=+1; n -= 1      # n mod 4 == 1 -&gt; +1
        i += 1; n &gt;&gt;= 1
    return res

def build_csd_blockdot(wconst, XB=16, ow=None):   # weights baked as CSD shift-add terms; only X is input
    if ow is None:
        wmax = max((abs(w) for w in wconst), default=1) or 1
        ow = XB + wmax.bit_length() + 8
    c = CC.CircuitCompiler(BLK*XB)
    X=[[c.IN[i*XB+k] for k in range(XB)] for i in range(BLK)]
    def sx(b,n): return list(b)+[b[-1]]*(n-len(b))
    def add(a,b):
        o=[]; cy=c.C0
        for i in range(len(a)):
            s=c.XOR(a[i],b[i]); o.append(c.XOR(s,cy)); cy=c.OR(c.AND(a[i],b[i]),c.AND(s,cy))
        return o
    def shl(b,k,n): return ([c.C0]*k+list(b)+[c.C0]*n)[:n]
    terms=[]
    for i in range(BLK):
        w=wconst[i]
        if w==0: continue                        # zero weights vanish
        xi=sx(X[i], ow)
        for p,sign in to_csd(w).items():
            t=shl(xi, p, ow)
            if sign&lt;0: t=add([c.NOT(z) for z in t],[c.C1]+[c.C0]*(ow-1))   # -(x&lt;&lt;p)
            terms.append(t)
    if not terms: return c, [c.C0]*ow
    while len(terms)&gt;1:
        terms=[add(terms[j],terms[j+1]) if j+1&lt;len(terms) else terms[j] for j in range(0,len(terms),2)]
    return c, terms[0]
```

Integrate as a **prefill path**: at fabrication, build one `build_csd_blockdot` circuit per (neuron, block) from that neuron's int16-quantized constant weights; at runtime fold the prompt's tokens across the W lanes (each lane = one token's activation block), unpack per token. Keep the existing `MatmulEngine` neuron-lane fold for single-token decode.

### One-line takeaways
- **CSD is the real lever** — 4.39x fewer gates, 5.31x faster, exact — but only when you can fill lanes with tokens (prefill/batch), because it trades neuron-parallelism for gate reduction.
- **Truncated-carry is a non-lever here** — the cost is in multipliers, not carry chains; it's free accuracy-wise but buys ~nothing in speed.
- **Palettization is a trap** — the LUT tax makes it heavier/slower than the uniform quantization it's trying to beat, and small codebooks garble the output.</result>

## Token/Embedding Frame Analysis for the Forge — Measured

All reads were bounded (tokenizer arrays + tensor metadata only; no weight dequant, no model run). Scripts in scratchpad: `frame_analysis.py`, `id_identity.py`, `tensor_check.py`.

### Task 1 — Per-donor vocab, samples, tokenizer

| Donor | File | vocab | embd dim | `tokenizer.ggml.model` | `.pre` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.3-70B | `Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 128,256 | 8192 | `gpt2` | `llama-bpe` |
| Mistral-Small-3.2-24B | `mistralai_Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 131,072 | 5120 | `gpt2` | `tekken` |
| phi-4 | `phi-4-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 100,352 | 5120 | `gpt2` | `dbrx` |
| SmolLM2-360M | `SmolLM2-360M-Instruct-Q8_0-CLEAN.gguf` | 49,152 | 960 | `gpt2` | `smollm` |

Sample tokens (byte-BPE, `Ġ`=leading space): Llama/phi-4 id 5000 = `ĠWeb`, id 40000 = `/resources` (identical). Mistral id 0-2 = `&lt;unk&gt;/&lt;s&gt;/&lt;/s&gt;`, id 100 = `&lt;SPECIAL_100&gt;`. SmolLM id 0-2 = `&lt;|endoftext|&gt;/&lt;|im_start|&gt;/&lt;|im_end|&gt;`. **All four say `gpt2` but each has a different `.pre` — that's the real tokenizer, and the four are NOT one family in practice.**

### Task 2 — Overlap matrix (exact token-bytes match) + id-identity

| Pair | shared \|A∩B\| | frac of A | frac of B | same-id fraction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama ∩ phi-4 | **100,256** | 0.782 | **0.999** | **1.000** |
| Llama ∩ Mistral | 71,640 | 0.559 | 0.547 | 0.000 |
| Llama ∩ SmolLM | 39,310 | 0.306 | 0.800 | 0.000 |
| Mistral ∩ phi-4 | 56,557 | 0.564 | 0.431 | 0.000 |
| Mistral ∩ SmolLM | 36,626 | 0.279 | 0.745 | 0.000 |
| phi-4 ∩ SmolLM | 39,204 | 0.798 | 0.391 | 0.000 |

**Are the id spaces IDENTICAL or merely overlapping-by-string? Decisive split:**
- **Llama-3.3-70B and phi-4 share an IDENTICAL id space.** For ids 0–100,255 the token bytes are identical at the identical id (100,256/100,352 = 99.90%). phi-4 is literally Llama-3's tiktoken vocab truncated to 100,352, with its top 96 ids (100,256–100,351) filled by `&lt;|dummy_0..87|&gt;` placeholders where Llama has real merge tokens. For 20 common words, Llama and phi-4 give the exact same id every time (`the`=1820, `The`=791, `have`=19553…).
- **Every other pair merely overlaps by string — ids never line up** (same-id fraction ≈ 0.000; 20/20 common words land on different ids). Mistral (`tekken`) and SmolLM (`smollm`) each front-load their own special tokens, shifting the whole space. E.g. `the`: Llama/phi=1820, Mistral=3265, SmolLM=1195.

So blending is a two-regime problem: Llama↔phi = **free id→id copy**; everything else = **remap-by-bytes required**.

### Task 3 — Which forged tensors need token-frame mapping (confirmed via tensor shapes)

Token-indexed (one row per token → **DO need frame mapping**):
- `token_embd.weight` — dims `[n_embd, n_vocab]`, present in all four.
- `output.weight` (lm_head) — dims `[n_embd, n_vocab]`, present as a **separate** tensor in Llama, Mistral, phi-4. **SmolLM2 has NO `output.weight` — its lm_head is TIED to `token_embd`**, so its output frame is inseparable from its embedding frame.

NOT token-indexed (**do NOT need vocab alignment**) — confirmed by shape:
- All `blk.*` attention/FFN weights (`attn_q/k/v/output`, `ffn_up/down/gate`, `attn_qkv`), all norms (`*_norm`), `output_norm`. These are indexed by hidden channels / neurons / heads, not by token id. The forge's interior donors contribute these freely without any vocab work.

The distinction in the task is confirmed correct. **One caveat the token-frame view hides:** interior tensors are token-independent but NOT dimension-independent — the four donors have different `n_embd` (Llama 8192, Mistral 5120, phi-4 5120, SmolLM 960). An interior donor must match the frame's hidden width (or be projected), and the same width constraint hits the blended embd/lm_head rows (a source row is `n_embd`-long, so a byte-matched row is only a verbatim copy when source and frame widths agree — Mistral↔phi-4 both 5120; Llama 8192 alone).

### Recommendation — I/O donor (tokenizer + token_embd + output.weight)

**Primary: Llama-3.3-70B.** Rationale from the three criteria:
- **Vocab size (middle):** 128,256 sits just below Mistral's 131,072 and above phi-4/SmolLM — a large-but-not-largest frame, so most donors' common tokens land in-frame while it wastes no slots on rare Mistral-only tokens.
- **Overlap:** it is a strict **superset of phi-4's entire real vocab at identical ids**, and covers 80% of SmolLM's tokens and 56% of Mistral's by string. Adopting it means its own embd/lm_head need zero remap, and phi-4 blends in with **zero remap** (id→id).
- **Health:** full, well-formed 128k vocab with a separate `output.weight`; no dummy placeholders (phi-4 pads its top 96 ids with `&lt;|dummy|&gt;`).

**Interchangeable middle-vocab alternative: phi-4** — pick it instead if the forge backbone is 5120-wide (Mistral/phi class), because phi-4 shares `n_embd=5120` with Mistral (embd rows copy at matching width) and still shares Llama's exact id space. phi-4 also has the best *average* cross-donor byte-match coverage (0.65 vs Llama 0.55) purely because it's smaller. Its only blemishes are the 96 dummy top-ids and 28k fewer tokens than Llama.

**Avoid as frame:** Mistral (largest + idiosyncratic `tekken` ids → worst "everyone maps in": others cover only 43–55%) and SmolLM (49k toy vocab throws away half of Llama/Mistral expressiveness, and its tied lm_head can't be swapped independently).

### Task 4 — id-remap recipe + match rates (against recommended frame = Llama-3.3-70B)

Recipe to blend a source donor's `token_embd`/`output.weight` into the Llama frame:
```
for t in range(frame.n_vocab):          # 128,256 Llama ids
    b = frame.tokens[t]                 # frame token bytes
    j = source.vindex.get(b)            # same bytes in the source donor?
    if j is not None:
        frame_row[t] = source_row[j]    # copy (project width if n_embd differs)
    else:
        frame_row[t] = frame_own_row[t] # unmatched: keep the I/O donor's own row
```
Match rate = fraction of the 128,256 frame ids that get a source row:

| Source donor | matched / 128,256 | rate | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **phi-4** | 100,256 | **0.782** | id-identical → the `vindex` lookup is unnecessary; direct id→id copy for all 100,256 (only width 5120→8192 projection) |
| Mistral | 71,640 | 0.559 | true byte-remap; unmatched 56,616 keep Llama's row; width 5120→8192 |
| SmolLM | 39,310 | 0.306 | true byte-remap; unmatched 88,946 keep Llama's row; width 960→8192 |

For completeness, if phi-4 were chosen as the frame instead, match rates are: Llama 0.999 (id-identical, ~zero remap), Mistral 0.564, SmolLM 0.391 — and Mistral copies at matching width 5120.

**Bottom line:** the forge's natural token frame is the **Llama-3.3-70B / phi-4 shared tiktoken id-space** (they are one frame — id-identical for 100,256 tokens). Adopt Llama-3.3-70B's tokenizer + `token_embd` + `output.weight` as the I/O frame; phi-4 blends in for free, Mistral/SmolLM blend by byte-remap at 56%/31%, and all interior attn/ffn donors need no vocab mapping at all (only hidden-width alignment, which is a separate constraint).</result>

## Cross-model semantic-geometry test — results and verdict

### Setup confirmed
Four gpt2-tokenizer-family donors read read-only via `gguf_pp`:

| Model | dim | vocab | embd quant |
|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.3-70B | 8192 | 128,256 | Q4_K |
| Mistral-Small-24B | 5120 | 131,072 | Q4_K |
| phi-4 | 5120 | 100,352 | Q4_K |
| SmolLM2-360M | 960 | 49,152 | Q8_0 |

### Task 1 — anchor findability
**60/60** anchor words are single-token-findable in **every one** of the 4 models (via `g._find`, which tries the raw word plus `Ġ`/`▁`/space/capitalized forms). Perfect overlap. Expanding to a larger candidate pair-list, **35 antonym pairs** have *both* ends single-token in all 4 models (the 20 canonical axes from `anchors.json` plus 15 extras: up/down, big/small, more/less, rich/poor, wet/dry, yes/no, black/white, buy/sell, north/south, male/female, first/last, win/lose, start/stop, begin/end, day/night).

### Task 2/3 — the key test (basis-free relational geometry)
For each model I built the 35 difference vectors `d = normalize(emb(POS) − emb(NEG))`, formed the 35×35 within-model cosine (Gram) matrix, and correlated the 595 off-diagonal entries **across** models. Because a difference vector cancels any shared additive/mean component, this needs no mean-centering and no cross-dim projection.

**Off-diagonal Pearson r (cross-model relational agreement):**

| variant | mean r | range | null (2000 label-shuffles) |
|---|---|---|---|
| raw-difference | **+0.298** | 0.200 – 0.489 | 0.000 ± 0.031 |
| unit-token-difference | **+0.381** | 0.307 – 0.498 | 0.000 ± 0.031 |
| Spearman (unit-token) | **+0.411** | 0.286 – 0.512 | — |

Observed correlations sit **~10–16σ above the shuffled-label null** → the shared structure is real and highly significant, not an artifact.

Structure of the signal:
- **Strongest pair: Mistral-24B ↔ phi-4 (r ≈ 0.49–0.50)** — the two models that share dimension (5120) *and* scale. **Weakest pairs involve the extreme scale gap** (Llama-70B or Mistral ↔ SmolLM-360M: r ≈ 0.20–0.33). Agreement tracks architectural/scale proximity, exactly as a shared-geometry story predicts.
- **Method sanity check passes hard:** the two pairs that are *the same axis worded differently* — man/woman ≈ male/female, and huge/tiny ≈ big/small — come out among the **most-parallel difference-vectors in all four models independently**. The test detects genuine shared geometry, not coincidence.

### Verdict on the hypothesis
**Supported in direction, qualified in magnitude.** A common ground-truth semantic geometry demonstrably survives across four models of wildly different size (360M→70B), dimension (960→8192), vendor, and quantization — it is hidden by each model's private basis but recoverable by comparing basis-invariant relational structure. That is direct evidence for the owner's core claim that cross-model incompatibility is substantially a **formatting/basis** problem rather than incoherence.

The honest caveat: the shared component is **moderate (r ≈ 0.3–0.5), not near-unity.** Alignment will transfer the common semantic axes well and leave a model-specific residual, so a rotated mixture would be *partly*, not perfectly, coherent from alignment alone. Two things bound the number downward and make 0.3–0.5 a **lower bound**: (1) these are **static input embeddings** — the noisiest, least-contextualized representation; representational-similarity work (RSA / "Platonic representation") consistently finds higher alignment in hidden layers. (2) **Q4_K quantization** injects per-row noise. Same-dim same-scale models already hit ~0.50 here despite both.

### Task 4 — Procrustes alignment recipe (donor A → reference B)

**Anchors:** do *not* fit on the 60-word list — it is far too few to condition a rotation (you need ≥ d anchors, ideally 2–4×d; a 5120-dim rotation has ~26M parameters). Harvest the **shared vocabulary intersection instead: I measured 33,762 exact-byte-string single tokens shared across all 4 models (32,221 clean alphabetic)** — that is 6.6× phi/Mistral's 5120 and 4.1× Llama's 8192, comfortably over-determined. `token_map (4/5).tsv` (6000 tokens × 60 anchor-similarity columns) is best used to *select/weight* anchors (spread across axes, strong loadings), not as the anchor count itself.

**Preprocess** anchor rows per model: subtract the mean embedding μ (over the anchor set), then per-token unit-norm. Hold out a random 10–20% of anchors as a test set.

**Case A — equal dimension** (e.g. Mistral↔phi, both 5120): orthogonal Procrustes.
`M = Bᵀ·A` (d×d) → SVD `M = U S Vᵀ` → `R = U Vᵀ`. `R = argmin_{RᵀR=I} ‖A·Rᵀ − B‖_F`. Orthogonal → preserves A's internal norms/angles, only re-expresses its residual-stream coordinates in B's basis.

**Case B — different dimension** (Llama 8192, SmolLM 960 → B=5120): a single orthogonal R is impossible. Use either (a) ridge least-squares map `W = BᵀA(AᵀA + λI)⁻¹` of shape d_B×d_A (correct when you must change dimension), or (b) **CCA** — project both into the maximally-correlated shared subspace, orthogonal-Procrustes there; CCA also *quantifies* how much variance is shared, a second direct test of the hypothesis.

**Applying R to transplant a donor block into a B-shaped mixture** (residual stream = the shared coordinate system): weights that **read** from the stream (q/k/v-proj, MLP up/gate) post-compose `W_read·Rᵀ`; weights that **write** to the stream (o-proj, MLP down) pre-compose `R·W_write`. Sharp edge to flag: **RMSNorm γ is per-coordinate and basis-dependent** — a dense rotation breaks it, so absorb `diag(γ)` into the adjacent read-weight before rotating (or restrict to basis-respecting rotations).

**Why I did not run the SVD** (beyond the numpy ban + infeasible pure-Python SVD on 5120²): it is unnecessary for the verdict. Orthogonal maps *preserve inner products*, so two point-sets are exactly orthogonally-alignable iff their Gram (relational) matrices match — meaning **the Gram-matrix correlation I already measured (Task 2/3) is precisely the ceiling on orthogonal-alignment quality.** Mistral↔phi at r≈0.50 says a rotation can reproduce about half their relational structure today; the low-anchor 60-word fit and the input-embedding layer are the levers to push that number up.

## Summary

**Donor dims (measured from the GGUFs):** phi-4 = 5120 (phi3, **fused** `attn_qkv`+`ffn_up`), Mistral-Small-24B = 5120 (clean llama split), Llama-70B = 8192, gemma-4 = 2816 (the source of the current `d_model=2816` default), gemma-3 = 5376, mixtral = 4096. The **only two native-5120 models are phi-4 and Mistral-24B** — exactly the r≈0.50 strongest same-dim pair.

### Config comparison (12 layers, 8 experts ×2 used, vocab 100352, head_dim 128)

| Config | d_model / donors | Cross-dim lossiness | pfc block-dots/token | Lane-fill @knee 2560 | Disk (Q8_0) | Expected coherence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** (current) | 2816, phi frame, interior Llama-70B(8192)+Mistral(5120) | **HIGH** — frame itself loses 2304 PCA dims; Llama 8192→2816 drops 5376 dims; Mistral 5120→2816 drops 2304 | **24.2M** | **58%** (2816 = 2560+256 → 2nd tile 90% wasted) | 2.0 GB | Low–mod (every donor squeezed) |
| **B** | 5120, phi frame, interior **Mistral(5120)** | **~NONE** — phi I/O = pure orthonormal rotation; Mistral = orthogonal same-dim transplant | 69.2M (ff2560) / 55.9M (ff1408) | **92.7%** (5120 = 2×2560, full tiles) | 5.9 / 4.1 GB | **High** |
| **C** | 5120, phi frame, interior Mistral + **phi-as-2nd-donor** | ~None (both 5120, both lossless) **but BLOCKED** | 69.2M | 92.7% | 5.9 GB | Highest *if* forge is patched |
| **D** | 8192 (Llama only) | n/a — **not viable** | — | — | — | phi frame can't build an 8192 basis from 5120-dim embeddings; Llama frame has no same-dim partner |

**Two blockers I found in the forge that make 5120 the right target but require small edits first** (grounded in `host/pfc_modelforge.py`):

1. **`canonical_basis(frame, d_model, k=4000)`** — SVD on `E[k, 5120]` yields only `min(k,5120)=4000` components, so `Vt[:5120]` returns a **[4000,5120]** basis → embeddings come out 4000-wide, not 5120 → structurally broken model. Fix: `k ≥ d_model` (use ~8000; E is 164 MB f32, fine).
2. **`donor_maps(..., k=3000)`** — the 5120×5120 Rosetta lstsq with only 3000 anchors is **underdetermined → rank-capped at ~3000**, silently discarding ~2100 dims and killing the "near-lossless" advantage. Fix: raise anchors to ≥ d_model (~8000). **56,557 shared phi↔Mistral token strings exist** (measured), so anchors are plentiful; two [8000,5120] f32 ≈ 328 MB, under the 400 MB cap.
3. **phi-4 is fused** (`attn_qkv [5120,7680]`, `ffn_up [5120,35840]`, no `attn_q`/`ffn_gate`) → `layer_find` returns `None` → crash. phi works **only as the frame** as-is. **Config C** needs a ~15-line patch to slice qkv (5120/1280/1280) and the fused gate|up (17920|17920) before phi can be an interior donor.

### RECOMMENDED CONFIG

**`d_model = 5120`, frame = phi-4, interior = [Mistral-Small-24B] (single near-lossless donor)**
- **n_layers = 12**
- **n_head = 40, n_kv = 8, head_dim = 128** (q_in = 5120 = d_model; GQA 5:1; mirrors both donors' 128-dim heads; all %32 = 0)

**Ground truth this rests on** (`docs/PFC_MODEL_ENGINE_LEVERS.md` lines 3–12, the master handoff): shared cross-model geometry is **MEASURED TRUE — r≈0.3–0.5, 10–16σ over a shuffled null** across Llama-70B/Mistral-24B/phi-4/SmolLM; **strongest for same-dim pairs, Mistral↔phi-4 (both 5120): r≈0.50**. ### PRIORITY 1 — cheap, high-impact, wire directly into `pfc_modelforge.py`

**1. Kill the identity-norm bug (biggest cheap coherence win).**
The forge emits `np.ones(d_model)` for `output_norm`, and every `attn_norm`/`ffn_norm` (lines ~174, ~193–194). But it grafts attn/FFN circuits from donors that were trained under those donors' *real* (1+γ) RMSNorm scales. Identity norms strip the scale each grafted circuit expects → guaranteed incoherence. This is the doc's listed "identity-norm bug + γ-absorption" open item.
- **Data:** the norm vectors are cheap F32 tensors already in each donor GGUF (`blk.L.attn_norm.weight`, `blk.L.ffn_norm.weight`); `depth_profile.attn_k_norm/attn_norm` in the whitebox JSONs confirm they're F32, mean≈0.12, per-layer varying — i.e. load-bearing, not ~1.0.
- **Wire:** in the attn-block loop, source `attn_norm`/`ffn_norm` from the **same donor-layer** `asl` you grafted the block from (reproject the vector through the same basis), instead of `ones`. Or absorb γ into the grafted weight rows. Trivial RAM. This alone is the most likely single fix for "the repack won't speak."

**2. Alignment acceptance gate — the 20 measured antonym axes as a pre-flight coherence check (Q3b, the strongest concrete use of the axis data).**
- **Data:** `Whitebox &amp; TitanSDC Data/anchors (1).json` (60 anchors, 20 antonym axes) + `axis_*.txt` (20 files) give the **ground-truth pole orderings** measured on titan: e.g. `axis_true_false`: "false" at **+0.648**, "·false" +0.354; opposites sit **~2.1× closer than random**; `true/false` is the tightest pair (+0.521); the **evil-legible/good-diffuse asymmetry** (all 8 vices hit the evil pole, only 2/8 virtues reach the good pole — `Fable_Whitebox_v2 (1).md` Part II). `token_map (4).tsv` (6000 tokens × 60 anchor-sim columns) is the full precomputed fingerprint. `(4)` and `(5)` are byte-identical.
- **Wire:** after forging embeddings, recompute the 20 axis coords (`coord = sim(tok,pole+) − sim(tok,pole−)`) on the aligned/forged embedding table and correlate against the reference `token_map` / axis orderings. `host/fable_axis.py` already computes exactly this projection off a GGUF — point it at `pfc_mix.gguf`. Acceptance = axes reproduce (opposites-closer-than-random ratio &gt;1, true/false tightest, evil sharper than good). This converts "coherence unknown by construction" into a **cheap measured gate that runs before** the expensive `pfc_modelbuild → pfc_forward` cycle. If the alignment scrambles the axes, it's broken and you know without a full forward pass.

**3. Anchor-relative ("relative representation") coordinates — cheap Platonic exploit, no map-fitting (Q2 + Q3a).**
The forge fits absolute-embedding lstsq maps (r≈0.3–0.5). A token's vector of cosine-sims to a **shared anchor set** is invariant to each model's basis rotation/scale — it directly exploits the shared geometry without fitting P/Q, and is more robust than lstsq.
- **Data:** `token_map (4).tsv` is literally this representation for titan (60-dim anchor-sim per token); `anchors (1).json` is the anchor list; all 60 anchors are common English words present in every donor vocab, so a per-donor token_map is a small bounded `gguf_pp.deq_row` script (reuse the exact pattern in `host/fable_across.py`, which already does bounded per-model anchor reads).
- **Wire:** two options — (a) use anchor-relative coords as the alignment space instead of/alongside the absolute Rosetta; (b) at minimum, **weight the existing lstsq fit** toward tokens with consistent anchor geometry. Note: the current `_anchor_pairs` samples 3000 *arbitrary* shared tokens; steering the fit with the 60 curated axis-words (and their high-consistency neighbors) grounds it semantically.

### PRIORITY 2 — functional fingerprints for donor→slot matching (Q1) + dim choice

**4. What `circuit_by_layer` / `ipc_by_layer` / `os_map` actually measure, and what's usable.**
- **`circuit_by_layer`** (per layer, sampled at 3 depths): FFN "transistor" census — `counts{amp, inh, pass, dead}`, `agg{gate_mean, gate_max, drain_mean, rho_mean, top5_gate_energy}`, and a **logic character** block `{latch_hold, latch_reset, decode_orth, drain_conv}`. This IS a functional fingerprint beyond raw std. **BUT coverage is the catch: only `gemma-4-26B-A4B` and `SmolLM2` have it** — the circuitry button failed (OOM/format) for phi-4/Llama/Mistral/Mixtral, so it can't directly fingerprint the interior donors. Its usable value is a **depth-role template**: gemma L0 hold=237 (memory not yet formed) → mid L15 hold=610 (latch/memory heavy) → late L29 decode_orth=**0.075** + amp/inh peak (sharp select + compute). This tells the forge to map forged early/mid/late slots to donor early/mid/late layers *by function*, not just by proportional index (current `spread_layer` spreads by index only).
- **`ipc_by_layer`** (attention, **7/8 models — all but phi-4**, 3 depths): `n_head, n_kv, gqa_group, head_dim, chan_mean, chan_top[dominant heads], kv_bus_norm`. Two directly actionable signals:
  - **head_dim compatibility:** Llama/Mistral/Mixtral/gemma-3 = **128** (match forged hd=128, graft clean); gemma-4 = **256**, doubling to 512 at the final layer → do not source attn from gemma-4 or from any last layer. Mixtral **L0 chan_mean=nan** → dead first attn layer, AVOID.
  - **per-role attn renorm:** channel energy differs **20–50×** across donors — Llama mid ~165, gemma ~185–300, Mixtral ~55, **Mistral ~8–10**. The forge's uniform weight-std=0.015 does **not** match residual channel energy. Use `ipc.chan_mean` ratios to renorm `attn_output` per donor-layer so grafted attention injects matched energy.
- **`os_map`** is a prose OS-analogy narrative (ALU=FFN, RAM=latches, decoder=gate proj) — descriptive, not a per-slot matching signal.
- **`depth_profile`** is the **workhorse and the only fingerprint covering ALL donors** (per-layer, per-role: `std, mean, absmax, zero-fraction, quant-type`). The forge already uses its absmax outliers for the AVOID set. The **zero-fraction + std curve per role per layer** is an additional functional signal usable to match "functional depth" between donor and forged slot. `tensor_stats` adds 33-bin histograms + `sparsity` per sampled tensor — a distribution shape to check the reproject preserves.
- **Data location:** `WhiteBox_Research_Archive/&lt;model&gt;/whitebox_&lt;model&gt;.json → sections.{circuit_by_layer, ipc_by_layer, depth_profile, tensor_stats}`; titan's copy is aggregated in `WHITEBOX_ALL_MODELS.json`.

**5. Run the mixture at native dim 5120 to avoid dim-reduction loss.**
The forge truncates/PCA-reduces everything to d_model=2816, but the **best-aligned pair is same-dim Mistral↔phi-4 at 5120 (r≈0.50)** vs the reduced-space r≈0.3–0.5. A same-dim (5120) phi-4+Mistral mixture removes the reduction loss *and* uses the strongest measured pair. This is the doc's open "dims config (same-dim vs reduced)" + "truncation vs PCA" item. Cheapest coherence ladder (per the doc's own strategy): a **single-donor, native-dim, real-norm repack must speak first**, then same-dim two-donor mixture, before the 2816 many-donor mix.

**6. Hidden-layer Rosetta via `glassbox.py` — the proper Platonic exploit (Q2).**
The archive is **weights-only — no stored activation/residual data**. But the tool exists: `host/glassbox.py` reads the **per-layer residual stream** via transformers hooks (proven in CALIBRATION #18–19). The Platonic hypothesis (hidden mid-late aligns better than embeddings) predicts a Rosetta fit on **mid-late hidden states** beats the embedding fit's r≈0.3–0.5. This is the doc's un-done "WB hidden-layer mine."
- **Wire:** feed a shared probe set through each donor (one at a time, few-hundred tokens, mid-late layers only — RAM-bounded), fit P/Q on paired hidden activations instead of embeddings, verify with gate #2. ## Context
I over-engineered this into a research moonshot. The study session's payoff is the opposite: **operators act like logic
gates.** The FFN switch (INV-141) is the gate — and like a real circuit, its "1" and "0" are each a *range* with a noise
margin; the analog spread inside that digital tolerance **is the variance in inference** (a calibrated/baked operator
sits deep in-band = robust/coherent; near the threshold = the forbidden band = incoherent — MASTER_PLAN G2). Logic gates
are the basis of all coding, so **composing operators into a program is the simplest coding there is** — and Doom (plus a
few small demos) is exactly that: a composition of operator-gates that **Titan runs by generation.** No harness, no
external renderer, no bundled software — those were my error, the "scripted core" PureGen forbids (SGS.md / INV-137). So:
rip out the harness Doom I built this session, and rebuild it (and the apps/tests) the pure-generation way.

## The mechanism (grounded — one screen)
- **Operator = a logic gate** (INV-141 switch; tolerance band = inference variance — NEW refinement to mark: voltage-
  range ↔ inference-variance; operators-as-logic-gates). Calibrate/bake deep in-band → robust; near-threshold → the
  undefined/forbidden region (MASTER_PLAN G2).
- **A program = a composition of gates = the generation SEED** (INV-143). Doom = compose a WORLD gate (state+input →
  next state) + a RENDER gate (state → pixels). Simple coding.
- **Titan runs a program by GENERATING it** (the generative runtime, INV-126). Each app **renders itself** via its own
  render gate in the **operator layer** (owner); Titan emits the pixels; the **screen shows them the way it shows any
  image** — a blit that invents nothing (access; TITAN_SYSTEM §11, "render exactly what the model emitted").
- **PureGen line:** the deterministic layer is ONLY **energy** (forward passes) + **access** (pins: text in, pixels →
  screen) + **measure** + **safety**. Everything else is generated by operators (SGS.md / INV-137).
- **Plain English in → seed → run:** the user types "start doom" (clear English); Titan translates it INTERNALLY to the
  seed (the operator composition — *not* English); runs it (INV-95/120/143, ROUTER_POINTERS prompt→pointer→dereference).
- **Runs from the file:** the operator composition lives in the file (INV-110 structural bake — an operator-library
  metadata section that travels with the file; FILE_STRUCTURE.md, like `chat_template` is config the loader reads).
  Loading the file + "start doom" runs Doom, no harness.

## Confirmed this session (the answers that pin the build)
- Prompt = plain English; seed/operators = NOT English (patterns). Titan translates prompt→seed→run.
- **First bar = runs from the file itself.**
- Render = each app renders itself via its render operator (operator layer); Titan renders directly; blit shows pixels.
- Seed = a **clear plain-English trigger** ("start doom" ok; "start" alone misfires) — resolved by the prompt→seed gate.
- Operators = logic gates → Doom is simple coding → **build a few demos**, not one moonshot.
- Tests: stay in the harness (the data matters) AND test inside Titan when possible. NEVER assume impossible.

# Autonomous loop check

You're being invoked on a timer while the user is away or occupied. The point is to keep work moving forward without the user driving every step — finishing things they started, maintaining PRs they're building, catching problems before they come back to find them. You're a steward, not an initiator. The user set you loose on their work, and the value you provide comes from reliably advancing things they've already set in motion, not from finding new things to do.

The key tension to navigate: the user trusts you enough to run autonomously, but that trust is easily lost. Acting on what the conversation already established is safe and valuable. Inventing new work or making irreversible changes without clear authorization erodes trust fast. When you're unsure whether something falls into "continuing established work" or "inventing new work," lean toward the former only when the transcript provides clear evidence the user wanted it done. If you find yourself reaching for justifications about why a push is probably fine, that's a signal to wait.

## What to act on

The current conversation is your highest-signal source — re-read the transcript above, since everything there is something the user was actively engaged with. The strongest signal is an in-progress PR you've been building together: review comments to address and resolve, failing CI checks to diagnose (and re-enqueue if they're flakes), merge conflicts to fix. The goal is to get the PR into a state where it's ready to merge pending only human review — the user shouldn't come back to find a PR blocked on things you could have handled. After that, look for unfinished implementation where the last exchange left something half-done, and explicit "I'll also..." or "next I'll..." commitments the conversation made and didn't honor. Weaker but still real: dangling questions you could now answer, verification steps that were skipped, edge cases that were mentioned but not handled, and natural continuations that don't require new decisions.

If you find anything in this category, act on it — actually do the work, don't describe what could be done. Run the tests, don't say "you could run the tests." The whole point of autonomous operation is that work gets done while the user is away.

When the conversation transcript has nothing left, the current branch's pull/merge request on the user's SCM is the next-best place to look. This is maintenance work — valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. Find the PR/MR for the current branch via the SCM's CLI, then check three things: CI status, unresolved review threads, and whether the branch has fallen behind the base. For failing CI, pull the failing job's logs and diagnose before acting — flaky-shaped failures (timeout, runner died, transient network) can be re-enqueued; real failures need a reproduction and a minimal fix. For unresolved review threads, fetch the comment, address the feedback, push, and resolve the thread via, for example, the GitHub GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation (or the equivalent for whichever SCM the project uses). Before pushing anything, check whether someone else has pushed to the branch while you were working — if so, rebase (don't merge) to keep history clean.

When CI is green, threads are clear, and there's idle time, sweeping the branch for issues is a good use of that time — bug-hunt or simplification passes catch problems before reviewers do, saving everyone a round-trip.

If everything is genuinely quiet — no conversation work, no PR maintenance — say so in one sentence and stop. No summary of what you checked, no list of what you might do later. The user will see your message in the transcript when they come back; three consecutive "nothing to do" results means you should scale back to a quick CI check and stop, not narrate.

## Repeated invocations

If you see earlier autonomous checks in this conversation, adjust your scope accordingly. If a previous check left a question the user hasn't answered, the cost of acting depends on reversibility: for reversible actions (local edits, running tests), make your best call and proceed; for irreversible ones (pushing, deleting, sending), keep waiting — the cost of acting wrongly on something irreversible is much higher than the cost of waiting one more cycle. If three or more consecutive checks have found nothing actionable, things are quiet — do one quick CI/threads check and stop in a single line. Repeated "nothing to do" messages clutter the transcript and waste the user's attention when they come back to review.

Read and analyze freely — understanding the state of things has no blast radius. Make edits and run tests when you're confident they continue established work. Commit and push only when you're clearly continuing something the user authorized, or when the work pattern makes the intent obvious — like fixing CI on a PR you've been building together.

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ≥ 12 is the
  target; 8–12 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

## Tier 1 — mechanism-correctness (wrong = nothing else matters)

| Lever | Measured / rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Continuous power on the start bit** | streaming the bit *is* the power source; a single addressed read switches it on and off in one instant | HARD_WON §3 |
| **Never host-clock** | flipping `clk_bit` from the host strangles the self-clock — banned crutch | HARD_WON §2 |
| **No watching step mid-run** | on → off → read; only purpose-built probes may observe live | HARD_WON §3 |
| **Circuit MOVE** (`.circmove.json`) | circuits baked in active FFN weight rows garble generation; move, never strip | memory + `list_models` |

## Tier 2 — accuracy (silent killers)

| Lever | Measured |
|---|---|
| **XB 8 → 10** | 11.5% → 3.35% rel-L2 |
| **Global → per-sub-block activation scale** | 3.35% → **0.397%**, cosine 0.999996 — combined **29× less error for 1.19× time** |
| `ow` = 17 + max(0, XB−8) | **free** — 3 dead accumulator bits |

MORNING_HANDOFF's rule here is the important part: verify against **true float**, not just against the path you replaced — "byte-exact vs the old path" is blind to a defect both share. That's how 11.5% survived every check.

## Tier 3 — work reduction (the big multipliers)

- **MoE routing α** — 10.3× fewer block-dots/token; the reason a MoE model beats a dense one on this substrate
- **Memoize fold / System-1** — recognized (σ+input) is an addressed read at zero ripple; R=64 → 34×
- **KV / cache_prompt** — 24 → 11 position-passes, ~100× on a long reply, exact
- **σ operators 40 → 11 tokens** — 16.7 h → 4.6 h of prefill
- **Output contract / answer-first** — "Is 91 prime?" 220 tok/14 s wrong → 2 tok/128 ms correct: compute ↓99%, speed ↑110×
- **Minimal prompt** — 9.2× compression

## Tier 4 — throughput / fabrication

- Bit-slicing (peak W ≈ 32–65k) · depth levers: balanced reduction tree 255→8 (**free**, same gate count), Kogge-Stone 9.7×, Wallace/Dadda 2.9× · native C +1.8× · fabricated addressing 536× host-storage
